abstract.text: In conclusion, clinicians should avoid using US as the primary imaging modality among nongravid overweight patients, especially those who do not have isolated RLQ pain, when acute appendicitis is suspected.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract.label: CONTEXT
abstract.text: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions.

abstract.label: STUDY SELECTION
abstract.text: RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible.

abstract.label: DATA EXTRACTION
abstract.text: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Revisiting the Risk of Bacteremia in Well-Appearing Infants With Fever Without a Source ≥40 °C: A Multicenter Study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Fever without a source (FWS) in infants is a frequent reason for emergency consultation. Historically, very high fever (≥40 °C) has been associated with an increased risk of bacteremia, prompting extensive diagnostic testing and empiric antibiotic therapy. However, recent epidemiological changes, including expanded vaccination and post-pandemic shifts in pathogen circulation, may have modified this risk. We aim to address this in our study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study in 2 tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2018 to 2025). Well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months presenting with FWS ≥40 °C were included. The primary outcome was bacteremia. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 184 infants were included (median age 14.3 mo). Blood cultures were obtained in 168 (91.3%). Only one case of bacteremia (0.5%; 95% CI: 0.1-3.0) was identified, secondary to urinary tract infection (UTI), with no cases of occult bacteremia. UTI prevalence was 19.6%, and pneumonia 2.7%. Overall, 42.3% received antibiotics, and 16.3% were hospitalized, with all patients showing favorable outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months with FWS ≥40 °C, bacteremia appears uncommon, although the wide confidence interval precludes firm conclusions. These exploratory findings suggest that a more selective diagnostic approach may warrant consideration over routine blood cultures and empiric antibiotics, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Traumatic Diaphragmatic Crural Hematoma in Crush Trauma: Diagnostic Challenges and Management in a Rare Case.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of case reports

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries are uncommon in thoracoabdominal trauma, and traumatic diaphragmatic crural hematoma (TDCH) is even rarer in this context. Because of its retroperitoneal position, TDCH can be difficult to detect early. Although TDCH is usually not life-threatening and does not often require emergency surgery, it is important to note that it often coexists with other serious injuries. This report describes the case of TDCH and shock following crush trauma. After stabilization, whole-body contrast-enhanced CT identified TDCH and unstable pelvic fractures. She then underwent diagnostic angiography followed by surgical management of the pelvic injuries. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old woman with no prior health issues was brought to the emergency department after being accidentally crushed between 2 vehicles while her husband was reversing his car. She experienced pain in her chest, abdomen, and right hip. Initially in shock, she stabilized following initial resuscitation and blood transfusion. Initial evaluation, including extended FAST ultrasound (E-FAST), was negative. Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed fractures of the right sacrum, iliac wing, acetabulum, and pubic rami, along with a hematoma in the bilateral diaphragmatic crura (T12-L1) with contrast extravasation. Diagnostic angiography showed no active contrast extravasation from the diaphragm or pelvis. She subsequently underwent surgical fixation of pelvic fractures. Her postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged in stable condition. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights that TDCH is rare and may indicate a high-energy injury requiring prompt diagnosis. Whole-body contrast-enhanced CT is reasonable in patients presenting with shock and negative E-FAST findings. Management should be guided by bleeding status, and diagnostic angiography may be considered when active bleeding is suspected.

articles.title: How Discrimination Shapes Care-Seeking for Black Caregivers of Children With Medical Complexity.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Black children with medical complexity (CMC) experience a disproportionately high number of hospitalizations and emergency department (ED) visits. This disparity may reflect systemic and interpersonal racism and discrimination. Understanding Black caregivers' experiences is essential to designing programs that reduce acute care use. This study described caregivers' experiences of racism and discrimination and explored how these experiences influence care-seeking and communication among Black caregivers of CMC.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In partnership with family advocacy organizations, we recruited Black caregivers of CMC via national advocacy groups, social media, and electronic health record messaging. Eligible caregivers had a child aged 0 to 21 years with a hospitalization or ED visit in the previous year and a score of 3 or more on the Children with Special Health Care Needs screener. Purposive sampling ensured that one-third of participants were from rural areas. Semistructured interviews, guided by Critical Race Theory, were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-one caregivers completed interviews. Caregivers described discrimination in health care based on race and other characteristics. Five themes emerged in caregivers' experiences of racism: dismissal, stereotyping, fear of retaliation, dehumanization, and differential access to resources. These experiences contributed to distrust, caregiver burnout, and perceived negative health outcomes. Caregivers' responses to discrimination included withholding concerns, advocating, documenting, selecting specific clinicians, managing perceptions, and staying informed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Perceived racism and discrimination shaped how Black caregivers of CMC communicated with clinicians and navigated health care, underscoring the need for health care systems and clinicians to foster trusting partnerships, address structural inequities, and provide equitable, family-centered care.

articles.title: Social Media Asthma Education to Reduce Pediatric Health Care Use: A Bayesian Randomized Control Trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Traditional pediatric asthma education is often fragmented and time limited. Social media may provide a more sustained platform for education. We hypothesized that social media-based education (SME) about asthma would reduce health care use the year after asthma hospitalization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a 2-center Bayesian randomized trial, caregivers of patients aged 3 to 17 years hospitalized for asthma were randomly assigned to social media plus usual care or usual care alone, stratified by age (3-11 vs 12-17 years) and center. The SME group received at least weekly educational post via Facebook and Instagram. The primary outcome was total number of treatment days in a medical setting within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included treatment days across different settings, time to emergency department (ED) revisit or hospital readmission, missed school days, and patient satisfaction. Analyses were conducted using Bayesian generalized linear models with a neutral prior.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Two hundred participants were enrolled. Compared with usual care, SME had a 93% probability of reduced total treatment days (relative risk [RR] 0.80; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.59-1.07) and a 96% probability of decreased unplanned treatment days (RR 0.67; 95% CrI, 0.43-1.05). Mean time to ED revisit was 186 days in controls vs 225 days in the SME arm, with a 92% probability of reduction. Social media participants had longer time to readmission (293 vs 218 days; 81% probability of reduction) and greater satisfaction with education (73% vs 36%) than controls.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: SME was well accepted and likely reduced health care use and delayed posthospitalization ED visits and readmissions compared with usual care.

articles.title: Safety and Clinical Impact of Emergency Department Closed Reduction for Gartland Type III Supracondylar Humerus Fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric type 3 supracondylar humerus fractures (SCHFs) are typically immobilized in situ before definitive operative fixation because of concern for neurovascular injury during closed reduction. This study assesses the safety and clinical outcomes of emergency department (ED) closed reduction versus in situ splinting for type 3 SCHFs before definitive fixation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review was conducted of all pediatric extension-type 3 SCHFs that underwent closed reduction versus no reduction by orthopaedic surgery residents in the ED at a single Level 1 trauma center over a 5-year period. Data included pre- and postreduction neurovascular examinations, multiple radiographic parameters, durations of time between injury, consult, and reduction to the operating room (OR), total operative time, and OR fluoroscopy duration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 112 patients, 54 underwent closed reduction (CR) while 58 were not reduced (NR). Nine (20%) patients in the CR group and 9 (18%) patients in the NR group had abnormal neurological exams on presentation. Four (8%) patients in the CR group and 2 (4%) patients in the NR group had abnormal vascular exams. All 4 patients who underwent closed reduction had improved vascular exams from Doppler-able to palpable radial pulses (P=0.12). No vascular injuries occurred with closed reduction. Importantly, 6 patients in the NR group with initial normal exams developed abnormal neurological deficits while awaiting surgical fixation (P=0.03). The CR group demonstrated significantly improved radiographic parameters postreduction, including AP and lateral displacement, anterior humeral line displacement, lateral Baumann angle, and hourglass angle. The time from consult or reduction to OR was significantly less for the NR group compared with the CR group (9.83 vs. 13.45 h; P<0.01). The time from injury to the OR was also significantly less in the NR group (21.0 vs. 17.0 h; P=0.02). The CR group trended towards shorter operative times (33 vs. 40 min; P=0.15).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Closed reduction of pediatric type 3 SCHFs in the ED by orthopaedic surgery residents is safe and can improve both neurovascular deficits and radiographic fracture alignment. As most pediatric extremity fractures undergo closed reduction in the ED, type 3 SCHFs should not be considered an exception.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III-retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: An Inferior Sinus Venosus Defect With Anomalous Right Middle and Lower Pulmonary Veins.

abstract.text: Sinus venosus defects are uncommon interatrial communications located outside the oval fossa. We describe a case of a seven-year-old girl with a history of fainting episodes, brought to the emergency department after several witnessed vacant episodes at school. Neurological examination was normal, but cardiovascular examination detected an ejection systolic murmur at the upper left sternal edge (pulmonary area). She was observed for 48 hours in hospital with ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring, which showed sinus rhythm with no arrhythmia. She was seen in the cardiology clinic six months later, where she reported to be well and asymptomatic. Initial transthoracic echocardiography showed right atrial and ventricular dilatation with a left-to-right shunt, which initially looked suspicious to be at or near atrial level, later confirmed on further transthoracic echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography to be a large inferior sinus venosus defect (approximately 11 mm in diameter on echocardiography and 16 x 8 mm on computed tomography), with anomalous connection of the right lower and right middle pulmonary veins to the right atrium through a common channel overriding the atrial septum, with associated marked right heart volume loading with preserved biventricular function. She is planned for surgical repair. This case shows how an unrelated presentation led to the diagnosis of a rare congenital anomaly and highlights the difficulty of identifying inferior sinus venosus defects on transthoracic echocardiography, and the less commonly described involvement of the right middle pulmonary vein, with an isolated anomalous connection of the right lower pulmonary vein being the usual finding.

articles.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Ambulance Transport for Suspected Bacterial Pneumonia and In-Hospital Mortality: A Population-Based ORION Study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate changes in difficult ambulance transport, in-hospital mortality, and ambulance transport rates for suspected bacterial pneumonia before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic in Osaka, Japan.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study used the population-based Osaka Emergency Information Research Intelligent Operation Network (ORION) registry (2018-2023). Patients with pneumonia (ICD-10 codes J13-J18) were identified independently using emergency medical technician diagnoses for transport analyses and physician diagnoses for mortality analyses. Periods were pre-pandemic (2018-2019), pandemic (2020-2022), and recovery (2023). Difficult transport was defined as four or more hospital selections and at least 30 min on scene. Annual ambulance transport rates and population-based in-hospital mortality were calculated per 100,000 residents.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 78,720 patients with suspected pneumonia identified by emergency medical technicians, difficult transport increased from 2.7% before the pandemic to 10.3% during the pandemic and 9.3% in recovery. Among 65,510 patients with physician-diagnosed pneumonia, in-hospital mortality was 7.8%, 10.7%, and 9.1%, respectively. Difficult transport was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.14; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.25). Population-based in-hospital mortality showed no corresponding increase. Annual ambulance transport rates decreased from 166.3 per 100,000 residents in 2018 to 117.3 in 2021, returning to 167.0 in 2023.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: During the pandemic, difficult transport and in-hospital mortality increased while ambulance transport rates for suspected pneumonia decreased. Changes in patient selection and case mix may partly explain the mortality trend.

articles.title: Competences of Paramedics in Prehospital Emergency Care: An Umbrella Review.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: The aim of this umbrella review is to describe and define the competences required of paramedics in out-of-hospital emergency medical care.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: The review was conducted in accordance with the methodological guidelines of the Joanna Briggs Institute.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: Keywords were defined according to the PCC-based inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were retrieved from the Medic, PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL and ProQuest databases. Publications in Finnish and English were included. The search was conducted in 2024.

abstract.label: REVIEW METHODS
abstract.text: Five reviewers independently screened the eligibility of reviews based on titles and abstracts (n = 2224) and full texts (n = 105). In the final stage, 20 studies were selected and critically appraised. Methodological quality was assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklist. Data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Confidence in the synthesised findings was assessed using the GRADE-CERQual approach.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight reviews were included in the final synthesis. The competences required in out-of-hospital emergency medical care were categorised into five main domains: interpersonal and teamwork competence; cognitive and decision-making competence; professionalism and ethical competence; clinical competence; and competence across paramedic certification levels and in special or high-stress situations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This umbrella review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the competences required of paramedics in out-of-hospital emergency medical care, both currently and in the future. Furthermore, future research should examine which educational and assessment approaches most effectively support the ongoing maintenance and development of competence within a changing operational context and an expanding scope of practice.

articles.title: Cardiac Tamponade Masquerading as Lactic Acidosis.

abstract.text: An 85-year-old male presented with acute dyspnea and syncope, with pertinent initial vital signs including hypertension, normal heart rate, tachypnea, and hypoxemia requiring oxygen supplementation. The Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) team was consulted for treatment of acute hypoxic respiratory failure, severe hyperglycemia, and lactic acidosis; on MICU evaluation, bedside point of care ultrasonography (POCUS) revealed a large, circumferential pericardial effusion. Despite ongoing intravenous fluid resuscitation, the patient rapidly developed cardiac tamponade with pulsus paradoxus and hypotension. Given the severe hyperglycemia and likely resultant osmotic diuresis, his atypical presentation may have represented low-pressure cardiac tamponade phenotype. He was emergently taken for pericardiocentesis and drain placement with immediate resolution of clinical tamponade; the etiology of his pericardial effusion was deemed idiopathic, although a hemorrhagic effusion from anticoagulation use cannot be ruled out. Ultimately, this case highlights POCUS as an essential clinical tool that should be utilized upon initial assessment of ICU level of care patients to avoid missing indolent but fatal conditions, such as developing or manifest cardiac tamponade. Once cardiac tamponade is identified, careful intravenous fluid resuscitation may be appropriate under the correct circumstances, although definitive treatment involves emergent pericardiocentesis.

articles.title: Deterministic Noncontact Release and Transfer Through Programmable Interfacial Stress Reconfiguration.

abstract.text: Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro-LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact-mediated detachment, which concentrates stress at the perimeter and causes slip and misalignment. Here, we report a diving beetle-inspired electroactive switchable adhesive (DESA) that achieves deterministic transfer through vibration-driven noncontact release enabled by interfacial stress reconfiguration. A perforated electrode couples a bioinspired adhesive layer to an electroactive PVC gel actuator, defining electrically contracting electrode-contact regions and mechanically linked gel-continuous hole regions. Under actuation, differential displacement between these regions deforms the adhesive layer and promotes partial peel-off at distributed interior sites rather than along a single perimeter front. At the 269 Hz resonance, vibration amplifies the displacement mismatch and spreads peel-off across the contact area, progressively reducing the load-bearing area. The resulting inertial stress completes noncontact separation, suppressing misalignment. The adhesive layer provides > 20 kPa dry and > 42 kPa wet adhesion across diverse substrates and retains stable performance over 1000 attachment-detachment cycles. On a robotic platform, the device transfers microcomponents with a lateral placement error of 318 ± 155 µm (≈99.5% placement accuracy). This interfacial stress reconfiguration offers a route to deterministic placement beyond adhesion-strength control.

articles.title: Can Pediatric Emergency Medicine Clinicians Identify Solid Organ Injuries Using Contrast-Enhanced FAST in Abdominal Trauma?

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Contrast-enhanced FAST (cFAST) has demonstrated superior sensitivity to B-mode FAST for detecting solid organ injury in blunt abdominal trauma, yet no prior study has evaluated cFAST image interpretation by pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) clinicians. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of cFAST interpretation for solid organ injuries by PEM clinicians following a web-based didactic.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, single-center study (February-May 2026), PEM clinicians credentialed in B-mode FAST without prior cFAST training completed a web-based didactic. Participants interpreted 12 simulated cases (25 cine clips), evaluating 41 organs (15 injured, 26 non-injured), all reviewed by a cFAST expert or cFAST-trained pediatric radiologist with CT confirmation. Pooled organ-level sensitivity and specificity were calculated with clustering correction using robust standard errors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 41 participants, 1681 organ-level decisions were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 87.97% (95% CI: 84.96%-91.09%), specificity was 89.12% (95% CI: 86.53%-91.78%), negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.77% (95% CI: 90.99%-94.59%), and positive predictive value was 82.34% (95% CI: 78.68%-86.17%). False-negative decisions occurred in 4.4% (n = 74/1681).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: After a web-based curriculum, PEM clinicians achieved high sensitivity, specificity, and NPV with few missed injuries, supporting future investigation of cFAST as an adjunctive screening tool in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma risk-stratification assessments.

articles.title: The unexpected orange hue in a patient with spondyloarthritis receiving biologic therapy.
Dental Coverage, Fluoridation, and Emergency Department Use: Implications of Recent Policy Changes.
articles.journal_full: Inquiry : a journal of medical care organization, provision and financing

abstract.text: Emergency departments in the United States are increasingly being used as a last resort for dental problems that could often be prevented or treated in routine dental care settings. Non-traumatic dental conditions, including dental caries, abscesses, pulpal and periapical disease, and periodontal disease, lead to millions of ED visits and billions of dollars in treatment costs. These visits rarely provide definitive dental treatment, and the burden is higher among Medicaid, Medicare, and uninsured patients. This policy insights discusses how three recent policy developments may worsen this problem: Medicaid cuts under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, state-level rollbacks of community water fluoridation, and the CMS rule excluding routine adult dental services from Marketplace Essential Health Benefits. Although these policies are different, they share a common pathway of weakening access to prevention and routine dental care. We argue that reducing preventable dental ED visits will require protecting Medicaid adult dental benefits, restoring flexibility to include adult dental benefits in Marketplace plans, preserving fluoridation, and building stronger ED-to-dental referral systems.

articles.title: Risk factors of in-hospital mortality in adult emergency department patients with atraumatic acute abdominal pain: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute abdominal pain (AAP) accounts for 7-10% of adult emergency department (ED) visits and represents a heterogeneous presentation. While diagnostic pathways have improved, early prognostic assessment remains limited. Identifying routinely available parameters associated with in-hospital mortality may provide prognostic information at initial triage. Therefore, we aimed to identify such parameters in adult AAP patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients assigned to the "abdominal pain in adults" Manchester Triage System flowchart at the University Hospital Bonn ED (2023-2025). Candidate predictors comprised all structured parameters available at initial triage. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Group differences were assessed using Fisher's exact and Mann-Whitney U tests. We fitted a multivariable logistic regression model to assess associations between candidate predictors and in-hospital mortality. P-values were Bonferroni-adjusted. A focused literature search contextualized mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 6,370 encounters, 94 (1.5%) ended in death during the ED encounter or subsequent hospitalization. In-hospital mortality (1.5%) was within previously published ranges (0.4-8.0%). Patients who died were older and had lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure and SpO₂, higher pain NRS scores, and a different distribution of GCS scores at initial triage after adjustment for multiple testing. In multivariable analysis, age (OR 1.067 per year; 95% CI 1.052-1.082), lower diastolic blood pressure (OR 0.953 per mmHg; 95% CI 0.932-0.976), higher heart rate (OR 1.022 per beat/min; 95% CI 1.009-1.036), lower SpO₂ (OR 0.885 per percentage point; 95% CI 0.833-0.940), and higher pain NRS scores (OR 1.283 per point; 95% CI 1.126-1.462) were associated with mortality after adjustment for multiple testing. Among patients who died, vascular or bleeding disorders, bowel ischemia, and malignancy were the leading diagnostic categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adult ED patients presenting with atraumatic AAP, in-hospital mortality was 1.5%, within the previously reported range. Age, lower diastolic blood pressure, higher heart rate, lower SpO₂, and higher pain intensity were independently associated with mortality after adjustment for multiple testing. These routinely available parameters may provide prognostic information at initial triage, but their value for improving risk prediction or clinical decision-making requires further investigation.

articles.title: Non-operative management after declining surgery in frail older adults with localised colorectal cancer: Survival, palliative interventions and healthcare utilisation in a prospective cohort.
articles.journal_full: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Surgery is the standard treatment for localised colorectal cancer, but its benefit-risk balance is heterogeneous in frail older adults. Evidence describing outcomes when frail patients decline surgery and are managed non-operatively remains limited. This study aimed to describe survival, palliative interventions and healthcare utilisation in frail patients with localised colorectal cancer managed non-operatively within a structured geriatric-oncology pathway.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This single-centre prospective cohort study included consecutive adults with non-metastatic colon or rectal cancer and a positive PRISMA-7 frailty screen between 2017 and 2024. Patients underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment, including IF-VIG frailty severity stratification. Outcomes were primarily described among patients who elected non-operative management; a contemporaneous frail surgical cohort was included for contextual comparison.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1028 patients assessed for curative-intent treatment, 115 screened positive for frailty: 74 (64.3%) were managed non-operatively and 41 (35.7%) underwent surgery. Mean follow-up was 24.5 months. In the non-operative cohort, 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) died, with a mean overall survival of 28 months. Compared with the surgical cohort, non-operative management was associated with higher mortality (87.8% vs 65.8%; p = 0.008) and shorter survival (28 vs 50 months; p < 0.001). Palliative interventions were required in 62.2% of non-operative patients. Emergency department attendance and hospital admission rates were 0.81 and 0.65 per patient-year, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In frail older adults with localised colorectal cancer, non-operative management after declining surgery was common and associated with shorter survival, frequent palliative interventions and measurable healthcare utilisation. Frailty severity stratification may support realistic surgical decision-making and goal-concordant treatment selection.

articles.title: Field Amputation by helicopter emergency service personnel: A cross-sectional survey of clinical practice and experience within air ambulance services in England.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Field Amputation (FA) is a rare, but potentially life-saving procedure undertaken by helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) in the UK. Literature pertaining to FA predominantly originates from outside the UK, where the operational, clinical and legal differences make its applicability to the UK uncertain. Consequently, the severe lack of FA reports from the UK mean that FA is poorly documented in this setting. The aim is to establish the current prehospital FA clinical guidance and practice in the UK.

abstract.label: METHOD/DISCUSSION
abstract.text: An electronic, cross-sectional survey was sent to all UK HEMS. The survey sought to improve understanding of clinical practice, including service provision, scope of practice, equipment, training, governance and incidences of FA. Surveys were analysed with descriptive statistics and descriptive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 15 HEMS responded, with 14 included for final analysis after one response was excluded. All respondents were from England. Every HEMS (n = 14, 100%) could provide FA, with 12 (86%) having a Clinical Practice Guideline specific to FA. Four services (29%) had undertaken FA within the last five years, totalling six cases, which were deemed notable given the absence of case reports from the UK in that time. A Gigli saw was the most popular instrument for bone disarticulation (n = 13, 93%). Unlike the USA and Korea, no respondents used hospital response teams to provide FA.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: FA service provision is widely available across England, with cases of FA being undertaken, yet little standardisation nationally. A national or international registry of every FA case could provide further insights into this area of clinical practice.

articles.title: Emergency medical service capacity and prehospital stroke care in Africa: a critical narrative review.

abstract.text: Stroke is a time-critical medical emergency in which rapid recognition, transport, and treatment are essential to preserving neurological function. Yet across much of Africa, the prehospital systems required to support timely stroke care remain fragmented, underdeveloped, or entirely absent. This critical narrative review examines the evidence on emergency medical service (EMS) capacity for acute stroke care in Africa. Available evidence demonstrates major deficiencies across the entire prehospital stroke pathway. Formal EMS systems are absent in many African countries, and where services exist, ambulance coverage is limited, unevenly distributed, and concentrated largely in urban settings. Community awareness of stroke symptoms and emergency response pathways remains critically low, while reliance on self-transport, pharmacies, traditional healers, and informal care pathways contributes to substantial delays in hospital presentation. Across multiple African settings, most patients with stroke arrive at healthcare facilities hours or days after symptom onset, well beyond established therapeutic windows for reperfusion therapy. The review argues that these delays are not isolated failures of individual behavior but manifestations of broader structural deficiencies in emergency care systems, transport infrastructure, health financing, and stroke preparedness. Limited integration of stroke into national EMS planning, inadequate investment in emergency care infrastructure, and the absence of African-specific implementation research have collectively constrained the development of effective prehospital stroke systems across the continent. Improving stroke outcomes in Africa will require coordinated investment in EMS infrastructure, culturally appropriate stroke awareness programs, community health worker training, mobile health-supported emergency coordination, and integrated prehospital-to-hospital stroke pathways. This evidence is drawn from Ghana, Nigeria, and South Africa, the minority of African countries with published, country-level EMS and stroke-pathway data. Findings and recommendations should be interpreted as characterizing this documented subset rather than the continent as a whole.

articles.title: Arthroscopic Stabilization Reduces Recurrence but May Delay Return to Sport After First-Time Traumatic Anterior Shoulder Dislocation in Elite Male Athletes: A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To evaluate arthroscopic stabilization versus nonoperative management for first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation in adult athletes, with a focus on recurrent instability, return-to-play rates, and time to return to play.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Five databases were searched from inception to July 2025. Studies comparing arthroscopic stabilization versus nonoperative management in adult athletes (≥18 years) with first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation were included. The primary outcome was recurrent instability. Secondary outcomes included return-to-play rates and time to return to play. A narrative synthesis was performed given the nonrandomized and heterogeneous nature of included studies. Evidence certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five studies (232 participants: 111 operative, 121 nonoperative) were included. Recurrent instability rates ranged from 3% to 14% in the operative group and 24% to 80% in the nonoperative group. Return-to-play rates were high for both approaches (operative: 93%-100%; nonoperative: 97%-100%). Nonoperative management was associated with earlier return to sport (2.3-5.7 weeks vs 18.7-39.3 weeks for operative management in studies reporting this outcome). All studies involved elite athletes, with female athletes substantially under-represented.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Arthroscopic stabilization was consistently associated with lower rates of recurrent instability than nonoperative management after first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation but required a longer time to return to play. Nonoperative management enabled an earlier return to play but was associated with higher recurrence. The evidence is limited primarily to male military, collegiate, and professional athletes, restricting generalizability to female, recreational, and broader adult athletic populations.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, systematic review of Level II and III studies.

articles.title: When It All Falls On the Physicians: A Qualitative Study of Physician Workforce Changes Post-Dobbs in Four States With Abortion Bans.
articles.journal_full: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We aimed to explore how abortion bans in four highly restrictive states affected physician workforce dynamics among physicians of diverse specialties after the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Medical Integrity Initiative conducted in-depth interviews with physicians in Alabama, Idaho, Oklahoma, and Tennessee, states with strict abortion bans and severe legal penalties for physicians. Participants included specialists in emergency medicine, maternal-fetal medicine, medical genetics, obstetrics, oncology, and reproductive endocrinology and infertility. We used stratified and snowball sampling and conducted interviews via Zoom from July to October 2024. Grounded theory methodology informed the inductive approach to data analysis. We began with open (descriptive) coding and followed it with axial (interpretive) analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-two physicians across all specialties reported new challenges following the Dobbs decision. We identified the following overarching themes: 1) heightened liability concerns, 2) shifting burden of care onto academic hospitals, 3) added advocacy responsibilities, 4) emotional strain and ethical dilemma of leaving the state, and 5) increased challenges regarding workforce size and workload. Challenges that participants described included colleagues' exodus, difficulty recruiting providers and trainees, and labor and delivery unit closures. Many reported that they considered leaving their state. Participants expressed a desire for their institutions to support evidence-based clinical practice.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Physicians experienced changes in workforce composition and responsibilities following the Dobbs decision. Collective action and robust occupational, legal, and mental health support from their institutions and medical societies might enable physicians to safely stay and sustainably advocate in states with abortion bans.

articles.title: Comparison of subarachnoid block using hyperbaric levobupivacaine plus fentanyl versus hyperbaric bupivacaine plus fentanyl in elective lower limb orthopaedic procedures: A randomized controlled study.
articles.journal_full: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Racemic bupivacaine is the reference agent for subarachnoid block, but its cardiotoxic potential has prompted interest in its S-enantiomer, levobupivacaine. We compared intrathecal hyperbaric levobupivacaine plus fentanyl with hyperbaric bupivacaine plus fentanyl in lower limb orthopaedic surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Eighty patients with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I or II, aged 18-60 years, undergoing elective lower limb orthopaedic surgery were randomly allocated to 12.5 mg of 0.5% hyperbaric levobupivacaine with 25 µg fentanyl (Group A) or 12.5 mg of 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine with 25 µg fentanyl (Group B). The primary outcome was duration of analgesia; secondary outcomes were block characteristics, haemodynamic variables, and complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-nine patients were analysed (Group A = 40, Group B = 39). Duration of analgesia was comparable (192.3 ± 40.0 vs. 181.6 ± 40.6 min; mean difference 10.7 min, 95% CI-7.4 to 28.7; p = 0.243). Group A had slower onset of complete motor block and longer time to peak sensory level (p < 0.05), but faster motor recovery (76.4 ± 14.1 vs. 119.0 ± 14.8 min; p < 0.001). Postoperative pain scores and rescue analgesic requirements were lower in Group A, and complications occurred only in Group B (p = 0.005). Haemodynamic profiles were comparable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hyperbaric levobupivacaine with fentanyl has a slower onset, a comparable duration of analgesia, and faster motor recovery than hyperbaric bupivacaine with fentanyl, and is an effective alternative for lower limb orthopaedic surgery.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Learning Profiles in Surgical Services: A VARK and Experiential Learning Theory Analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Surgical services engage multidisciplinary residents from various specialties; however, the educational delivery frequently adopts a "one-size-fits-all" model. This reliance on passive, aural-visual instruction may not adequately address residents' diverse cognitive preferences, leading to a misalignment between instructional design and residents' specific needs.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To identify Visual, Aural, Read/Write, and Kinesthetic (VARK) learning preferences among surgical and nonsurgical residents who rotate through surgery services and examine associations with specialty, gender, and postgraduate year (PGY).

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: This is a single-institution, retrospective, cross-sectional study that assessed VARK learning style profiles in general surgery, emergency medicine (EM), obstetrics and gynecology (OB-GYN), and orthopedics residents through the lens of Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory, using descriptive statistics and Chi-square analyses.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: St. Luke's University Health Network, at the level I and level II academic trauma centers located in Bethlehem and Easton, Pennsylvania.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A total of 123 residents in general surgery, EM, OB-GYN, and orthopedics who rotated through Trauma and Surgical Critical Care from 2023 to 2025.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This study included 78 male and 45 female residents. Multimodal was the most common preference (N = 60; 48.8%), followed by Kinesthetic (N = 40; 32.5%). OB-GYN uniquely favored Aural as a secondary preference, while EM and Orthopedics demonstrated the strongest Kinesthetic profiles. Gender was statistically significantly associated with VARK preferences (p = 0.037). Females predominantly preferred Multimodal (28; 62.2%) compared to males (28; 41%). In contrast, males showed higher Kinesthetic preferences (27; 34.6%) than females (13; 28.9%). Learning profiles remained stable across PGY levels.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings indicate that a uniform instructional approach is suboptimal. Educators should move away from passive observation to active, multimodal engagement, incorporating kinesthetic and specialty-aligned strategies to better support the diverse educational needs of residents in high-acuity surgical services.

articles.title: Respiratory Infections at Mass Gatherings: A Travel-Medicine Review with Hajj and Umrah as a Longitudinal Case Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mass gatherings combine international mobility with dense, repeated contact and can amplify respiratory infections across travel corridors. Hajj, Umrah and Kumbh Mela, offer a uniquely recurrent case study, while other religious or sporting mega-events, and music or cultural festivals provide contrasting exposure systems.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A focused narrative review was conducted of peer-reviewed studies, systematic and scoping reviews, and authoritative public-health guidance. Searches and project evidence synthesis prioritized publications from January 2021 to August 2026, with selected foundational sources. We examined respiratory symptoms, laboratory detections, clinical disease, vaccination, antimicrobial use and resistance, surveillance, environmental modifiers, and pre-, during-, and post-travel practice. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias scoring was undertaken.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Respiratory risk is determined less by attendance alone than by contact intensity, duration, ventilation, vocalization, shared accommodation, traveler susceptibility, and pathogen circulation. Recent Hajj evidence confirms a substantial burden of respiratory symptoms and clinical consultations, but estimates vary because denominators range from volunteers and tested samples to healthcare encounters. Rhinovirus, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and bacterial pneumonia remain important. There is continued abuse of antibiotics for predominantly viral syndromes and acquisition of resistant organisms link individual care to global antimicrobial resistance. Syndromic, laboratory, event-based, genomic, and wastewater surveillance are complementary, not interchangeable. Heat, dust, air quality, fatigue, and differential access to protective infrastructure modify respiratory symptoms, severity, and care seeking. Comparative events share mechanisms but not directly transferable rates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Travel-medicine practice should treat mass gatherings as longitudinal exposure systems spanning preparation, transport, the event, and return. Layered vaccination, risk-based masking, ventilation and crowd-flow measures, prompt diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and explicit travel histories, can reduce respiratory morbidity while preserving denominator discipline and access to protective infrastructure.

articles.title: ED red blood cell transfusion in severe anemia: stay and recurrent use-a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in the emergency department (ED) may occur during prolonged ED stays. We evaluated hospital stay and recurrent ED use among adults with severe anemia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort included ED encounters at a single tertiary academic hospital in Poland from January 2025-June 2026 with first hemoglobin <8.0 g/dL. Exposure was recorded ED RBC administration. Hospitalized encounters underwent propensity-score overlap weighting and patient-clustered bootstrap. Missing endpoints and available vital signs were recovered. Sensitivity analyses included 50 imputed datasets and weighted medians.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 131,711 ED encounters, 1381 met eligibility criteria; 742 involved ED RBC transfusion. The hospitalized cohort included 610 encounters (175 with and 435 without ED RBCs). The adjusted total stay difference among survivors was 10.9 h (95% confidence interval [CI], -42.5 to 65.8); downstream estimates remained imprecise. ED stay was 9.4 h longer (95% CI, 8.0-10.8). Among 341 patients with transfusion followed by direct discharge, recurrent patients generated 52.1% of 541 episodes; 31.7% returned within 30 days.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hospitalized encounters with recorded ED RBC administration had longer ED stays; treatment-related time could not be separated from waiting for inpatient beds. Downstream estimates allowed benefit or harm. Neither causal effects nor equivalence can be inferred. Pathways for stable recurrent anemia warrant evaluation while preserving urgent ED transfusion.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for assessing the inferior vena cava: validity of an instructional video.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: to analyze the content validity evidence of educational videos for assessing the inferior vena cava using point-of-care ultrasound.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: a study of educational technology development and validity. The video was assessed by experts using Educational Technology in Health Appearance Validity Instrument (IVATES) in terms of clarity, practical relevance, and theoretical significance, and the Content Validity Ratio (CVR) was calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: the script was assessed by a focus group. Subsequently, it was recorded and assessed by 12 nurses, resulting in a CVR of 1.0 in relation to the assessed indicators, and a score close to 5 on the IVATES (high agreement).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: the video presented adequate evidence of content validity and can be used to train nurses in performing this assessment.

articles.title: Moral stress, support and professional quality of life among emergency department staff in Stockholm: a mixed-methods survey study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The demanding work environment in emergency departments (EDs) places staff at risk of experiencing moral stress and burnout. This study aimed to describe professional quality of life among ED staff and explore the support received, valued and requested by staff when experiencing moral stress.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All physicians, nurses and assistant nurses employed at two EDs in Stockholm were invited to participate. Of 637 eligible employees, 179 responses (28.1%) were included. Professional quality of life, perceived frequency of moral stress and both used and valued support were analysed descriptively. Free-text responses concerning requested workplace support were analysed using content analysis, and quantitative and qualitative findings were subsequently integrated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants reported moderate levels of burnout (mean 23.6, SD 5.8) and compassion satisfaction (mean 37.9, SD 7.1) and low levels of secondary traumatic stress (mean 21.8, SD 5.5). Almost half (48%) reported experiencing morally stressful situations every shift or several times per shift. Informal support from colleagues was both the most commonly received and most highly valued type of support. Free-text responses highlighted requests for greater managerial involvement, structured reflection, education and formal support. Integration of the quantitative and qualitative findings indicated a gap between the support participants valued and the structured support available in the workplace.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Moral stress was frequently reported among participating ED staff, alongside moderate self-reported levels of burnout and compassion satisfaction. Informal collegial support was central, while participants also requested greater access to structured workplace support. Formal support structures may complement collegial support alongside organisational efforts to address workplace conditions contributing to moral stress.

articles.title: The epidemiology and burden of injury in The Gambia: A prospective trauma registry study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic injury is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet robust prospective data characterizing injury epidemiology remain limited across sub-Saharan Africa. This study describes the demographic, injury, and initial treatment characteristics of patients enrolled in a hospital-based trauma registry in The Gambia. These data provide a foundation for characterizing the country's injury burden, guiding resource allocation, and informing continued trauma-system development.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective descriptive study was conducted using data from a hospital-based trauma registry established at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital, The Gambia's principal tertiary referral center for trauma and orthopaedic care. Injured patients presenting to the Trauma Emergency Unit from June 2022 through September 2025 were enrolled. Data included demographics, injury mechanism and setting, intent, anatomic injury location, injury type, and Trauma Emergency Unit disposition. Descriptive statistics were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 3380 enrolled patients, 76.1% were male, with a median age of 25 years. Most injuries occurred in villages (41.1%). Transport-related injuries were the leading mechanism (47.1%), followed by falls (29.3%) and violence/assault (21.4%). Streets/highways were the most common place of injury (43.3%), and nearly all injuries were unintentional (96.1%). The lower extremity below the knee (29.6%), head (22.3%), and hand (21.7%) were the most frequently injured body regions. Soft tissue injuries predominated (57.0%), followed by closed fractures (24.3%) and open fractures (11.7%). Overall, 55.9% of patients were discharged home, 29.3% were dispositioned to the operating theatre, and 10.1% left without being seen or before completing treatment. Among patients with recorded Trauma Emergency Unit disposition, 2.6% (n = 84) were categorized as 'mortuary or died.'

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: To our knowledge, this represents the largest prospective trauma registry analysis of injury epidemiology in The Gambia. Trauma disproportionately affected young males and was driven primarily by transport-related injuries, with a substantial burden occurring in rural settings. The frequency of fractures and incomplete treatment encounters highlights priorities for road-safety interventions, strengthened prehospital and referral systems, and expanded trauma, orthopaedic, and diagnostic capacity. Continued prospective trauma surveillance can support resource allocation, quality improvement, and national trauma-system development.

articles.title: Is it necessary to distally lock all pertrochanteric cephalo-medullary fixation in the geriatric population?
Integrating Social Determinants of Health Into Emergency Medicine Clerkships: A Qualitative Study of Student Reflections.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Social determinants of health (SDH) significantly influence emergency department (ED) care and patient outcomes, yet experiential learning opportunities in SDH remain inconsistently integrated into clinical education. Prior work has been effective but resource intensive. We sought to explore an adapted SDH-focused clinical experience that built on prior curricula and pre-clerkship SDH instruction while minimizing additional non-clinical resources.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We implemented a semi-structured SDH-focused experience within a required emergency medicine (EM) clerkship which sought to integrate prior knowledge from a pre-clerkship SDH curriculum. In the ED, students partnered with care managers or social workers to identify patients affected by SDH, conducted patient interviews, and completed written reflections. De-identified reflections from one academic year (2023-2024) were analyzed using an inductive thematic analysis approach. Two investigators independently coded an initial subset, developed a shared codebook, and applied iterative constant comparison to generate themes with investigator triangulation to enhance trustworthiness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Students described intersecting barriers to care, including language discordance, financial insecurity, and immigration-related challenges. Reflections also linked these barriers to direct clinical consequences such as delays in care, limited follow-up access, and patients leaving against medical advice. Students described how communication barriers and limited interpreter availability impacted care delivery and safety. Reflections also described structural inequities and the role of interdisciplinary teams in mitigating these challenges. Two additional themes, chronic illness and aging and health systems science, were interpreted as cross-cutting factors that modified how SDH were experienced rather than as determinants themselves.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A semi-structured, experiential SDH curriculum embedded within the ED clerkship elicited reflections in which students identified and interpreted real-world barriers to care. These findings describe how students applied SDH concepts in the ED rather than demonstrating change attributable to the activity. This approach offers a feasible model for embedding SDH learning within existing clinical workflows.

articles.title: Wake-Up Call for the Right Ventricle: Rethinking Pulmonary Embolism Diagnostics in Critical Care.
articles.journal_full: Australasian journal of ultrasound in medicine

articles.title: Association of a Fever Clinic Package With Waiting Time Among Walk-in Emergency Department Patients Ineligible for Fever-Clinic Streaming.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Seasonal surges of patients with fever may delay emergency department (ED) care. This study examined whether a multicomponent fever clinic package was associated with waiting time among walk-in ED patients ineligible for fever-clinic streaming.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective before-and-after study compared year-end/new year periods in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026. The primary outcome was time from registration to first physician documentation, used as a proxy for initial physician assessment. Gamma generalized linear models were adjusted for patient characteristics, physician staffing, preceding-hour demand, study day, and arrival time. A calendar-day cluster-robust analysis and an interaction analysis between study period and arrival mode were also performed. Post-assessment throughput was exploratory.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 2056 ED visits, 793 walk-in visits ineligible for fever-clinic streaming had evaluable waiting time. Median waiting time decreased from 54 to 26 min (p < 0.001). The period with the fever clinic package was associated with shorter waiting times (adjusted mean ratio 0.57, 95% confidence interval 0.46-0.70; p < 0.001), and calendar-day cluster-robust inference was consistent with this association. The association differed by arrival mode (p for interaction < 0.001), with model-estimated waiting time decreasing among walk-in visits but not among ambulance arrivals. No consistent adjusted difference was observed in post-assessment throughput.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The period with the fever clinic package was associated with shorter waiting times among walk-in ED patients ineligible for fever-clinic streaming, without a consistent adjusted difference in post-assessment throughput. Residual between-period confounding and inseparable package components preclude causal attribution; studies with contemporaneous comparators are warranted.

articles.title: Clinical Profiles Among Adolescents Referred for Suspected Clinical High Risk for Psychosis: an Exploratory Retrospective Study.

abstract.text: IntroductionThe Clinical High Risk of psychosis (CHRp) concept is widely used to identify adolescents at risk of psychotic disorder. However, current tools lack specificity regarding actual transition, as they struggle to distinguish developmental vulnerabilities from true prodromal psychotic states.MethodsThis retrospective monocentric study included 26 French adolescents aged 11-18 referred between 2021 and 2023 to a specialized CHRp consultation. The multidisciplinary evaluation, involving involving child and adolescent and adult psychiatry professionals, combined the CAARMS, developmental and attachment-based interviews, and final synthesis considering differential diagnoses.ResultsNine adolescents were classified as CHRp, and 5 of them transitioned to psychosis. CHRp adolescents were significantly younger and more often referred through emergency department. An exploratory multidimensional analysis identified two clinical profiles: a psychosis-spectrum profile and a broader psychological and environmental vulnerability profile characterized by attachment-related difficulties, child welfare placement, and self-harm behaviors, without transition to psychosis.ConclusionA diagnostic approach grounded in developmental and environmental specificities may enhance the predictive specificity of CHRp status in adolescents. Differentiating psychotic vulnerability from alternative psychopathological trajectories-particularly attachment-related and intrafamilial relational difficulties-may appear crucial for tailoring early interventions. It may help identify a more homogeneous and genuinely at-risk population.

articles.title: Mitigating Failure Modes in Next-Generation Batteries via High-Entropy Materials: A Cross-System Review.

abstract.text: The demand for advanced energy storage drives the exploration of novel battery materials. High-entropy materials (HEMs), multicomponent alloys, oxides, and related compounds with high configurational entropy, stabilize structures and create synergistic "cocktail" effects that mitigate dendrite growth, volume expansion, and side reactions. This review critically examines how the structural heterogeneity of HEMs influences electrochemical performance across battery components. We first discuss anodes, where HEMs suppress volume change and improve cycling stability, and then cathodes, including disordered rock-salt and layered HEMs for Li-, Na-, and K-ion systems. For electrolytes, we distinguish multi-component liquid formulations from high-entropy solid electrolytes (garnets, argyrodites, NASICONs and halides), which widen electrochemical windows and enable low-temperature operation. In Li-S and metal-air batteries, HEM catalysts benefit from multi-site adsorption and bifunctional activity; we compare them semi-quantitatively with low-entropy Li-S catalysts and distinguish the requirements of Li-O2 and CO2/H2O-containing Li-air operation. A cross-system analysis then maps shared failure modes to entropy-driven strategies across monovalent, multivalent, and catalytic systems. Finally, we discuss the characterization challenges that limit mechanistic understanding and outline future directions, including AI-guided materials design.

articles.title: The global research landscape of emergency medical services in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major cause of death, and emergency medical services (EMS) are central to recognition, resuscitation, transport, and linkage to post-arrest care. Although previous bibliometric studies have mapped the broader cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation literature, the intersection of EMS and OHCA warrants focused characterization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective bibliometric analysis of records indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 1972 through June 2026. The search combined OHCA terms with terms for EMS, paramedics, and emergency medical technicians. Annual output, research categories, journals, authors, and countries were described. VOSviewer version 1.6.20 was used for author co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and cited-reference co-citation analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The search identified 3,005 records. Annual output increased markedly after 2010, peaked at 244 publications in 2021, and remained above 200 publications per year from 2022 to 2025; 130 records were indexed for the partial 2026 year. Emergency Medicine (1,745; 58.1%) and Critical Care Medicine (1,014; 33.7%) were the most frequently assigned Web of Science categories. Resuscitation published 694 records (23.1%). The United States had the greatest country-level output (1,022; 34.0%), followed by Japan (375; 12.5%) and Canada (281; 9.4%). The most prolific author was Shin SD (98 publications). Co-authorship mapping showed registry-centered regional communities, while keyword analysis yielded ten interpreted domains spanning epidemiology, resuscitation interventions, dispatch, registries, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, equity, and technology-related topics. Co-citation analysis identified four major intellectual communities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: EMS-focused OHCA publications indexed in Web of Science show sustained output and international collaboration associated with established registries. Limited visibility of low- and middle-income settings within this database warrants further investigation. Equity, implementation, and digital and resuscitative technologies are potential areas for further research; the pooled network analysis does not establish their temporal growth.

articles.title: Early clinical experience with vericiguat after acute decompensated heart failure in elderly patients with HFrEF: a prospective observational study.

abstract.text: Vericiguat has demonstrated clinical benefit in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), particularly in those at high risk of recurrent heart failure events. However, evidence regarding its early use in elderly patients following hospitalization for acute decompensated HF (ADHF) remains limited. In this prospective single-center case series, 143 consecutive patients aged > 70 years hospitalized for ADHF with HFrEF were enrolled and vericiguat was administrated. Clinical evaluations, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), six-minute walk test (6MWT), Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ), and laboratory parameters were assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks. After 4 weeks of treatment with vericiguat, 44.8% of patients were in NYHA class II and 55.2% in NYHA class III, no patients were in NYHA class IV (p < 0.001); LVEF improved from 34 ± 4.7% to 46.8 ± 7.5% (p < 0.0001); exercise capacity increased significantly (p < 0.001), while a significant decrease in MLHF-Q, NT-proBNP levels and hsCRP was observed (p < 0.001). No symptomatic hypotension, syncope or relevant deterioration in renal function or electrolytes occurred during the observation period. In this single-arm cohort of older patients with HFrEF recently stabilized after ADHF, initiation of vericiguat was feasible and coincided with substantial short-term changes in functional status, LVEF, and circulating biomarkers, without major safety signals during 4 weeks of observation. Given the absence of a control group, these changes cannot be attributed to vericiguat and may reflect, at least in part, recovery from the acute event, decongestion, optimization of background therapy, learning effects, and regression to the mean. These findings should therefore be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in controlled studies.

articles.title: Acute Care Utilization and Cost Outcomes of Home-Based Palliative Care for Persons Living with Dementia in the United States: A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Given the shift toward value-based payment models, which reward high-quality and cost-effective care, an increasing number of palliative care programs are being integrated across care settings in health systems and organizations in the United States to reduce patient use of more costly services such as hospitalization and emergency department (ED) visits. Home-based palliative care (HBPalC) is one community-based palliative care delivery model that may help delay facility and nursing home placement and reduce hospital use and costs.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This review synthesized evidence on hospital utilization and cost outcomes associated with HBPalC among people living with dementia (PLWD) in the United States.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: PubMed, Embase, and Cumulated Index in Nursing and Allied Health Literature were searched from inception through October 2025. All U.S.-based studies were included if samples included PLWD and the study examined the impact of HBPalC on hospital utilization (i.e., hospitalization and ED use) or health care costs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of eight studies were included. Overall, HBPalC provided core services such as symptom management and advanced care planning. PLWD-specific HBPalC focused on addressing neurobehavioral symptoms and supporting caregivers. HBPalC was consistently associated with reductions in hospitalization and associated costs, although evidence for changes in ED utilization was not available, with no studies reporting ED outcomes for PLWD specifically.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HBPalC was associated with reduced hospitalization, but its impact on ED use was inconclusive for PLWD. Most studies had heterogeneous patient samples and did not report PLWD-specific outcomes. There is a lack of HBPalC specifically designed for PLWD, and more studies are needed to evaluate HBPalC's impact on ED use among PLWD.

articles.title: Impact of Hands-On Pediatric Emergency Training on Wound Suturing, Airway Management, and Orthopedic Casting Skills: Prospective Pre-Post Interventional Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Opportunities to practice low-frequency skills for high-acuity pediatric emergency procedures in clinical settings are limited. The Basic Emergency Skills Techniques 3N1 (BEST 3N1) workshop was designed as a structured, hands-on training program to support procedural skill development among pediatric emergency care practitioners.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate preworkshop to postworkshop changes in procedural performance and knowledge after a 3-day hands-on pediatric emergency skills workshop.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A quasi-experimental prospective pre-post interventional study was conducted during the 8th BEST 3N1 workshop, held from February 11 to 13, 2025, at the Simulation and Skills Development Centre, Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The workshop included 24 scheduled continuing medical education hours in 3 domains: wound suturing, pediatric airway management, and pediatric orthopedic emergencies and casting. Procedural performance was assessed using complete paired preworkshop and postworkshop data for each assessment. Day 1 wound suturing and day 2 airway management were assessed using 4-item checklists scored from 0 to 8. Day 3 orthopedic casting competence was assessed using a keyword-based rubric covering equipment, procedural steps, and postapplication care, with a total score range of 0 to 30. Written knowledge was assessed using a 30-item multiple-choice test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The number of paired observations differed in assessments because the analysis was based on complete matched preworkshop and postworkshop data for each outcome. Day 1 wound suturing checklist mean scores increased from 4.14 (SD 1.72) to 7.72 (SD 0.68) among 88 paired participants, with a mean change of 3.58 (SD 1.71; P<.001) points. Day 2 airway management checklist scores increased from 5.47 (SD 1.88) to 7.81 (SD 0.56) among 77 paired participants, with a mean change of 2.34 (SD 1.96; P<.001) points. Day 3 orthopedic casting total competence scores increased from 4.20 to 6.39 among 77 paired participants, with a mean change of 2.19 (SD 1.72; 95% CI 1.80-2.58; P<.001). Written knowledge scores increased from 19.04 (SD 3.77) to 22.32 (SD 3.23) among 94 paired participants, with a mean change of 3.28 (95% CI 2.16-4.39; P<.001) points.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The BEST 3N1 workshop was associated with improved checklist-based procedural performance, orthopedic casting competence, and written knowledge among pediatric emergency care practitioners. These findings support the use of structured hands-on workshops for high-acuity, low-frequency pediatric emergency skills.

articles.title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices.
authors: Cardiology/CV Surgery Section, Pulmonary Vascular Disease and Cardiovascular Network.

abstract.text: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

articles.title: Ultrasound Teaching in UK Undergraduate Medical Education: A National Survey.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Ultrasound teaching is increasingly incorporated into undergraduate medical education (UGME), yet its implementation within UK medical schools remains poorly described. This study aimed to provide the first comprehensive national overview of ultrasound teaching across UK UGME curricula.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2025 among UK medical schools. Respondents provided data on ultrasound curriculum integration, teaching delivery, faculty involvement, assessment methods and implementation barriers. Descriptive statistics were used to analyse responses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-nine of 43 eligible medical schools responded (91% response rate). Twenty-six schools (67%) currently include formal ultrasound teaching in their curriculum, and seven further schools planned to introduce it in the 2025/26 academic year (85% if implemented). Most (69%) deliver ultrasound teaching across both early/pre-clinical and later/clinical years. Anatomy (81%) and procedural skills (65%) were the most common domains. The median total ultrasound teaching time was 5hours (IQR 3-10; n = 24), with 88% of schools providing ≤10hours. Small-group hands-on sessions were the predominant teaching method (96%), and 69% of schools did not assess ultrasound knowledge/skills. The main implementation barriers were limited curriculum capacity and trained faculty shortage (54% each). Overall, 59% of respondents supported inclusion of ultrasound as a mandatory GMC competency for graduates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ultrasound teaching is gaining momentum within UK UGME. However, considerable variation exists in content, duration and assessment. Addressing faculty shortages, curriculum capacity and the absence of national competency standards will be essential to ensure consistent, high-quality ultrasound education across UK medical schools.

articles.title: Comparing behavioral outputs across automated tracking software reveals platform-dependent variability in zebrafish neurobehavioral analysis.

abstract.text: The zebrafish (Danio rerio) is a prominent vertebrate model in behavioral neuroscience, with the novel tank diving test (NTT) representing one of the most validated paradigms for assessing anxiety-like responses and vertical exploration. Although automated video-tracking software are widely used to quantify behaviors, the results obtained from different programs are rarely equivalent, representing a critical challenge for data comparability. Variations in detection algorithms and coordinate processing may compromise the interpretation of behavioral outcomes and reproducibility across studies. Here, we aimed to systematically assess the agreement, accuracy, and reproducibility of behavioral metrics across different video-tracking platforms, and to determine whether a standardized post-analysis approach could improve cross-system comparability. To achieve our goal, we compared four well-established systems: ANY-maze and EthoVision (closed-source software), and TrackR and ToxTrac (open-source software), using the zebrafish NTT paradigm. To enable comparison across platforms, an independent post-analysis approach was applied using the CartesianBehaviour package, which utilizes spatial coordinates to calculate movement patterns and minimize biases introduced by software-specific data processing. Our results revealed differences in tracking accuracy and intra- and inter-software data variability, demonstrating systematic discrepancies in behavioral parameters such as total distance traveled and time spent in the top area. Despite these differences, the use of a common post-analysis framework showed strong positive correlations across systems. Finally, our findings demonstrate the lack of direct equivalence between behavioral metrics obtained from different tracking platforms and reinforce the importance of standardizing post-analysis to ensure data reproducibility in neurobehavioral research.

articles.title: Apparent temperature, heat waves, and unintentional injury-related emergency medical service calls: A case-crossover study.

abstract.text: Evidence on apparent temperature, heat waves, and unintentional injuries remains limited. We aimed to examine the short-term associations of apparent temperature and heat waves with injury-related emergency medical service (EMS) calls and variation across injury types and population subgroups. We conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study of 170,538 unintentional injury-related EMS calls in Minhang District, Shanghai, from July 2021 to June 2025. Conditional logistic regression with distributed lag models evaluated apparent temperature and nine heat-wave definitions combining temperature percentiles and consecutive-day durations. Cumulative associations were summarized over lag 0-2 days for apparent temperature and lag 0-1 days for heat waves.
