The cumulative exposure-response curve generally increased with apparent temperature, with the estimated minimum at the lower boundary of the observed range. Comparing the 99th percentile (42.5 °C) with this minimum (-2.9 °C), the cumulative odds ratio (OR) was 1.21 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.12-1.31). The apparent-temperature association was largest for traffic injuries (OR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.56-2.07). Among adults aged 18-64 years, the OR was 1.38 (95% CI: 1.24-1.53), with evidence of overall heterogeneity across the three age groups (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q = 0.001). For heat waves defined by daily mean temperature at or above the 95th percentile for ≥ 3 consecutive days, the cumulative OR was 1.07 (95% CI: 1.03-1.11). High apparent temperature was associated with increased odds of unintentional injury-related EMS calls. These findings support the inclusion of injury prevention in heat-health planning, although comparisons across exposure windows and heat-wave definitions remain exploratory.

articles.title: [Patterns of safety incident reporting in a paediatric department: a six-year analysis].

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Patient safety incidents are a global healthcare concern, and paediatric patients are particularly vulnerable. Although voluntary reporting systems cannot estimate the true incidence of these incidents, they help identify reporting patterns and opportunities for improvement. This study aimed to describe reports submitted from a hospital paediatric department and to analyse their association with incident type and severity, the reporter's professional category, and the clinical area.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Observational, descriptive, retrospective study of 659 reports recorded in a centralised reporting system between 2019 and 2024. Year, type and severity of the reported incident, reporter's professional category, and clinical area were analysed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 87.4% of reports involved near misses or no-harm incidents. Medication/vaccines was the most frequently reported category (28.5%), followed by patient care and follow-up (25.8%). Adverse events were mainly concentrated in patient care and follow-up (42.2%) and diagnosis (32.5%). Nursing staff submitted the highest number of reports, whereas reports submitted by physicians included a higher proportion of adverse events (P<.01). The paediatric emergency department accounted for 47.5% of reports, with no significant differences in severity among clinical areas (P=.063).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The reporting system predominantly recorded reports of near misses and no-harm incidents, with differences in reporting patterns according to incident type, professional category, and clinical area. Analysis of these patterns can identify processes requiring further review and help guide feedback strategies tailored to different professional groups and clinical settings.

articles.title: Association of Care Intensity With Survival and Long-Term Cost-Effectiveness in Sepsis Without Initial Organ Support After Emergency Admission: A Multicenter Cohort Study in Japan.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To identify subgroups of patients hospitalized for community-acquired sepsis without initial organ support who may derive survival and cost-effectiveness benefits from ICU or high-dependency care unit (HDU) admission.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: A 140-hospital Japanese database (April 2016-March 2024).

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Adults admitted via emergency ambulance for community-acquired sepsis not requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, mechanical ventilation, catecholamines, or renal replacement therapy before or on the antimicrobial-initiation day.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: None.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: We compared ICU and HDU admissions, each vs. general ward (GW) admission, balancing patient characteristics using overlap propensity-score weighting. In-hospital mortality was estimated as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs using modified Poisson regression. Cost-effectiveness was measured by the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) in 3-year costs per quality-adjusted life year (QALY). Among 28,211 patients (GW, 18,349; HDU, 8,706; ICU, 1,156), ICU and HDU admissions were not associated with lower mortality overall (HDU vs. GW; RR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92-1.06 and ICU vs. GW; RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.92-1.22). However, HDU admission was associated with lower mortality among patients with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score greater than or equal to 6 (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75-0.99) or Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score less than or equal to 12 (RR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92). Under the Japanese (50,000 USD/QALY) and U.S. (100,000 USD/QALY) thresholds, ICU and HDU admissions were not cost-effective overall (ICERs > 200,000 USD/QALY). However, the HDU subgroup with GCS score less than or equal to 12 (ICER, 47,738 USD/QALY; 95% CI, 45,918-49,558) was cost-effective under both thresholds, and that with SOFA score greater than or equal to 6 (ICER, 55,319 USD/QALY; 95% CI, 52,018-58,624) met the U.S. threshold.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ICU or HDU admission was not associated with survival or economic benefits overall, whereas HDU subgroups (SOFA score ≥ 6 or GCS score ≤ 12) were associated with lower mortality and better cost-effectiveness. These findings may help optimize resource allocation.

articles.title: Hallucinated Evidence and Real-World Risk-Physicians' Intent to Act on AI-Generated Abstracts in Emergency Medicine and Trauma Surgery: Cross-Sectional, Vignette-Based Diagnostic Accuracy Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in academic writing and can generate linguistically polished but factually incorrect scientific content. Such misinformation may distort evidence appraisal and, if translated into clinical practice, compromise patient care.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to estimate physicians' likelihood of misperceiving false information embedded in LLM-generated abstracts as true and reporting an intent to use that information in future practice. We also explored which features were associated with perceived credibility and intended clinical action.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey of physicians working in emergency medicine and trauma surgery across 4 hospitals in Germany. Each participant assessed 4 abstracts generated using GPT-5 Thinking mode, of which 2 contained intentionally false claims supported by plausible explanations and 2 contained accurate claims. The primary outcome was the proportion of physicians reporting an intent to use or act on recommendations contained in abstracts with false claims. Secondary outcomes included perceived accuracy, rejection of accurate claims, and ratings of precision, structure, and grammar.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty physicians provided 80 ratings of 4 abstracts. Overall, physicians reported that they would act on 68% (54/80) of abstracts. Using abstract truth status as the reference, the decision to act had a sensitivity of 78% (31/40), specificity of 43% (17/40), positive predictive value of 57% (31/54), and negative predictive value of 65% (17/26). The positive likelihood ratio was 1.35 (95% CI 0.98-1.85), the negative likelihood ratio was 0.53 (95% CI 0.27-1.04), and the diagnostic odds ratio was 2.55 (95% CI 0.96-6.73). True and false abstracts received similar ratings for perceived accuracy (mean 3.15, SD 0.89 vs mean 2.88, SD 1.04; P=.21), precision (mean 3.15, SD 0.89 vs mean 2.93, SD 1.00; P=.29), structure (mean 3.23, SD 0.77 vs mean 3.20, SD 0.88; P=.89), and grammar (mean 3.40, SD 0.59 vs mean 3.43, SD 0.68; P=.86). Abstracts that physicians intended to act on were rated substantially higher for perceived accuracy, precision, and structure than those they would not act on (all P<.001), whereas grammar ratings did not differ (P=.80).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Physicians frequently reported an intent to act on LLM-generated abstracts containing false claims, and true and false abstracts were not reliably distinguished on perceived quality measures. Perceived accuracy, precision, and structure were strongly associated with intended action, whereas grammar was not. These findings highlight the risk that persuasive scientific presentation may increase the credibility and potential clinical influence of fabricated or inaccurate AI-generated evidence.

articles.title: Task Force 11: Additional Cardiac Conditions and Considerations in Competitive Athletes.
articles.journal_full: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstract.text: The recently updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Abnormalities provides a comprehensive framework for guiding clinicians in the evaluation and management of competitive athletes. Divided into 11 Task Forces, it covers a broad range of cardiovascular diseases and clinical scenarios. Task Force 11 was devoted to cardiac conditions and considerations in athletes not included in the other Task Forces. Here, we present the detailed rationale for the clinical considerations covered in this section of the Scientific Statement. These topics include hypertension, commotio cordis, pulmonary embolism, performance-enhancing drugs and supplements, exercise in extreme environments (specifically altitude and scuba diving), and pregnancy.

articles.title: Task Force 9: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Cardiac Channelopathies.
articles.journal_full: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstract.text: Cardiac channelopathies, including long QT syndrome, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, Brugada syndrome, and short QT syndrome, are heterogeneous conditions, which can lead to varying risks in athletes depending on their symptoms, disease severity, genotype, and therapies initiated. Historically, athletes with these conditions were excluded from participation with blanket restrictions, despite an absence of data. More recently, a number of studies have provided more scientific evidence to guide decision making and have been incorporated into these guidelines for athletes with cardiac channelopathies. Many athletes with these conditions may be supported in their decision to return to play as part of a shared decision-making model when they have been assessed, risk stratified, and appropriately treated by a specialist with expertise in these conditions.

articles.title: Task Force 8: Care of Competitive Athletes with Arrhythmias and Sudden Cardiac Arrest: Clinical Considerations and Electrocardiogram Interpretations.
articles.journal_full: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstract.text: This document outlines recommendations for managing competitive athletes with arrhythmias and risks of sudden cardiac arrest, emphasizing individualized risk assessment, shared decision-making, and return-to-play protocols tailored to each athlete's cardiac profile and sport demands. It provides evaluation strategies for ventricular arrhythmias, implantable cardiac defibrillators, atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern/syndrome, and syncope, alongside guidance for electrocardiogram interpretation in athletes. A key focus is placed on differentiating between low-risk and high-risk conditions, with recommendations for treatment strategies and ongoing monitoring to ensure athletes' safety.

articles.title: Task Force 5: Clinical Considerations for Myocarditis and Selected Cardiovascular Conditions, Including Valvular Heart Disease.
articles.journal_full: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstract.text: Athletes with myocarditis, pericarditis, valvular heart disease, and other acquired cardiovascular conditions require careful evaluation when considering competitive sports participation. This document outlines key clinical considerations, risk factors, and expert consensus, serving as the rationale for Section V of the recent AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Abnormalities. Disease-specific risk stratification and shared decision-making are essential in determining return-to-play eligibility. This Task Force document addresses myocarditis, pericarditis, the cardiovascular impact of respiratory viral infections, incidental myocardial fibrosis, Kawasaki disease, infiltrative cardiomyopathies, and valvular heart disease.

articles.title: Effect of airway assistant training on intubation time during simulated prehospital airway management: A pilot study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Challenging airways are common in the out-of-hospital setting, where delays or failure to secure the airway can result in significant morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this pilot study aimed to determine whether training paramedics in the role of airway assistant improves intubation time during a simulated regurgitating airway using suction-assisted laryngoscopy and airway decontamination (SALAD).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Twelve qualified paramedics were randomly allocated to one of two groups (n = 6) and paired with intensive care paramedics (ICPs). Airway assistants in Group 1 completed a one-hour airway assistant training program, whereas airway assistants in Group 2 received no training. Participants completed a standardized, timed simulation using a continuously regurgitating mannequin designed to replicate the challenges of out-of-hospital intubation. The primary outcome was time to successful intubation, defined as passage of the endotracheal tube through the vocal cords with cuff inflation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Airway assistant training significantly reduced intubation time. The untrained group recorded a median intubation time of 102.5 seconds (IQR 36), compared with 53 seconds (IQR 19) in the trained group. Group comparisons demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in intubation time (p = 0.009) and corresponded to a very large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.86; Hedges' g = 1.72). No association was observed between intubation time and the age or experience of either the airway assistant or the ICP. No esophageal intubations occurred in either group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this pilot study, training paramedics to perform the airway assistant role significantly reduced intubation time in a simulated regurgitating airway. These preliminary findings suggest that incorporating structured airway assistant training into prehospital education programs may improve airway management performance in challenging environments. Given the small sample size and simulated setting, larger studies are required to confirm these findings and determine whether the observed benefits translate to clinical practice.

articles.title: External validation of a decision rule for bacteremia vs contaminants in pediatric blood cultures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Half of positive blood cultures in pediatric emergency departments (PEDs) represent contaminants, driving unnecessary hospitalization, antibiotic exposure, and repeat visits. A clinical decision rule derived at CHU Sainte-Justine showed 99% sensitivity and 60% specificity for distinguishing bacteremia from contaminants but had not been externally validated. We sought to validate this rule in an independent pediatric cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective diagnostic study spanned from January 2015 to May 2025 at a tertiary PED in Switzerland, using positive blood cultures from patients younger than 16 years. The four predictors (Gram-negative organisms or Gram-positive cocci in pairs or chains; time to positivity <17 hours; indwelling device; suspected osteoarticular infection) classified each case as low, moderate, or high risk. The primary outcome was bacteremia, adjudicated by two independent reviewers, based on organism identity and infectious disease specialist's assessment. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed with 95% CIs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 130 children included (median age 3.8 years [IQR 0.9-9.9]; 61.5% male), 78 (60.0%) had true bacteremia. The rule yielded a sensitivity of 97.4% (95% CI, 91.0-99.7), specificity of 69.2% (95% CI, 54.9-81.3), positive predictive value of 82.6% (95% CI, 73.3-89.7), and negative predictive value of 94.7% (95% CI, 82.3-99.4). Both false-negatives were immunocompetent children with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia without indwelling devices. Among contaminants, 71% received antibiotics under usual care versus 31% classified as moderate or high risk by the rule.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This first external validation supports the Sainte-Justine rule in a distinct pediatric population, preserving sensitivity with higher specificity. Multicenter validation is warranted before adoption.

articles.title: Successful management of arrow‑rebound‑induced transcervical penetrating trauma with major vascular and pharyngolaryngeal injuries: A case report.

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: Penetrating neck injury involving major vessels is highly lethal. Long-trajectory transcervical penetration caused by rebounding arrows is exceptionally rare in civilians, posing significant diagnostic and management challenges.

abstract.label: PATIENT CONCERNS
abstract.text: A man in his early 50s presented to the emergency department approximately 2 hours after an arrow, rebounding from a nearby training target, penetrated his neck (entering above the left mandible, exiting on the right). He was conscious with minimal external bleeding but copious oropharyngeal secretions. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed the arrow traversing the hyoid bone and oropharynx, abutting the right common carotid artery (CCA) and compressing the right internal jugular vein (IJV).

abstract.label: DIAGNOSES
abstract.text: Open neck injury; combined right CCA and IJV injury; hemorrhagic shock; pharyngolaryngeal trauma without aerodigestive perforation; and pulmonary infection with consolidation.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Initial stabilization included arrow shaft shortening by firefighters. Emergency exploration under general anesthesia involved tracheotomy, cervical exploration, primary repair of the right IJV and CCA, and foreign body removal. Postoperative management in the intensive care unit included damage-control resuscitation (transfusion of 7.0 U packed red blood cells, 1100 mL plasma, and 10.5 U cryoprecipitate), antimicrobial therapy (cefuroxime, guided by cultures showing Staphylococcus epidermidis), early individualized anticoagulation (enoxaparin transitioned to rivaroxaban), and systematic correction of coagulopathy and electrolyte disturbances.

abstract.label: OUTCOMES
abstract.text: The patient was discharged on postoperative day 12 with healed wounds. Follow-up at 1, 3, 6.5 months, 1, 2, and nearly 3 years showed intact neurological function. Imaging confirmed stable right IJV occlusion. Anticoagulation was discontinued at 1 month without subsequent bleeding or thromboembolism. Although long-term imaging was limited to a 6.5-month non-contrast computed tomography, the patient remained asymptomatic without signs of venous hypertension or neurological deficits throughout the follow-up period.

abstract.label: LESSONS
abstract.text: High-quality preoperative computed tomography angiography with 3D reconstruction is critical for defining the relationship between the foreign body and vital structures. In selected patients, early individualized anticoagulation after excluding active bleeding may mitigate venous thrombosis. Systematic intensive care unit management of coagulopathy, electrolytes, and pulmonary complications is pivotal for survival.

articles.title: Informal Digital Information Use in Hospital Mass Casualty Incident Management During Wartime: Multicenter Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Managing mass casualty incidents (MCIs) during an active warfare environment presents unique challenges, including operating under extreme uncertainty. Traditionally, emergency communications rely on strict, hierarchical channels from prehospital services to receiving hospitals. However, informal digital communication streams, particularly instant messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram, are increasingly used within medical workflows. Despite international interest in public social media during disasters, empirical research regarding how hospital leadership echelons use informal messaging tools for real-time operational and clinical decision-making during active warfare remains sparse.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to characterize the adoption of social media and instant messaging platforms as early information sources among hospital-based MCI managers during wartime and to evaluate their specific impact on real-time operational and clinical decision-making.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured questionnaire distributed across all 24 national medical centers authorized to receive MCIs during wartime in Israel. Target respondents encompassed diverse leadership echelons, including emergency department directors, trauma service directors, trauma coordinators, charge nurses, emergency team members, and hospital executive leadership.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 76 medical professionals representing key decision-makers across national receiving centers completed the survey. WhatsApp emerged as the most frequently used platform (median 3.0, IQR 2.00-4.00). Although these informal channels provided rapid initial intelligence, 65.3% (49/75) of respondents encountered false information during emergency events. Consequently, 81.3% (n=61) reported routinely verifying social media data against official channels before executing major actions. Multivariate regression analysis revealed distinct pathways of influence: higher platform use intensity was strongly and independently associated with enhanced situational awareness (P=.002) and greater operational decision-making influence (P=.02). In addition, participants' level of trust and reliance was associated with clinical decisions (P=.01) and real-time team management (P=.03). Furthermore, active platform engagement during live threat conditions was positively correlated with heightened situational awareness during missile launch alerts (P<.001) and missile fall alerts (P<.001). Platform use and trust behaviors remained consistent across years of professional experience, qualifications, and executive roles.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Informal digital platforms, dominated by WhatsApp, serve as vital, rapid early information channels for hospital MCI leadership during wartime emergencies. While use intensity directly enhances situational awareness and operational control during active missile threats, clinical and team management actions remain strictly contingent on trust. Given the high exposure to unverified data, formalizing structured verification protocols and incorporating informal digital communication strategies into hospital disaster preparedness frameworks are essential to optimize real-time decision-making in future large-scale health emergencies.

articles.title: Non-cardiac comorbidities and functional impairment in acute heart failure: a hospital-wide real-world cohort study (COMPACT-HF).

abstract.text: Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults and is associated with non-cardiac comorbidities (NCCs) and functional impairment. Their prognostic and therapeutic implications remain incompletely characterized. COMPACT-HF was a retrospective cohort study of adults discharged after hospitalization for AHF at a tertiary teaching hospital in 2023. Comorbidity burden was assessed using the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and predefined NCCs. Functional impairment was defined as loss of ≥ 1 basic activity of daily living (ADL). Primary outcome was 12-month all-cause mortality. We included 456 patients (mean age 82.6 ± 8.6 years; 50% male); 96% had ≥ 1 NCC and 48% had functional impairment. Twelve-month mortality was 31%. CCI was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.17 per point; 95% CI 1.07-1.27, p < 0.001), while functional impairment provided additional prognostic information beyond comorbidity burden. Advanced chronic kidney disease, dementia, and active malignancy were among the NCCs most strongly associated with mortality. Among patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, dementia, advanced chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease, and functional impairment were associated with lower prescription of ≥ 3 of 4 guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes, whereas CCI was not; GDMT prescription also varied substantially according to discharge ward. In this hospital-wide real-world cohort of patients discharged alive after AHF hospitalization, NCCs and functional impairment were highly prevalent and associated with mortality, while specific clinical conditions and discharge ward were associated with GDMT implementation. Integrating comorbidity and functional assessment may improve risk stratification and support a holistic approach to AHF management.

articles.title: [Communication in the resuscitation room: a core element of crew resource management (CRM) for safe patient care : Current developments, practical examples, and key information for resuscitation room training].

abstract.text: The care of critically ill patients in the resuscitation room is generally provided by a multi-professional and interdisciplinary resuscitation team. Current developments among institutions that set the framework for healthcare underscore that effective communication and targeted team training must be understood not as supplementary measures, but rather as fundamental to successful patient care. For example, the German Association for Emergency Medicine (DGINA) considers qualifications in team leadership and crew resource management (CRM) for medical and nursing team members in the care of critically ill, non-traumatological patients to be indispensable. Secure and effective communication is one of these qualifications and is regarded as a central element of the five non-technical skills. The role of non-technical skills and the CRM training built upon them in preventing errors related to "human factors" has increasingly gained recognition in the medical community in recent years. Despite convincing literature, there are still no legal regulations in Germany at present stipulating the content, structure, or implementation of regular CRM (resuscitation room) training.

articles.title: Comparison of automated and manual oxygen titration in emergency care: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Supplemental oxygen is a cornerstone of emergency care but has a narrow therapeutic window, with both hypoxemia and hyperoxia associated with adverse outcomes. Despite guideline-recommended oxygen saturation targets, manual oxygen titration in acute care settings is frequently inaccurate due to human, system, and workflow limitations. Automated closed-loop oxygen titration systems, which continuously adjust oxygen delivery to maintain predefined saturation targets, have emerged as a potential solution. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of automated oxygen titration compared with standard manual titration in adult emergency care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study protocol was registered with the international prospective register of systematic reviews (PROSPERO). A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies involving adult patients receiving emergency care were identified, with full-text review and data extraction performed in accordance with the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-two records were identified; four met inclusion criteria, including three randomized controlled trials (n = 286) and one prospective observational study. In the meta-analysis, automated titration significantly increased time within oxygen saturation target ranges compared to manual care (mean difference 22.9%; 95% CI 9.6-36.2). While initial heterogeneity was high (I2 = 85.7%), sensitivity analysis excluding one high-performing manual cohort eliminated variance (I2 = 0%) and confirmed a robust treatment effect (mean difference 29.6%; 95% CI 23.7-35.6). The available data are limited to these surrogate physiological endpoints; evidence demonstrating improvements in patient-centered clinical outcomes remains absent.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Automated closed-loop titration demonstrates superior physiological precision in oxygen saturation target maintenance compared to manual care in emergency settings. While it effectively minimizes exposure to hypoxaemia and hyperoxia extremes, further large-scale trials are required to determine if these physiological improvements translate into definitive clinical benefits or improved patient-oriented outcomes.

articles.title: Integrating a Host-Protein Bacterial/Viral Test into the Emergency Department Sepsis Alert Order Set Is Associated with Changes in Sepsis Category Distribution and Patient Management: A Pre/Postimplementation Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of implementing a host-protein bacterial/viral test in the emergency department (ED) sepsis alert order set.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Pre/postimplementation study. Host-protein testing was automatically ordered both pre- and postimplementation as part of the ED sepsis alert order set; test results were accessible to treating clinicians only postimplementation. The pre- (September 2024 to December 2024) to postimplementation (January 2025 to March 2025) transition also involved education on the host-protein test to ED clinicians. The primary outcome was patient classification into Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) sepsis categories (definite/probable vs. possible vs. unlikely sepsis).

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: ED of an academic medical center.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Adults who triggered the ED sepsis alert order set.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Host-protein bacterial/viral test (MeMed BV) automatically ordered in ED sepsis alert order set. Test result was only visible to clinicians postimplementation.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 893 eligible patients; 505 patients in the preimplementation cohort and 388 in the postimplementation cohort. The distribution of SSC sepsis categories differed between pre- and postimplementation cohorts (χ2(2) = 8.73; p = 0.013). The difference was primarily driven by a larger proportion of patients classified as unlikely sepsis (from 32.5% to 41.1%; p = 0.009) and a smaller proportion classified as possible sepsis (from 18.4% to 13.2%; p = 0.043). Among unlikely sepsis patients, host-protein test implementation was associated with ordering fewer cefepime doses (from 3.3 to 2.2; p = 0.044) and a lower hospitalization rate (from 92.1% to 79.9%; p = 0.002).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings support an association between host-protein testing for patients triggering ED sepsis alerts and the distribution of possible vs. unlikely sepsis cases. Multicenter clinical utility studies are warranted.

articles.title: Methodological Considerations in Evaluating Point-of-Care Ultrasound Escape Rooms for Physician Assistant Education.
articles.journal_full: The journal of physician assistant education : the official journal of the Physician Assistant Education Association

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism and transfusion outcomes following intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total hip arthroplasty: A prospective two-center cohort study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used during total hip arthroplasty (THA) to reduce perioperative blood loss and transfusion requirements. Although extensive evidence supports its use, prospective real-world data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) and blood transfusion among patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) at two institutions in Bogotá, Colombia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, observational, descriptive, two-center cohort study included consecutive adults who underwent elective primary THA. Patients received intravenous TXA according to institutional protocols. The primary outcome was the occurrence of symptomatic VTE, including deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, and myocardial infarction during a 10-week follow-up period. The secondary outcomes included blood transfusion requirements, postoperative hemoglobin levels, and emergency department visits.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 151 primary THAs were performed in 133 patients. One case of symptomatic DVT was diagnosed, corresponding to a VTE incidence of 0.75%. Five patients (3.8%) required postoperative blood transfusions, including two complex reconstructive procedures. The mean postoperative hemoglobin level was 11.8 ± 1.9 g/dL. No pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, or myocardial infarction was observed during the follow-up period.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this prospective two-center cohort of patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary THA, including both conventional and complex cases, a low incidence of symptomatic VTE and transfusion was observed. These results provide prospective real-world evidence from a Latin American population and contribute to the regional literature on perioperative blood conservation strategies for primary THA.

articles.title: Clinical Assessments to Inform Return to Play Prognosis Following Acute Hamstring Injury: An Evidence-Informed Guide for Clinicians.

abstract.text: BACKGROUND: Rehabilitation clinicians aim to provide a return to play (RTP) prognosis following acute hamstring injury based on various clinical assessments, including subjective interview questions and physical examinations. CLINICAL QUESTION: What subjective interview questions and physical examinations should be prioritised during an initial clinical assessment following acute hamstring injury to inform RTP? KEY RESULTS: There are key subjective interview questions and physical examination findings to inform RTP prognosis following acute hamstring injury. Prolonged RTP time has been associated with athletes who: 1) recall higher pain ratings at the time of injury; 2) report pain with palpation closer to the ischial tuberosity; 3) have greater cranio-caudal length of palpable pain; 4) present with between-leg deficits of greater magnitude in maximal hip flexion active knee extension range of motion and isometric knee flexion strength in outer-range (supine with 90° hip/knee flexion) and/or mid-range (prone with 0° hip and ~15° knee flexion); and 4) experience pain during outer-range hamstring contraction. CLINICAL APPLICATION: This evidence-informed clinical commentary may help clinicians prioritise subjective interview questions and physical examinations to inform their RTP prognosis following acute hamstring injury.

articles.title: Toward a Definition and Differentiation of Secondary Traumatic Stress, Vicarious Trauma, Post-Traumatic Stress, and Compassion Fatigue in Relation to First Responders: An Integrative Literature Review.

abstract.text: This integrative review focuses on the psychological effects of direct and indirect exposure to trauma among first responders (firefighters, police investigators, police officers, paramedics, ambulance workers). The aim of this study is to provide conceptual clarification of the various terms used: secondary traumatic stress, vicarious trauma, compassion fatigue, and post-traumatic stress disorder. For this study, six databases were consulted: PsycINFO/ARTICLE; PubMed/Medline; Web of Science; Cochrane; Cairn; ScienceDirect, up to January 2026. To be included, articles had to be published in peer-reviewed scientific journals and concern an adult and professional population. Data extraction followed PRISMA guidelines, and 76 studies were included. Two researchers participated in data extraction and ensured the quality of the articles. The main results revealed conceptual porosity maintained by symptomatic overlaps and the limitations of measurement tools, often designed for other professional categories. The analysis also highlights the central role of organizational constraints in the emergence of trauma, the importance of considering the nature of exposure, cumulative burden, personal experience, and professional role in the study of traumatic responses. Finally, this review calls for exposure to trauma among first responders to be viewed as a public health issue.

articles.title: How Specialty Shapes Burnout in the Medical ICU: A Qualitative Study of Resident Experiences.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The negative impacts of burnout in resident physicians have been widely documented, and burnout rates in the Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) are high. While burnout has been studied in physicians and other personnel in Intensive Care Units (ICUs), little attention has been given to resident physicians in the MICU. Our prior study demonstrated very high rates of burnout in residents in the MICU and was suggestive that non-internal medicine (non-IM) residents may be at an even higher risk of burnout than their internal medicine (IM) colleagues.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to determine and compare drivers and mitigators of burnout experienced by IM and non-IM (Family Medicine (FM) and Emergency Medicine (EM)) resident physicians rotating in the MICU. It also sought to identify drivers and mitigators of burnout that may be amenable to intervention strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Three different resident disciplines (IM, EM, and FM) hosted trained investigators who mediated focus groups of 4-12 trainees during protected teaching time between April 2022 and May 2023. The focus groups aimed at identifying contributors to and mitigators of burnout in the MICU. Trained scribes recorded notes from the conversation, which were later parsed into themes and compared across groups to determine if similar themes existed in other resident specialties.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In this study, we identified common themes in the focus groups from residents of all specialties and themes unique to each specialty. Universal drivers of burnout included moral distress and ethical concerns and insufficient orientation. Multiple unique drivers for FM and EM residents were identified including decreased gratification (FM), guilt (FM), communicating uncertainty to families (EM), managing chronic medical diseases (EM), and hierarchical relationships (FM & IM). Universal mitigators across all three specialties include meaningful patient experiences, time and access to food, and positive team dynamics.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Drivers and mitigators of burnout vary across residency training specialties in the MICU, though common themes exist amongst different specialties. Identifying these themes creates opportunities for intervention strategies with the potential to improve resident satisfaction, training quality, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Shortages of agents used to treat poisoning from 2014 to 2024.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Drug shortages are a threat to patient care. Previous research described frequent and prolonged shortages of drugs used to treat poisoned patients. In this study, we characterize more recent trends in toxicology drug shortages.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Shortage data from the University of Utah Drug Information Service from 2014 through 2024 were analyzed. Drugs used in the practice of toxicology (antidotes and key supportive agents) were included. Information regarding drug type, formulation, number of shortages, shortage reason and duration, and single-source and marketing status was collected. The availability of alternative therapies and whether the alternative was affected by shortage during the study period was evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,670 shortages, 223 shortages (13.4%) involved toxicology agents, and 41/223 (18.4%) toxicology shortages remained ongoing at the end of 2024. New shortages peaked at 30 in 2018, and total ongoing shortages consistently exceeded new shortages annually. Median shortage duration was 12.6 months. Shortages predominately impacted parenteral drugs (177/223, 79.4%), and 96.4% (215/223) were generic. Sedative-hypnotics were most frequently impacted. For 186/223 (83.4%) shortages, a therapeutic alternative existed; however, in 93.5% of cases (174/186), the substitute was on shortage. The most common reported reason for shortage was manufacturing problems.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Common themes in drug shortages remained over time; however, the shortage landscape has been complicated by discontinuation of the critical antidotes physostigmine and dimercaprol. Therapeutic alternatives may not be readily available, and medication errors and delayed and less effective therapies can impact patient outcomes and increase healthcare costs. Toxicologists are uniquely poised to study and mitigate shortages, and advocate as stakeholders to address the root causes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In the last decade, toxicology drug shortages have persisted and new shortages have emerged. Clinicians caring for poisoned patients should be aware of ongoing shortage trends and implement mitigation strategies to ensure adequate care.

articles.title: Comment on "Identification of DCS risk factors in recreational diving: multifactorial model based on the DAN DSL Database 2024".
Scoliosis affects preoperative presentation, surgical management, and postoperative outcomes in pediatric Chiari I malformation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ideal management of patients with both Chiari I malformation (CIM) and scoliosis is unclear, and pathophysiology between these diseases is not well understood. We compared presentation, operative strategy, postoperative outcomes, and complications between CIM patients with and without scoliosis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients aged ≤21 years who underwent decompressive surgery for CIM at a single institution between 2013 and 2023 were included. Patients managed without decompression were excluded. Patients were split into two groups: patients with and without scoliosis. Preoperative symptoms, medical history, surgical variables, and postoperative outcomes and complications were compared using univariate analysis and multivariate linear regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 79 patients were included; 23 with and 56 without scoliosis. Preoperatively, patients with scoliosis had fewer headaches (60.9% vs. 83.9%, P=0.04) and reported cognitive impairment (17.4% vs. 42.9%, P=0.04) than patients without scoliosis. Patients with scoliosis were also more likely to have syringomyelia (87.0% vs. 28.6%, P<0.0001). Intraoperatively, cases for patients with scoliosis were less likely to use ultrasound (4.3% vs. 39.3%, P=0.002) and more likely to involve arachnoid dissection (65.2% vs. 23.2%, P=0.0004) compared to cases in patients without scoliosis. Postoperatively, patient reported symptoms did not differ significantly between the two groups. However, emergency department (ED) visits postoperatively were lower for patients with scoliosis (β=-0.13, 95% CI -0.25-0.01, P=0.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: CIM patients with scoliosis reported fewer symptoms preoperatively, were more likely to have syringomyelia and arachnoid dissection intraoperatively, and had decreased presentations to the ED postoperatively. Additional studies could further elucidate the mechanism behind the association between CIM and scoliosis.

articles.title: ICU utilization, capacity strain, and mortality before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.journal_full: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic created a unique instance of hospital capacity strain including deviations in ICU bed utilization.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate trends in ICU utilization among patients with common critical illness syndromes before, during, and after the pandemic, and across degrees of hospital capacity strain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: At 26 U.S. hospitals across two health systems, 2013-2024, we performed a retrospective cohort study among high-acuity patients with sepsis and/or acute respiratory failure (ARF) who did not require mechanical ventilation or vasopressor support in the emergency department. We modeled ICU admission rates and hospital mortality across eras and associations between validated hospital strain indices and ICU admission.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: ICU admission rates decreased markedly from the pre-pandemic to the pandemic era and were sustained in the post-pandemic era: sepsis (n = 136,153) 24% (24-24%) pre-pandemic, 16% (15-16%) pandemic, and 14% (14-14%) post-pandemic; ARF (n = 63,290) 36% (35-36%) pre-pandemic, 25% (25-26%) pandemic, and 23% (22-24%) post-pandemic; all p < 0.001. Increasing hospital capacity strain was associated with reduced predicted probability of ICU admission (sepsis: 29% [29-30%] ICU admission at lowest strain to 9% [8-9%] at highest strain; ARF: 51% [49-52%] at lowest strain to 15% [14-16%] at highest strain; all p < 0.001). Compared to the pre-pandemic era, in the post-pandemic era patients with sepsis (11% [11-11%] vs. 14% [13-14%]) and ARF (12% [11-12%] vs. 14% [14-15%]) had reduced mortality (both p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among high acuity patients with sepsis and ARF who did not require initial life support, ICU admission rates decreased during and after the pandemic.

articles.title: Pre-pandemic Probable Sarcopenia and COVID-19-Related Healthcare Utilization Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults : A Retrospective Cohort from Health and Retirement Study.
articles.journal_full: Annals of geriatric medicine and research

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sarcopenia has become a significant concern that detrimentally affects older adults' health. Patients with sarcopenia demonstrated higher disease severity and mortality rates of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). This study aims to evaluate the effect of pre-pandemic probable sarcopenia on COVID-19 related healthcare demands among older adults living in community settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study was conducted using a Health and Retirement Study, a national representative dataset for older adults in the US. The study included participants with COVID-19 diagnosis and retrospectively assessing their sarcopenia status using a SARC-F questionnaire.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study cohort included 354 participants with COVID-19 with a mean age of 61.03 years (SD = 9.49). Probable sarcopenia was identified in 13.56% of the study population. In adjusted analyses, probable sarcopenia was independently associated with higher odds of COVID-19-related emergency room visits (OR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.03-4.57), hospitalization (OR = 3.12, 95% CI: 1.37-7.12), and oxygen or ventilator requirement (OR = 3.15, 95% CI: 1.08-9.21). Female sex was associated with lower odds of hospitalization and oxygen/ventilator requirement. Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic participants demonstrated significantly higher odds of COVID-19-related healthcare utilization compared with Non-Hispanic White participants. No statistically significant interaction effects were observed between probable sarcopenia and sex or physical activity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pre-pandemic probable sarcopenia was independently associated with increased COVID-19-related healthcare utilization among community-dwelling older adults. These findings highlight the importance of early identification and management of sarcopenia in older adults to potentially reduce severe COVID-19 outcomes. Further studies are warranted to evaluate targeted preventive interventions.

articles.title: The cath lab readiness gap: a national survey of technology-driven role shifts and training needs among nurses and radiographers in France.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Rapid technological change in cath labs is redistributing operational responsibilities towards nurses and radiographers. We aimed to quantify this redistribution, and to assess whether training, regulatory framing, and professional recognition have kept pace.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: A national cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2025 among 371 professionals in French catheterisation or electrophysiology laboratories (207 nurses, 60 radiographers, 78 cardiologists, 26 nurse managers). The primary outcome - perceived change in responsibilities - was analysed as binary (moderate or strong increase vs other responses) by logistic regression adjusted for profession, age, sex, and seniority. A strong increase in responsibilities of nurses and radiographers was reported by 54.6% of nurses and 48.3% of radiographers, versus 25.6% of cardiologists and 38.5% of nurse managers. Nurse/radiographer status was the strongest predictor (adjusted OR 6.11 [95% CI 2.86-13.66] vs cardiologists and nurse managers; p < 0.001). Training was predominantly apprenticeship-based (on-the-job mentoring, 66.3%); the perceived adequacy of nurses' and radiographers' initial training was rated 20/100 by nurses and 31.5/100 by radiographers, versus 40/100 by cardiologists (p < 0.001). About half of nurses and radiographers considered that procedures are often performed outside the formal regulatory scope (52% and 45%, respectively); 93% of nurses and 90% of radiographers demanded regulatory clarification.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Technology is redistributing responsibilities towards nurses and radiographers faster than training, regulatory framing, or recognition - a readiness gap perceived far more acutely by paramedical than medical professionals. Every technology deployment should integrate team readiness, regulatory clarification, and recognition commensurate with current practice.

articles.title: The occult hypoperfusion index: a bedside formula to identify undetected critical illness.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The prehospital modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) score identifies patients with organ dysfunction but cannot detect normotensive occult hypoperfusion. To characterize the physiological correlation structure of mSOFA misclassification groups and to derive, internally validate and externally validate a bedside Occult Hypoperfusion Index (OHI) targeting undetected critical illness in patients classified as low acuity by the mSOFA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Prospective multicenter cohort study. Consecutive adults with acute illness attended by three physician-led emergency medical services. Prehospital mSOFA score computed from five point-of-care variables (mean arterial pressure, Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS], SpO₂/FiO₂ ratio, creatinine, and lactate). Primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 48 h of the index event. The index was then applied without refitting to an independent prospective cohort from Graz, Austria.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 16,106 enrolled patients, 933 (5.8%) died within 48 h. Cross-tabulation of mSOFA threshold and mortality yielded 848 true positives (5.3%), 85 false negatives (FN, 0.5%), 2,136 false positives (13.3%), and 13,037 true negatives (80.9%). Correlation analysis revealed that the FN group was uniquely sparse, with a dominant lactate-GCS coupling of ρ=+0.616 (p<.001). This co-variation was formalized as OHI=lactate × (16 - GCS). Applied to the mSOFA < 5 subgroup (n = 13,122), the OHI achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.851 (95% CI, 0.816-0.885), outperforming lactate alone (0.755; DeLong p = .004) and GCS alone (0.630; DeLong p < .001). In the external cohort (n = 802; 67 deaths), the OHI at the pre-specified threshold achieved an area under the curve of 0.861 (95% CI, 0.699-0.990), with sensitivity 80.0% and specificity 74.8%, and showed no evidence of miscalibration.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In a large prospective prehospital cohort, a multiplicative index derived from correlation analysis of mSOFA misclassification identified patients who died within 48 h despite being classified as low acuity. These findings are hypothesis-generating: the index was derived in one health system and externally validated in another, but the external estimates rest on few events and prospective evaluation before clinical use remains necessary. Consistent discrimination across three geographically distinct EMS systems in a leave-one-region-out analysis supports, but does not establish, its generalisability; this has now been extended to an independent cohort from a different country.

articles.title: Circulating miR-10b-5p drives Kawasaki vasculitis via endothelial reprogramming and nominates CXCL8 as an early diagnostic biomarker.

abstract.text: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis and the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, yet no specific biomarker enables early diagnosis at emergency department presentation. We aimed to define the molecular mechanisms driving KD vasculitis and to identify a clinically actionable early diagnostic marker. Whole microRNA sequencing of buffy coat specimens from patients with KD and febrile controls identified 68 upregulated microRNAs, of which 13 were prioritized. Candidates were validated in two KD-like vasculitis mouse models, and miR-10b-5p was consistently elevated. Inhibition of miR-10b-5p by a miRCURY locked nucleic acid inhibitor attenuated aortic root inflammation in vivo. In human coronary artery endothelial cells from adult donors, miR-10b-5p directly suppressed marker of proliferation Ki-67 (MKI67) and chromobox 5 (CBX5), driving a transition from proliferative and metabolic programs toward a proinflammatory phenotype, as confirmed by single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing. Chromatin accessibility profiling revealed increased accessibility at the C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (CXCL8) promoter, and motif analysis identified CCAAT enhancer binding protein alpha (CEBPA) as the key transcriptional activator; CEBPA knockdown abrogated miR-10b-5p-induced CXCL8 upregulation, and direct binding was confirmed by binding assays and chromatin immunoprecipitation. Serum CXCL8 was markedly elevated in patients with KD relative to febrile controls at first presentation before definitive diagnosis and declined significantly at the 8-week follow-up. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated diagnostic utility, with sensitivity and specificity of 83.3% at an optimal cut-off of 20.91 pg/ml. In conclusion, we define a miR-10b-5p-MKI67/CBX5-CEBPA-CXCL8 axis driving endothelial reprogramming and neutrophil-recruiting inflammation in KD and identify serum CXCL8 as a candidate biomarker for timely KD recognition.

articles.title: Serum lactate distribution across neurologic emergencies: implications for seizure identification.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Serum lactate is routinely measured in emergency departments (EDs) as a marker of systemic metabolic stress, but its distribution across neurologic emergencies is poorly characterized. We evaluated serum lactate distributions among patients with suspected neurologic emergencies and its utility for seizure identification.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 22,430 consecutive ED visits and identified 637 ambulance-transported patients with suspected neurologic emergencies. All underwent venous blood gas analysis and non-contrast computed tomography on arrival. Serum lactate levels were compared among seizure (SZ), cerebral infarction (INF), transient ischemic attack (TIA), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), and other diagnoses. Multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), and classification and regression tree (CART) analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Serum lactate differed significantly across diagnostic groups (P < 0.001) and was highest in patients with SZ and SAH. Among patients evaluated for ischemic stroke, age and serum lactate independently predicted SZ. ROC analysis showed moderate discrimination between SZ and ischemic stroke (INF/TIA) (area under the curve, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.73-0.90). CART identified 4.05 mmol/L as the primary lactate threshold, with age providing additional stratification. Patients with lactate ≥4.05 mmol/L and age < 59.5 years had a 100% probability of SZ.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Serum lactate shows distinct distributions across neurologic emergencies encountered in the ED. Although not disease-specific, age-adjusted interpretation of serum lactate may improve seizure identification in patients presenting with suspected stroke. Because lactate measurement is rapid and routinely available, it may provide practical support for early diagnostic decision-making.

articles.title: [Crisis in sight: The gradual buildup to a crisis admission of people with dementia].

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine which clinical and contextual factors precede crisis admissions in people with dementia.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective medical record review within a nursinghome organization, comparing crisis and planned admissions.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Analysis of new admissions over a 3month preadmission period up to 2 weeks postadmission. Assessed variables included somatic stability, behavioral symptoms, caregiver burden, hospital and ED contacts, psychotropic use and legal status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 419 admissions were analyzed. Crisis admissions (n=304) involved individuals with apparent somatic stability but clear cognitive deterioration, increasing behavioral symptoms and rising caregiver burden. More ED visits without hospital admission, more behavioral incidents and higher psychotropic use occurred in the preceding period. The proportion of involuntary admissions was substantial.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Crisis admissions represent the endpoint of gradually increasing instability. Early recognition and proactive care planning within a strong primarycare network are essential to prevent, or prepare for, escalation and ensure care aligns with evolving needs.

articles.title: Hajj vaccination-related awareness, attitudes, perceptions, and post-vaccination experiences of local pilgrims and Ministry of Health workers: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal_full: Journal of infection and public health

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Vaccination is an important preventive measure during Hajj, but awareness and attitudes may vary among groups Hajj participants. This study assessed awareness, attitude and perceptions toward vaccination and described self-reported post-vaccination symptoms and subsequent healthcare utilization among local Hajj pilgrims and Ministry of Health (MOH) workers assigned to Hajj duties in 2025.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted using an electronic questionnaire distributed in November-December 2025 to local Hajj pilgrims and MOH workers assigned to Hajj. Descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, t-tests, and unadjusted analyses explored factors associated with awareness. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses examined factors associated with a positive attitude toward Hajj vaccination.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 953 participants (434 MOH workers and 519 pilgrims). Awareness of the health value of Hajj vaccination was higher among workers (87.6% vs. 74.8%, p < 0.001). Regarding attitude toward the mandatory Hajj meningococcal vaccine, 86.4% reported willingness to receive it even if optional, with no significant group difference. Awareness was associated with a positive attitude toward Hajj vaccination and remained associated with a positive attitude after adjustment (adjusted OR 4.31, 95% CI 2.84-6.56, p < 0.001). Older age, non-Saudi nationality, and absence of medical conditions were also independently associated with a positive attitude. More information about Hajj vaccines was reported by 60.6% of participants. Among participants assessed for post-vaccination symptoms, 26.0% reported one or more symptom, most commonly injection-site pain and low-grade fever/chills/headache, and healthcare utilization following symptoms was limited.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Awareness of the health value of Hajj vaccination was associated with a positive attitude after adjustment for relevant covariates. As awareness and attitude were measured simultaneously, this indicates an adjusted association, not a causal relationship. The findings support the importance of clear and accessible Hajj vaccination information and the need to strengthen vaccination-related awareness among Hajj participants and healthcare workers.

articles.title: Retrograde gearshift pedicle probe-assisted reduction of displaced superior pubic rami fractures: A technical note.

abstract.text: Percutaneous fixation of superior pubic ramus fractures relies on establishment of safe corridors. Rotational and multiplanar deformity due to fracture disrupts the corridors and percutaneous or open reduction of these fractures is challenging. Retrograde insertion of a curved gearshift pedicle probe allows the surgeon to create a joystick to affect translation, rotation and angulation with a single instrument to restore the superior pubic ramus corridor and allow passage of an antegrade wire or screw. Following corridor restoration, reduction was captured antegrade, while definitive implant type and trajectory were selected independently according to fracture and osseous corridor morphology. Three displaced superior pubic ramus fractures were treated using this technique including mid-ramus, high ramus and segmental fractures with translational and rotational components. The probe was effectively used to de-rotate and reduce the fractures to allow for safe insertion of internal fixation with full containment and no complications. The curved gearshift pedicle probe is a rigid intramedullary reduction aid capable of multiplanar fragment manipulation and restoration of superior pubic ramus corridor while preserving independent selection of definitive fixation.

articles.title: Latent Profile and Decision Tree Analysis of Humanistic Care Satisfaction in Critically Ill ED Patients in China.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patient satisfaction with humanistic care varies among critically ill patients in emergency departments, yet little is known about its subgroup characteristics in China.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore the latent classes of humanistic care satisfaction among critically ill patients in emergency departments in China and the factors associated with these classes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: From October 2025 to January 2026, a survey was conducted among 663 critically ill patients treated in the emergency departments of five tertiary hospitals in Jiangxi Province, China. Of the 712 questionnaires distributed, 663 valid responses were returned, yielding an effective response rate of 93.12%. Data were collected using a general demographic questionnaire, a perceived value scale, and an emergency humanistic care satisfaction scale. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was performed to identify distinct subgroups of humanistic care satisfaction, and multinomial logistic regression along with decision tree modeling was used to examine the factors associated with these latent classes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three latent classes of humanistic care satisfaction were identified (entropy=0.996): a high-satisfaction group (57.5%), a moderate-satisfaction group (23.1%), and a low-satisfaction group (19.4%). Multinomial logistic regression revealed that age, education level, monthly household income, waiting time before treatment, and perceived value were significantly associated with the latent classes (P < 0.05). Among these, education level, waiting time, and perceived value were the most important associated variables, with perceived value positioned at the root node of the decision tree model. The decision tree model achieved an overall accuracy of 84.0%, but sensitivity for the low-satisfaction group was only 43.8%, limiting its clinical utility as a standalone screening tool.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Humanistic care satisfaction among critically ill emergency department patients in China exhibits distinct subgroup characteristics, which may inform the development of targeted quality improvement strategies.

articles.title: Longer wait times after ED-initiated buprenorphine associated with lower appointment attendance.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Buprenorphine, a medication for opioid use disorder, improves patient outcomes, and emergency department induction of buprenorphine (EDIB) offers a low-barrier entry to treatment. While longer intervals between referral and first outpatient appointment in non-ED settings are known to decrease attendance, the effect of the interval between EDIB and first outpatient follow-up has not been established.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To examine how the wait time between EDIB and the first outpatient appointment for medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) affects attendance at that initial visit. We tested the null hypothesis that wait time is not associated with attendance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, data were collected on adult ED patients who received EDIB (observed induction) or a buprenorphine prescription only (unobserved induction) between July 1, 2019, and December 31, 2025. Follow-up appointment attendance was obtained from referral centers. Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney U tests were used to compare attendance across demographic variables. Multivariable logistic regression estimated the adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of appointment attendance, controlling for demographics, insurance status, buprenorphine formulation, induction type, primary opioid, and polysubstance use. A Kaplan-Meier curve illustrated the relationship between appointment attendance and wait time.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 301 included individuals (65.4% male, 74.8% white, 30.9% insured), 51.2% attended the follow-up appointment. No associations were observed with demographics, substance use factors, or buprenorphine administration characteristics (all p > 0.05). Each additional day of wait time increased the odds of non-attendance by 31% (AOR = 1.310, 95% CI 1.099-1.560). The wait time at which attendance probability reached 50% was 3 days (95% CI 2.493-3.507).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A shorter wait time from EDIB to the first outpatient follow-up appointment is associated with increased appointment attendance. This study was limited to a single ED and may not be generalizable to all EDIB programs.

articles.title: Troponin Request Indications and Subsequent Cardiac Management in Acute Care: A Retrospective Quality Improvement Project.

abstract.text: Introduction Troponin-I tests are recommended for suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but troponin-I can also be raised in many other conditions. The test is widely available and frequently requested. Results from requests without a clear indication can be difficult to interpret and may lead to further investigations. We looked at the range of indications for troponin-I requests and what happened after an elevated result. Aim This quality improvement project (QIP) had two aims: to describe how the documented indication for troponin-I requests related to recorded further investigation or management after a result meeting local rule-in criteria and to assess whether a poster and a teaching session changed the proportion of requests with chest pain or electrocardiogram (ECG) changes (the primary outcome). No numerical target was set in advance. Methods This was a retrospective QIP at a single district general hospital using Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles: baseline data collection, a poster (PDSA 1) and a teaching session for emergency department (ED) doctors (PDSA 2). Troponin-I was measured using the Atellica IM High-Sensitivity Troponin-I assay. Patients met local rule-in criteria for a 'likely myocardial infarction' if the result was above 120 ng/L, or rose by at least 20 ng/L at two hours. Each request was assigned to one of three symptom-based categories using the documented indication: chest pain or ECG changes, other possible cardiac symptoms, or other presentations. The outcome was recorded as further cardiac investigation or management (from the discharge summary) in those meeting the criteria. Fisher's exact and chi-square tests were used, and comparisons between cycles were exploratory. Results Of 1,048 patients screened, 988 were included (baseline 489, PDSA 1,282, PDSA 2,217). Overall, 674 (68.2%) had chest pain or ECG changes, 167 (16.9%) had other possible cardiac symptoms and 147 (14.9%) had other presentations. In total, 95 patients (9.6%) met local rule-in criteria, and 42 of these (44.2%) had recorded further investigation or management. The proportion of requests with chest pain or ECG changes did not change significantly across the cycles (69.3%, 64.2% and 71.0%; p = 0.21). In exploratory comparisons, the proportion of all patients who met the criteria and had recorded investigation or management rose from 2.7% to 5.7% and 6.0% (p = 0.048 for each versus baseline), although this cannot be attributed to the interventions. Among those who met the criteria, recorded further investigation or management followed in 38/58 (65.5%) requests with chest pain or ECG changes, 4/22 (18.2%) with other possible cardiac symptoms and 0/15 (0%) with other presentations (chest pain or ECG changes versus the other two groups combined: odds ratio (OR) 15.7, 95% confidence interval (CI) 4.9-50.5). Conclusions Among patients meeting local rule-in criteria, recorded further cardiac investigation or management was more frequent in those with chest pain or ECG changes than in those with other presentations. We saw no clear change in requesting after a poster and a single teaching session. These are exploratory findings suggestive of an association only, and future work could evaluate more active approaches, such as a mandatory indication field, alongside balancing measures.

articles.title: Task-specific gait biomechanics following unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury may experience residual functional limitations. It remains unclear how these limitations manifest during tasks with different biomechanical demands. This exploratory study compared task-specific gait biomechanics between patients after fixation and healthy controls.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective cross-sectional observational study, 11 patients after unilateral iliosacral screw fixation (mean age 68.73 ± 9.89 years; 10 women) were compared with 21 healthy controls (52.48 ± 20.36 years; 11 women). Participants performed level walking, stair climbing, and step crossing using an Xsens MVN inertial motion capture system. Pelvic kinematics and model-estimated muscle activation and joint contact forces were evaluated using Computed MyoGraphy. Repeated trials were analyzed using participant-level random-intercept mixed models adjusted for age and sex. Pelvic rotation during stair climbing was the primary outcome; other outcomes were secondary or exploratory.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Pelvic rotation during stair climbing was lower in patients (adjusted difference -5.45°, 95% CI -7.98 to -2.92°; within-family FDR-adjusted q = 0.0003). Contralateral pelvic tilt during step crossing was greater (adjusted difference 1.44°, 95% CI 0.46-2.41°; q = 0.011). No statistically significant group differences were detected in the analyzed level-walking parameters, thoracic counter-rotation, lower-limb muscle activation, or hip joint contact-force asymmetry. Model-estimated peak L5-S1 joint contact force during stair climbing was lower in patients (adjusted difference -0.70 × body weight; q = 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Patients after posterior pelvic ring injury treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation showed task-specific differences in pelvic movement during demanding locomotor activities. The findings support including stair and step tasks in functional assessment, but do not establish that fixation caused the observed differences. Small sample size, demographic imbalance, and the absence of patient-reported outcomes limit clinical interpretation.

articles.title: Painless Takotsubo Syndrome Triggered by Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Retrospective Observational Study of Seven Cases.

abstract.text: Takotsubo syndrome (TS) as a manifestation of acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation is uncommonly reported. Emotional and adrenergic stress, hypoxemia, negative intrathoracic pressure, and the use of beta-agonists are frequently implicated in triggering myocardial dysfunction in this setting. We present a retrospective study of seven cases of TS in patients with COPD exacerbation in which none reported typical chest pain, representing a diagnostic challenge in patients with an apparent clinical justification for their dyspnea. All patients had electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, underwent echocardiography and coronary angiography or coronary computed tomography angiography, and received a confirmed diagnosis of TS. Five patients achieved complete recovery of ventricular function, one had partial recovery, and one died during hospitalization due to refractory ventricular arrhythmia. Systematic use of electrocardiography and cardiac biomarkers in COPD exacerbation enabled early diagnosis and appropriate management in the absence of typical angina.

articles.title: Covert brain infarction in the emergency department: incidence and outcomes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Covert brain infarction (CBI) is defined by neuroimaging evidence of cerebral infarction without history of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). The prevalence and management of covert brain infarction in the emergency department (ED) is not well understood. This study aimed to examine the prevalence, management, and one-year outcomes of patients with covert brain infarction detected during ED neuroimaging for non-stroke or TIA reasons.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational cohort study included ED patients from two academic hospitals with 24/7 access to computed tomography (CT). The primary outcome was detection of covert brain infarction on CT; secondary outcomes included stroke prevention therapy initiation or modification, specialist referral, and one-year adverse outcomes. Eligible patients were 50 years or older without history of stroke, TIA, or intracranial hemorrhage, who underwent CT in the ED for reasons unrelated to stroke or TIA from January 1 to December 31, 2022. Exclusion criteria included evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or final ED diagnosis of stroke/TIA.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 6,535 eligible individuals, a total of 102 patients (1.6%) had covert brain infarction detected on neuroimaging. These patients (age: 78.5 ±10.7 years; 61% male) had substantial vascular risk factors, including hypertension (62.7%), dyslipidemia (45.1%), atrial fibrillation (26.5%), diabetes (20.6%), and smoking (41.2%). Prior to ED visit, 18.6% of patients were on antiplatelets and 23.5% were on anticoagulation. Among those with covert brain infarction discharged from the ED, 91.7% received no change in therapy. In one year after the index visit, 1 patient had a stroke/TIA (1.0%), 4 had a myocardial infarction (3.9%), 2 were diagnosed with new atrial fibrillation (2.0%), and 14 died (13.7%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Patients with covert brain infarction detected in the ED had multiple vascular risk factors, and ED physician initiation or modification of new stroke therapy was uncommon, underscoring the need for further characterization and ED-specific pathways for management of this population.

articles.title: Systematic Literature Review on the Impact of Hospitalisation and Associated Complications on Patients with Bacterial Infections Receiving Intravenous Antibiotics.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Hospitalisation, which carries a risk of hospital-acquired complications (HAC), is common for intravenous (IV) antibiotic treatment and is recommended for serious infections, including complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI). We conducted two systematic literature reviews (SLR) to evaluate IV-line complications (IVLC) associated with short-term IV antibiotic treatment in patients with bacterial infections and assess hospitalisation-related and hospital-acquired complications (including infections).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Studies of patients hospitalised with any bacterial infection treated with short-term (≤ 30 days) IV antibiotics, published during 2013-2023, were identified in MEDLINE, Embase and other sources. SLR1 included prevalence and incidence rate of IVLC and impact on outcomes and healthcare resource utilisation (HCRU). SLR2 included prevalence of HAC, length of stay (LOS), readmission and costs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
