abstract.text: In SLR1 (36 primary studies), median prevalence and incidence rate of any IVLC for all patients were 6.1% (18 studies) and 3.4 per 1000 catheter/outpatient antimicrobial treatment-days (7 studies), respectively. In patients with cUTI, median prevalence of any IVLC was 1.7% (1 study). Prevalence of IVLC was lower in patients who transitioned from IV-to-oral antibiotics versus IV cohort (5 studies). IVLC increased HCRU, including rehospitalisation, LOS, emergency department visits and IV-line replacement. In SLR2 (36 primary studies), median prevalence of HAC (25 studies) ranged from 0.2% (UTI) to 11.5% (fall) and for hospital-acquired infections in patients with cUTI (5 studies) from 0.2% (Clostridium difficile infection) to 5.4% (new infection). In all patients, each additional day in hospital was associated with a 1.4-1.6% increase in the probability of a hospital-acquired infection, while having a HAC increased LOS by up to 28 days (range: 0-28 days; 12 studies) and was associated with readmission and additional healthcare costs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hospital-acquired complications, including IVLC, are common and associated with increased HCRU among patients receiving < 30 days of IV antibiotics for bacterial infections.

articles.title: Activated partial thromboplastin time following Kcentra® versus Balfaxar® reversal of apixaban, rivaroxaban, and warfarin: a propensity-score matched cohort study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Kcentra® and Balfaxar® are the four-factor prothrombin concentrates (4F-PCCs) available in the United States. Both contain heparin to prevent in-vial activation, but Balfaxar® contains approximately 2-10 times more heparin versus Kcentra®. Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is commonly used to monitor heparin activity. This study compared aPTT changes following administration of Kcentra® versus Balfaxar® for apixaban, rivaroxaban, and warfarin reversal.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, retrospective, propensity-score matched cohort study included adults given Kcentra® or Balfaxar® for apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin reversal. Patients had a baseline aPTT and a repeat aPTT within eight hours after 4F-PCC administration. Patients were matched 1:1 based on baseline aPTT and 4F-PCC dose. The primary outcome was aPTT change following administration. Secondary outcomes were hemostatic effectiveness within 24 h, new thrombotic events within seven days, and all-cause mortality within seven days.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1026 orders were screened, of which 46 patients had a 4F-PCC order meeting inclusion criteria and 30 were successfully matched (15 in each group). Median (IQR) aPTT change was -1.2 (-5.4 to 0.9) s with Kcentra® and -2.4 (-10.7 to -0.4) s with Balfaxar®. The median difference (95% CI) was 2 (-3.2 to 9.1) s and was not statistically different between groups (p = 0.468). There was not a statistical difference between groups for hemostatic effectiveness, new thrombotic event, or all-cause mortality, but the CIs for the between-group differences were wide.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this small propensity-score matched cohort of patients treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin, Kcentra® and Balfaxar® were not associated with significantly different changes in aPTT despite their markedly different heparin content. No statistically significant between-group differences were identified for hemostatic effectiveness, thrombotic events, or all-cause mortality, but the wide CIs preclude any conclusion of clinical equivalence. Larger studies focusing on patient-oriented outcomes are needed.

articles.title: A Nomogram Based on MEWS, SpO2, Lactate, and Procalcitonin for Early Prediction of Septic Shock in Emergency Department Patients with Suspected Sepsis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore the early predictive value of a modified early warning score (MEWS) combined with bedside lactate, procalcitonin (PCT), and SpO2 for the development of septic shock in patients with suspected sepsis in the emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-center, prospective observational cohort study was designed, enrolling patients with suspected sepsis admitted to the emergency department of Beijing Electric Power Hospital of State Grid Corporation of China from June 2024 to June 2025. Early in the admission, MEWS, blood lactate, PCT, and oxygen saturation were collected. A multivariate logistic regression model was built, and the model's discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method, and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 302 patients were included, of whom 36 (11.9%) developed septic shock within 72 hours. Multivariate analysis revealed that lower SpO2, higher MEWS score, higher lactate, and higher PCT were independent predictors of septic shock. The final combined prediction model included SpO2, MEWS, lactate, and PCT, with an AUC of 0.775 (95% CI: 0.687-0.863) for predicting septic shock. After Bootstrap internal validation, the corrected C-index was 0.733 and the model calibration was good. Decision curve analysis showed that the model had clinical net benefit over a broad range of threshold probabilities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The combined prediction model based on SpO2, MEWS, lactate, and PCT can effectively identify high-risk patients who may progress to septic shock early in the emergency department.

articles.title: Modern Systemic Therapies for Psoriasis in Active-Duty German Soldiers: A Retrospective Single-Center Study of Treatment Outcomes and Service-Wide Operational Burden.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Several armed forces treat psoriasis as a categorical barrier to service, and systemic therapy can preclude enlistment or restrict deployment. These standards predate interleukin-17 and interleukin-23 inhibitors. We assessed efficacy, safety and drug survival of modern versus conventional systemic therapies in active-duty soldiers, and the psoriasis-attributable operational burden in the German Armed Forces.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Single-center retrospective cohort study. Of 142 active-duty soldiers with psoriasis seen in 2019-2023, 77 had received systemic therapy between 2004 and 2023 (first line 49 modern, 28 conventional, 127 treatment cycles in total). Endpoints were estimated Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) at initiation and at the last visit on first-line therapy, adverse events (CTCAE version 6.0), and drug survival (Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression). Operational outcomes came from four service-wide registries not linked to the cohort.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean estimated IGA improved by 2.0 points under first-line modern versus 0.8 points under conventional therapy (P < 0.001), and complete clearance (IGA 0) was reached by 38/49 (78%) versus 1/28 (3.6%) (P < 0.001). Adverse events caused discontinuation in 2/97 (2.1%) modern versus 14/30 (46.7%) conventional cycles (P < 0.001). No grade 3 or 4 laboratory abnormality occurred (0/60, 95% CI 0-6.0%). Modern therapy was associated with less discontinuation or switching (first-line hazard ratio 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.33; calendar-year adjusted 0.10, 95% CI 0.05-0.23). Service-wide, no declaration of permanent unfitness for service due to psoriasis was recorded over 20 years, and psoriasis caused 4 of 7096 repatriations (0.056%). Of 87 diving-fitness assessments documenting psoriasis, among 15,718 in total, one (1.1%) was negative, owing to psoriatic arthritis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this single-center military cohort, modern systemic therapies were associated with higher clearance, fewer adverse-event discontinuations and longer drug survival. Service-wide data showed a low observed psoriasis-attributable operational burden. These findings support giving demonstrated treatment response greater weight in individualized military fitness assessment.

articles.title: Multimodal Point-of-Care Ultrasound Indices and Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: An Exploratory Prospective Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CSA-AKI) remains a common and multifactorial complication. Conventional biomarkers such as Serum Creatinine (SCr) detect injury late. This study explored whether perioperative multimodal Doppler ultrasonography could identify early haemodynamic alterations associated with CSA-AKI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, single-centre observational study, adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital underwent serial transthoracic echocardiography and renal Doppler ultrasonography at baseline, on postoperative day 1, and on day 4. Clinical and Doppler-derived parameters were compared between patients who developed CSA-AKI and those who did not. CSA-AKI was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Univariable logistic regression was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-four patients were included; 21 (39%) developed CSA-AKI. CSA-AKI was associated with higher EuroSCORE II (OR 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.50), diabetes mellitus (OR 7.47, 95% CI 2.17-29.3), reduced baseline mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62-0.96), lower renal End-Diastolic Velocity (EDV) at baseline (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59-0.91) and Day 4 (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.89), and Day 1 elevated Central Venous Pressure (CVP) (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.04-1.41). SCr increased, and eGFR declined in the CSA-AKI group by Day 4.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The study findings suggest that CSA-AKI was associated with a perioperative haemodynamic profile characterised by lower MAPSE and renal EDV and higher CVP. These unadjusted associations are consistent with impaired longitudinal ventricular function, reduced renal diastolic perfusion, and venous congestion, respectively, but they do not establish causality. Left-ventricular ejection fraction and Renal Resistive Index (RRI) were not statistically associated with CSA-AKI in this cohort. The findings support a hypothesis regarding possible haemodynamic contributors to CSA-AKI that requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: CSA-AKI was associated with lower MAPSE, higher CVP, and reduced renal EDV in univariable analyses. In this observational study, reduced renal EDV may represent a potential haemodynamic marker warranting further investigation; however, no diagnostic threshold or clinical implication can be inferred from these data. Adequately powered prospective studies are required to validate this association and determine its potential clinical utility.

articles.title: Comparison of end-of-life care processes and outcomes for patients treated by allopathic versus osteopathic physicians: a population-based cross-sectional study in the USA.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The USA has two types of medical schools: allopathic and osteopathic schools. End-of-life (EOL) care requires shared decision-making between patients and physicians and is potentially influenced by physician factors. However, little is known about whether allopathic and osteopathic physicians show different practice patterns in EOL settings. Therefore, this study aimed to compare EOL care processes and outcomes for beneficiaries treated by allopathic and osteopathic physicians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used cross-sectional data of a 20% random sample of fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥66 years who died in 2016-2019. Each beneficiary was attributed to a physician responsible for the largest number of evaluation and management visits in the last 6 months of life. Our outcomes were eight EOL care-related measures categorised into (1) advance care planning (ACP) and palliative care and (2) high-intensity care at the EOL. We estimated differences in these measures for beneficiaries treated by allopathic and osteopathic physicians, adjusting for physician and beneficiary characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 306 335 decedents, 240 907 (78.6%) were treated primarily by allopathic physicians and 65 428 (21.4%) by osteopathic physicians. We observed no differences in the eight measured indicators: billed ACP (adjusted rate, 14.1% vs 14.5%; p>0.99), palliative care counselling or hospice use in the last 180 days of life (62.4% vs 62.2%; p>0.99), emergency department visits (57.0% vs 56.9%; p>0.99), hospital admissions (50.9% vs 50.4%; p=0.31), intensive care unit admissions (27.3% vs 27.2%; p>0.99), mechanical ventilation or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (14.5% vs 14.4%; p>0.99), placement of feeding tubes (1.4% vs 1.4%; p>0.99) in the last 30 days of life, and death in acute care hospital (20.9% vs 20.4%; p=0.13).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We found no evidence of differences in the eight measured EOL care indicators between beneficiaries treated by allopathic versus osteopathic physicians, although differences in unmeasured aspects of care cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Concomitant pelvic ring injury compromises acetabular reduction quality: A propensity score-matched analysis with surgical sequence subgroup study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Concomitant pelvic ring injury is reported to compromise acetabular fracture reduction, yet matched comparisons are scarce and the optimal surgical sequence remains debated. We assessed whether pelvic ring injury compromises anatomical acetabular reduction, and whether fixation sequence influences reduction quality and complications.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 119 consecutive patients with isolated displaced acetabular fractures and 20 patients with combined pelvic ring and acetabular injuries treated at a tertiary trauma center (2004-2023). One-to-one propensity score matching using age, sex, and Letournel classification yielded 20 matched pairs (n = 40). Within the combined group, eight patients underwent acetabulum-first and 12 underwent pelvic ring-first fixation. The primary outcome was anatomical acetabular reduction (modified Matta criteria, 0-1 mm) graded by two independent reviewers. Secondary outcomes were pelvic ring reduction and postoperative complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Anatomical acetabular reduction was achieved in 14 of 20 isolated patients (70.0%) versus four of 20 combined patients (20.0%; p = 0.004). Within combined injuries, acetabulum-first showed a numerical trend toward better reduction (37.5% vs 8.3% anatomical; p = 0.132). Pelvic ring reduction did not differ between sequence subgroups (75.0% vs 83.3%; p = 0.450). Excluding pre-existing sciatic palsies, any complication occurred in two of eight acetabulum-first (25.0%) versus eight of 12 pelvic ring-first patients (66.7%; p = 0.170), driven by post-traumatic osteoarthritis (12.5% vs 41.7%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Concomitant pelvic ring injury significantly compromises anatomical acetabular reduction. Where precise pelvic ring reduction is achievable, pelvic ring-first fixation remains appropriate; where it is not, acetabulum-first or temporary pelvic stabilization followed by definitive fixation should be considered to avoid fixing the acetabulum onto a malreduced pelvic ring.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.

abstract.text: Valvular heart disease (VHD) affects a substantial proportion of the population and remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in surgical and transcatheter therapies, important challenges persist. VHD remains underdiagnosed, assessment of disease severity is often variable, and the optimal timing of intervention continues to evolve. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool across the spectrum of VHD care. AI-based electrocardiogram analysis can identify both existing and future VHD, while AI-guided point-of-care ultrasound extends screening to nonspecialist settings. Across multimodality imaging, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms enable automated, reproducible assessment of VHD. In echocardiography, AI supports grading of disease severity across the main valvular lesions, including Doppler interpretation and automated report generation. AI-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance facilitates automated assessment of ventricular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis, while AI-assisted cardiac computed tomography improves procedural planning for transcatheter interventions. In parallel, ML has identified distinct patient phenotypes in multiple valvular lesions with differing clinical trajectories and responses to intervention. This review summarizes current applications of AI in detection, multimodality imaging, and potential clinical decision support for VHD and discusses opportunities and challenges for integration into routine practice.

articles.title: Overnight stay in the emergency department and mortality in sepsis patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis management in the emergency department (ED) faces challenges due to overcrowding and prolonged boarding, yet the impact of overnight ED stays on outcomes remains unclear. This study evaluated whether sepsis patients who spend a night in the ED waiting for admission to a ward/intensive care unit (ICU) are at increased risk of in-hospital mortality or morbidity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective cohort study of sepsis patients who visited the ED and were admitted to the hospital between January 2021 and August 2024 across the ED of a large general hospital in China. Patients were stratified into an overnight ED stay (midnight-8:00 AM) and a non-overnight (admitted to a ward/ICUs before midnight) group. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included septic shock, ICU admission, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) and length of stay (LOS). Multivariable logistic regression and sensitivity analyses were used to compare end points between groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,208 sepsis patients were enrolled in the study, including 503 (42%) female and 705 (58%) male, with 624 (51.7%) in the overnight ED stay group and 584 (48.3%) in the non-overnight ED stay group. Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups. Unadjusted in-hospital mortality was similar (21.2% vs. 21.7%; risk difference (RD) 0.59 [-4.04 to 5.23]). Adjusted logistic regression analyses confirmed no mortality association (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) (95% confidence interval (CI)), 1.090 [0.805-1.477]; P = 0.579). No higher risk was observed for secondary outcomes: septic shock (aOR (95% CI), 1.020 [0.747-1.393]; P = 0.903), ICU admission (aOR 1.362 [0.983-1.895]; P = 0.064), or IMV (aOR (95% CI), 1.048 [0.710-1.549]; P = 0.813). Compliance with the Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines was comparable between groups(31.6% vs. 29.1%; RD, -2.46 [-7.63 to 2.73]). These findings were consistent across subgroups and sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cohort study, overnight ED boarding was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality or morbidity among sepsis patients when care adhered to SSC guidelines. These results suggest that high compliance with the SSC 1-h bundle may help mitigate potential risks associated with overnight ED boarding.

articles.title: An Emergency Department and Emergency Medical Services Superutilizer - A Case Report of a Multidisciplinary Approach to Resolution.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.text: Frequent emergency department (ED) visitors, referred to as high-need, high-cost, or "superutilizers," are a challenging population for the health care system. Superutilizers account for a disproportionate share of overall health care spending (5% of the population accounts for 50% of health care spending) and have therefore been a focus of research and intervention over the past decade. Although ED superutilizers have been described previously, we report a case that demonstrates the additional strain on the emergency medical services (EMS). A 65-year-old woman was the highest 9-1-1 caller for a major metropolitan area, averaging 1.6 transports per day. Identifying the root causes of a patient's frequent utilization can be difficult and sometimes requires stepping back, gaining a fresh perspective, or returning to basic questions, including "why is this patient failing home therapy?" In this case, undetected cognitive impairment was a significant contributor to her frequent utilization. A hospital/EMS paramedicine partnership facilitated detection and care for this root cause and stopped the frequent ED and 9-1-1 use. This case highlights the impact of superutilizers on EMS, the promising role of intervention teams, and the complexity of cognition/capacity determination in the ED.

articles.title: Candidate biomarkers predicting clinical outcome after hyperbaric oxygen against chronic radiation cystitis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO2) is effective against radiation cystitis. In this exploratory analysis we employed proteomics to assess biomarkers predicting clinical efficacy and the pharmacodynamics of HBO2 in radiation cystitis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Global quantitative proteomics was performed on biopsies taken before and after HBO2 in patients with radiation cystitis from the RICH-ART trial (NCT01659723). The proteome of HBO2 responders (R) was compared to non-responders (NR) and between R and NR at baseline. Immunohistochemistry was employed to assess the expression of potential biomarkers in urinary bladder biopsies. Biological processes were identified by using the STRING database.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among proteins more expressed in R than NR at baseline were neutrophil defensin 1 and less expressed were chymase and mast cell carboxypeptidase A (CPA3). Among processes differentiating R from NR at baseline were processes regulating translation and complement activation. The top enriched biological processes in NR after HBO2 were processes regulating antigen processing and presentation. Only a few processes were affected by HBO2 in responders. No significant differences in the number of chymase+, CPA3 + and tryptase+ mast cells were observed in bladder specimens between R and NR before and after HBO2. The staining intensity of tryptase, chymase, CPA3 and complement factors C3, C4 and C8 were similar between R and NR and after HBO2.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Multiple processes regulating the immune system, complement activation and translation in radiation cystitis are changed after HBO2. However, only a few processes were associated with the clinical efficacy of HBO2. The involvement of mast cells in the pathogenesis of radiation cystitis is suggested.

articles.title: Co-administration of adrenaline and landiolol during cardiopulmonary resuscitation in a swine model of ventricular fibrillation.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: We examined whether early co-administration of landiolol and adrenaline improves successful extubation, hemodynamics, and 48-h outcomes in a swine ventricular fibrillation (VF) model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, randomized, investigator-blinded study, VF was electrically induced in healthy piglets and left untreated for 8 min. Thirty-nine female Landrace/Large White piglets were randomized (1:1:1): adrenaline 0.02 mg/kg plus saline, adrenaline plus esmolol 0.5 mg/kg, or adrenaline plus landiolol 0.02 mg/kg. Treatment was administered at the initiation of mechanical cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), 2 min before attempting defibrillation. Primary outcome was successful extubation. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), 48-h survival, 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery, and hemodynamic variables during and after CPR.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Successful extubation occurred in 2/13 (15%) control, 6/13 (46%) esmolol, and 9/13 (69%) landiolol animals (overall p = 0.021); the rate was significantly higher with landiolol than with control (adjusted p = 0.046). ROSC rates were 46%, 69%, and 100%, respectively (p = 0.006); 48-h survival rates were 8%, 31%, and 54% (p = 0.046); and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery rates were 0%, 23%, and 46% (p = 0.022). The landiolol group had higher observed rates of ROSC and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery than the control group; these secondary analyses were exploratory. No pairwise difference was significant for 48-h survival. Exploratory analyses during the first 4 min of CPR identified higher observed values for selected hemodynamic variables and end-tidal carbon dioxide in the landiolol group at specific time points. Esmolol had intermediate observed outcome rates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Early administration of landiolol with adrenaline was associated with a higher successful extubation rate and better observed early CPR hemodynamics compared with adrenaline alone and had the highest rates of ROSC, 48-h survival, and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery. Secondary-outcome findings were exploratory, and landiolol was not statistically superior to esmolol.

articles.title: Emergency Physician-Performed Point-of-Care Ultrasound Identified Left Atrial Myxoma in Acute Cerebellar Infarction.

abstract.text: Cardiac myxoma is a rare but potentially curable cause of cardioembolic stroke. Early identification of a potential cardiac embolic source may be challenging when neurological symptoms predominate during the initial emergency department evaluation. A 72-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with acute-onset dizziness and vomiting. Although her National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 0, she was unable to walk independently. Electrocardiography demonstrated newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation. Because a cardioembolic mechanism was considered, the emergency physician performed bedside cardiac point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), which revealed a highly mobile left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum. POCUS was performed 28 min after arrival, before brain magnetic resonance imaging, which demonstrated multiple acute cerebellar infarctions without large-vessel occlusion. Intravenous alteplase was not administered despite presentation within the therapeutic time window. Anticoagulation with intravenous unfractionated heparin was initiated. Surgical resection was postponed after hemorrhagic transformation of the cerebellar infarction was detected on hospital day 14. The patient underwent complete tumor resection on hospital day 41, and histopathological examination confirmed cardiac myxoma. She was discharged on hospital day 54 with a favorable outcome. This case illustrates the potential value of emergency physician-performed cardiac POCUS for early identification of structural cardiac abnormalities during the initial evaluation of selected patients with suspected cardioembolic stroke.

articles.title: Perioperative Management of a Breastfed Child Whose Mother Was Receiving Injectable Semaglutide: A Case Report Outlining Use of Gastric Point-of-Care Ultrasound.

abstract.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), including semaglutide, are increasingly used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus and for weight management. Although generally effective, specific end-organ effects, including delayed gastric emptying, may impact the perioperative care of patients receiving these agents. Given these concerns, guidelines have been suggested for the perioperative care of patients receiving GLP-1 RAs. However, these recommendations do not specifically address the increasingly encountered scenario in which a breastfeeding mother is taking a GLP-1 RA and the breastfed infant or young child is presenting for anesthetic care. We present a 15-month-old breastfed child who presented for surgery and whose mother was receiving once-weekly injectable semaglutide. Given limited evidence-based medicine to guide perioperative care in this clinical scenario, preoperative gastric point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) was used to evaluate gastric volume before induction of anesthesia. Perioperative care of breastfed children of mothers receiving GLP-1 RAs is discussed, the role of gastric POCUS is presented, and options for perioperative care are reviewed.

articles.title: Hospital-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Pathogen Positivity and Distribution: A Six-Year Epidemiological Study in Beijing, 2020-2025.

abstract.text: Objective: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are imposing a great economic burden, morbidity, and mortality on the healthcare system. Eleven common respiratory pathogens, based on age of onset, clinical setting, season and calendar year during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, were analyzed to optimize clinical diagnosis and prevention. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, respiratory pathogen testing results of 9882 samples from RTI patients from January 2020 to December 2025 were included to statistically analyze the positivity, distribution and trend of change. Multiplex PCR combined with capillary electrophoresis was used to simultaneously detect 11 respiratory targets. Results: The overall positive detection rate was 24.71%, with the top three pathogens being human rhinovirus (HRV) (6.20%), influenza A virus (InfA) (4.28%), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (4.13%). The patients aged under 18 had the highest detection rates (≤6 years: 39.80%; 7 to 17 years: 37.95%). HRV, RSV and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) were the primary pathogens among pediatric patients, while InfA was predominant in adults (including those >65 years). The 11 pathogens were most common in emergency department patients (29.14%), followed by outpatient patients (28.57%). InfA was the most predominant virus, followed by HRV and RSV, in the intensive care unit, emergency department, and outpatient settings. The detection rate was highest in autumn (33.22%), followed by winter (26.61%). MP had the highest rate in autumn, and InfA was the most frequent in winter. During the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2022), the respiratory pathogen spectrum was dominated by HRV, RSV, and human parainfluenza virus (HPIV). And the prevalent pathogens shifted to InfA, MP and HRV during 2023-2025. Co-detections were observed in 8.03% of the positive cases, and 82.65% occurred in patients aged < 18 years. The dominant co-detections were HRV + MP, HRV + RSV and HRV + HPIV. Conclusions: The distribution of respiratory pathogens exhibited specific variations based on age, clinical setting, season, and calendar year, suggesting that differentiated prevention should be developed for different patients.

articles.title: The Triage Frailty and Comorbidity Tool for Risk Stratification of Older Patients Admitted from the Emergency Department to a Geriatric Ward.

abstract.text: Introduction: Frailty assessment in the Emergency Department (ED) may provide prognostic information beyond triage, but the value of the Triage Frailty and Comorbidity Tool (TFC) in older patients admitted to geriatric wards is uncertain. Methods: This retrospective study included patients aged ≥75 years admitted directly from the ED to Merano Hospital Geriatric Ward between May and September 2025. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality; in-hospital mortality was secondary. Analyses included logistic regression, AUROC estimation, predefined TFC ≥ 10% threshold performance, and Kaplan-Meier curves. Results: A total of 225 patients were included. Median age was 86 years (IQR 82-90), median length of stay was 9 days (IQR 6-13), 90-day mortality was 27.6% (62/225), and in-hospital mortality was 11.5% (26/225). Patients who died within 90 days had higher TFC values than survivors [49.5 (31.4-72.3) vs. 19.4 (6.5-43.8); p < 0.001]. Each 10-point increase in TFC was associated with higher odds of 90-day mortality (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.26-1.63; p < 0.001) and in-hospital mortality (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.18-1.62; p < 0.001). The AUROC was 0.747 for 90-day mortality and 0.732 for in-hospital mortality. TFC ≥ 10% identified 54/62 deaths, with a sensitivity of 87.1% and NPV of 87.9%. Survival was lower in patients with TFC ≥ 10% (log-rank p = 0.001). Conclusions: The TFC showed prognostic value in older patients admitted from the ED to geriatric care. Although discrimination was moderate, the TFC may support risk stratification during ED-to-ward transition.

articles.title: Job Satisfaction Among Healthcare Professionals During and Directly After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review of Psychosocial, Organizational and System-Level Factors.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic substantially changed working conditions in healthcare and increased the workload of healthcare professionals. This systematic review aimed to identify factors associated with job satisfaction among physicians, nurses, and paramedics during the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular emphasis on psychosocial, organizational, and system-level factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Searches were performed in ScienceDirect (10 January 2026), PubMed (16 January 2026), and Scopus (22 January 2026). Original studies published between 2020 and 2025 in English or Polish were eligible. Three researchers independently conducted the study selection and methodological assessment. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI critical appraisal tools. Fifteen studies involving physicians, nurses, and paramedics were included. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity among the included studies. The review was registered in the Open Science Framework.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Higher job satisfaction was associated with older age, longer length of service and higher remuneration. In contrast, lower job satisfaction was associated with direct work with patients infected with SARS-CoV-2, higher levels of stress and burnout, and poor work organization.

abstract.label: LIMITATIONS
abstract.text: The main limitations were related to the fact that only three databases were searched, the heterogeneity of the studies, and a language restriction, as only articles in Polish and English were included in the search.

articles.title: Pediatric cardiopulmonary resuscitation in the emergency department: Factors associated with outcome.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Pediatric cardiac arrest is usually studied either before hospital arrival or after admission, although the emergency department (ED) team resuscitates both. We examined factors associated with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), recurrent arrest and mortality in an ED cohort including both out-of-hospital cardiac arrests (OHCA) and in-ED cardiac arrests.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort of all 83 children who received cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in a university pediatric ED over 14 years (January 2010-March 2024). The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge; multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with ED mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median age was 35 months; 54.2% occurred out of hospital. ROSC was achieved in 42.2% and 30.1% survived the ED phase, but 9.9% survived to discharge. Epinephrine given later than 2 min was independently associated with ED mortality among the 27 patients with documented timing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.73; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.27-46.97). Beyond 20 min of CPR, each additional minute was associated with ED death (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.01-1.73). Recurrent arrest after ROSC in the ED occurred in 42.9%, of whom 6.7% survived versus 38.9% without recurrence (p = 0.039). Survival did not differ by arrest location, initial rhythm or timing of advanced airway management.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Resuscitation in the ED restored spontaneous circulation in many children, but few survived to discharge. Time to first epinephrine was independently associated with ED mortality in this cohort, whereas prolonged resuscitation and recurrent arrest after ROSC in the ED identified children at very high risk.

articles.title: Drug-Induced Electrolyte Disturbances in Older Adults Presenting to the Emergency Department: Mechanisms, Recognition and Prevention.

abstract.text: Many older adults attending the emergency department (ED) take medications that interfere with water and electrolyte balance. This narrative review, based on a structured PubMed/MEDLINE search covering January 2016 to September 2026, summarizes evidence on drug-associated disorders of sodium, potassium, magnesium and calcium in older ED patients. Thiazides, antidepressants, antiepileptic drugs, antipsychotics, proton pump inhibitors and desmopressin are associated with hyponatremia; with thiazides, the risk peaks in the first weeks of treatment and is highest in women aged 80 years or older. Lithium can cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, which may persist after discontinuation and cause hypernatremia when water intake is inadequate. Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, trimethoprim and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs predispose to hyperkalemia, particularly in chronic kidney disease; diuretics and proton pump inhibitors are associated with hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia; and denosumab can cause severe hypocalcemia in advanced kidney disease. Most of this evidence is observational, and drugs usually act together with comorbidities, acute illness and other medications. We propose a severity-based ED algorithm integrating medication history, laboratory, electrocardiographic and volume assessment (including point-of-care ultrasound) to guide stabilization, drug adjustment, safe correction and disposition. ED-based medication safety programs reduce inappropriate prescribing, but their effect on electrolyte-related outcomes remains unproven.

articles.title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy and Female Infertility: A Systematic Review of Human Clinical Evidence.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Female infertility represents a major global health issue, and effective treatment remains challenging in several infertility-related conditions. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) has been proposed as a potential adjunctive intervention in reproductive medicine, although human clinical evidence remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the available human evidence regarding the association between HBOT and reproductive outcomes in women with infertility or infertility-related conditions. Potential biological mechanisms, including the hypothetical involvement of sirtuin-related signaling in adaptive responses to intermittent hyperoxia, were also considered. Methods: A systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, LILACS and the Cochrane Library was updated through 10 May 2026. The search was restricted to studies published from 1 January 2016 to 10 May 2026, reflecting the review's prespecified focus on approximately the preceding decade of human clinical evidence. Original human studies investigating HBOT in women with infertility or infertility-related conditions and reporting reproductive outcomes were eligible. Study selection was conducted according to predefined eligibility criteria and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and the certainty of evidence for the main outcomes was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity and the absence of sufficiently comparable outcomes across studies, a pooled meta-analysis was not performed. Results: Seventy-six records were identified through electronic database searches, and 11 reports underwent full-text eligibility assessment. Two original human studies involving women with resistant thin endometrium or poor ovarian response met the eligibility criteria. In women with resistant thin endometrium undergoing frozen embryo transfer, endometrial thickness increased after HBOT (6.57 ± 1.23 vs. 5.76 ± 1.66 mm before HBOT; p = 0.002). Compared with propensity-score-matched concurrent controls, women receiving HBOT had a higher implantation rate (RR, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.26-7.14) and a higher intrauterine pregnancy rate after blastocyst transfer (RR, 2.96; 95% CI, 1.14-7.70). In women with poor ovarian response undergoing IVF/ICSI, fully adjusted analyses showed that HBOT was associated with a higher number of retrieved oocytes (β = 1.51; 95% CI, 0.92-2.10), available embryo rate (β = 24.29 percentage points; 95% CI, 7.27-41.31), and normal fertilization rate (β = 17.23 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.35-32.11). Clinical pregnancy occurred in 1 of 10 pre-HBOT cycles (10.0%) and 1 of 19 post-HBOT cycles (5.3%); one live birth was reported following HBOT. This single event does not provide a comparative estimate of live-birth rates. Certainty of evidence was very low for all outcomes assessed using GRADE: endometrial thickness, implantation, intrauterine pregnancy, number of oocytes retrieved, available embryo rate, and normal fertilization rate. Conclusions: Available human evidence reports associations between HBOT and selected reproductive outcomes in women with resistant thin endometrium or poor ovarian response. However, the evidence is based on only two small, non-randomized studies addressing different clinical populations and outcomes, and the certainty of evidence was very low for all outcomes assessed using GRADE. Current evidence is therefore insufficient to establish a causal therapeutic effect, support the routine use of HBOT for female infertility or define an optimal treatment protocol. Further well-designed prospective controlled studies are required.

articles.title: Sim-SEA: Integrating Significant Event Audit and In Situ Simulation to Support Patient Safety Learning and Organizational Change-A Prospective Single-Center Pilot Study in Pediatric Emergency Care.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Patient safety depends on healthcare systems' ability to learn from clinical experience and translate insights into system-level improvement. Significant Event Audit (SEA) is well established but may only partly capture the dynamic, context-dependent nature of clinical performance. Although in situ simulation is increasingly used to explore team performance and system vulnerabilities, its routine integration into formal risk-management pathways remains limited. We developed Sim-SEA, a structured approach embedding in situ simulation within the SEA learning cycle.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Sim-SEA adapted the seven-phase SEA framework to incorporate in situ simulation as a core component. We conducted a 12-month single-center, uncontrolled pre-post pilot study in a tertiary pediatric emergency department, comprising 10 Sim-SEA cycles. Self-perceived competence in technical and non-technical domains was assessed at baseline and immediately after simulation using a 6-item ad hoc questionnaire. A follow-up assessment was conducted among participants who subsequently encountered a real emergency. Participants' perceptions, system vulnerabilities, and improvement actions were also examined.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-nine physicians, residents, and nurses participated. Self-perceived competence improved significantly from baseline to post-simulation across ABCDE assessment, teamwork, situational awareness, communication, speak-up behavior, and decision-making (all p < 0.01). At follow-up, available for 35/59 participants (59.3%) who subsequently encountered a real emergency, self-perceived scores remained significantly higher than baseline. Implemented changes included workspace reorganization, a cognitive medication aid, and a standard operating procedure for role allocation. Participants reported greater engagement, reflective learning, psychological safety, and awareness of risks and system vulnerabilities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this single-center, uncontrolled pilot study, Sim-SEA was feasible as a structured method for embedding in situ simulation within clinical risk management and supported potential benefits for self-perceived learning and the identification and development of organizational and environmental improvement actions. Further studies should assess effects on objective competence and patient-safety outcomes.

articles.title: The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee 2026 guidelines for initial management of minimal, mild and moderate head injuries in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis and modified Delphi consensus study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Several clinical guidelines exist to identify intracranial injury (ICI) after head injury. The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee (SNC) published evidence- and consensus-based guidelines in 2000, updated in 2013. Since then, demographic changes, including an ageing population and increased use of antithrombotic therapy have prompted further revision. The aim of this study is to provide a clinically relevant update to the SNC guidelines for the initial management of adults with minimal, mild, or moderate head injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis addressed population, exposure, comparator, and outcome questions on which emergency department patients with minimal or mild head injury require head computed tomography (CT), direct discharge, in-hospital observation, or repeat CT. Evidence was graded using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were developed through a modified Delphi process with stakeholder review.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Twenty-nine stakeholders participated in developing a seven-point recommendation set and updated management flowcharts. Key changes include reduced emphasis on routine CT in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants, incorporation of glial fibrillary acidic protein and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 biomarkers, and use of structured observation as an alternative to CT in selected risk groups.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: The updated guidelines support risk-adapted imaging and observation strategies that may reduce unnecessary CT scans and hospital admissions, although further validation of safety and effectiveness is needed.

abstract.label: FUNDING
abstract.text: No specific funding.

articles.title: Pressure ulcer/injury risk assessment, prevalence and incidence in emergency room.

abstract.label: AIM OF THE STUDY
abstract.text: To analyse the pressure ulcer/injury risk assessment, prevalence and incidence in adult patients admitted to the emergency room in a Portuguese hospital.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: Quantitative, prospective, observational and cross-sectional study carried out between 1 November 2024 and 28 February 2025 in an emergency room of a Portuguese hospital. Skin and tissue integrity and pressure ulcer/injury risk assessment were performed at the time of emergency room admission and discharge, using the "Skin Assessment Tool" and the "Braden Scale". The participants recruitment and data collection were carried out by the nurses responsible for the emergency room in each shift, using a form developed specifically for this purpose. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sample of 156 participants. At the time of emergency room admission, 55.8% of the participants were at "high risk" of pressure ulcer/injury development. At the time of emergency room discharge the percentage of participants at "high risk" of pressure ulcer/injury development significantly increased up to 67.3%. The prevalence of pressure ulcers/injuries on admission was 2.6% and the incidence was 0%. Participants with "obesity", "altered state of consciousness"' and "advanced age" were more likely to be at "high risk" of pressure ulcers/injuries development. After the initial approach, 65.4% of the participants were transferred from the emergency room to other clinical areas of the emergency service/department.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The risk of developing pressure ulcers/injuries in emergency services/departments is a real problem. Preventive measures should be applied systematically since the moment of emergency room/service/department admission.

articles.title: Rethinking Mild Therapeutic Hypothermia After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Dead End or Missed Opportunity? An Expert Viewpoint.

abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest remains associated with high mortality and neurological disability. Mild therapeutic hypothermia has been questioned after large trials failed to demonstrate superiority over controlled normothermia with fever prevention. In this expert viewpoint, we argue that these neutral findings should not be interpreted as proof of biological futility in every patient and setting. The clinical effect of hypothermia may depend on patient phenotype, timing of initiation, cooling technique, temperature-control quality, and integration with contemporary post-resuscitation care. This may be particularly important in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention, in whom hypothermia can impair the pharmacokinetics and antiplatelet effects of oral P2Y12 inhibitors. Current evidence does not support routine hypothermia in all comatose survivors. However, uncertainty remains regarding its value in selected patients. Patients with an intermediate degree of ischemic brain injury may represent a plausible target for neuroprotection, but this remains an unproven hypothesis. Future trials should investigate whether injury severity modifies the effects of early, precisely delivered hypothermia, using standardized protocols, active normothermia as the comparator, and prespecified antithrombotic and post-resuscitation strategies.

articles.title: Exploring Esophageal Widening in Computed Tomography Performed in Critically Ill Patients.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Early diagnosis and therapy stratification represent central factors in the management of critically ill patients, today often assisted by clinical scores, which also include laboratory testing results. The aim of this study was to further characterize computed tomography-detected abnormal esophageal widening, which we often observe in critically ill patients in our emergency department when reading CT examinations. We expect this factor to be potentially meaningful for clinical evaluation and prognosis of critically ill patients. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, critically ill patients receiving CT trauma room imaging in our hospital's emergency department were included. In the first part of the analysis, esophageal diameter at four anatomical landmarks were compared between patients who survived and those who died within 28 days in all critically ill patients presenting with AEW. In the second exploratory part of the study, the relevance of the laboratory parameters and AEW in predicting mortality were analyzed. In part three, the correlation between the 28-day mortality of all critically ill patients and the presence of esophageal widening was assessed. Results: Esophageal widening was detected in 98 of all 1683 included patient examinations. Nineteen of these patients have died (19.4%), and ten of them (52.6%) suffered primarily from a cerebrovascular event. In the group of patients with AEW, cervical AEW was more frequent among deceased patients (63.2% vs. 27.8%; p = 0.0064), and mean maximal esophageal diameter was also greater among deceased patients (19.2 vs. 16.4 mm; p = 0.0392). Multiple laboratory parameters were also found to correlate with mortality in all patients with AEW. No significant correlation of AEW alone with 28-day mortality in all critically ill patients that received ED-CT could be demonstrated in our retrospective sample. Conclusions: Esophageal widening, especially in the upper segment, was found in a substantial proportion of critically ill patients, with increased width correlating with mortality risk in the group of patients with AEW. Future studies should include much larger patient cohorts and a prospective design to evaluate if AEW might be a candidate to serve as a potential parameter of clinical scores which aim at early patient stratification.

articles.title: Modified pneumonia risk score using lung ultrasound for the prediction of radiographic pneumonia in children.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The diagnosis of pneumonia in children based on clinical findings is challenging. The Pneumonia Risk Score (PRS), a clinical prediction tool, estimates the risk of radiographic pneumonia. Most children are classified as moderate-risk and are recommended to undergo chest x-ray (CXR). We hypothesized that lung ultrasound (LUS) may add diagnostic value beyond the PRS for predicting radiographic pneumonia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We studied a convenience sample of children 6 months to 18 years old enrolled in a prospective LUS registry who presented to the emergency department with acute respiratory complaints and underwent CXR and LUS. The primary outcome was radiographic pneumonia. Logistic regression included the five PRS clinical predictors, and LUS consolidation ≥1 cm with bronchograms was added to create the PRS + LUS model. We compared the area under the curve (AUC) of the PRS to the PRS + LUS, evaluated risk re-classifications, and proposed a novel diagnostic algorithm.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 275 children, 58 (21%) had radiographic pneumonia. LUS consolidation was strongly associated with pneumonia (OR 28.68 [95% CI, 9.98 to 82.43]). The PRS + LUS demonstrated greater diagnostic accuracy than the PRS alone (AUC 0.85 [95% CI, 0.77 to 0.89] versus 0.70 [95% CI, 0.61 to 0.76]; P < 0.001). Using our proposed novel two-step diagnostic algorithm, the PRS + LUS was calculated for patients assigned a moderate-risk score by PRS, resulting in assigning an additional 120 (44%) patients a high- or low-risk score, decreasing the moderate-risk category.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Adding LUS to the PRS improves prediction of radiographic pneumonia and may reduce CXR use, particularly among patients with moderate risk.

articles.title: Private Equity Acquisitions and Home Health Agency Use, Expenditures, and Quality.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Over the past 2 decades, the number of private equity (PE) acquisitions of Medicare home health agencies (HHAs) has increased considerably, with 6% of HHAs currently owned by PE firms.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the impact of PE acquisitions of HHAs on home health use, costs, and quality measures.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This cohort study used Medicare fee-for-service claims data from 2011 to 2022 and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services HHA Cost Reports to measure home health visits, expenditures, and health outcomes among Medicare-certified HHAs. The sample included only Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries 65 years and older with any HHA use. These data were linked to a novel dataset of PE acquisitions of HHAs. A stacked difference-in-differences design was applied to compare outcomes before and after PE acquisition to a matched set of non-PE HHAs. Data analyses were performed from June 2025 through May 2026.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcomes included (1) home health use (ie, total number of HHA visits per episode), (2) type of service use (ie, skilled nursing, home health therapy, home health aide, social work), (3) patient quality outcomes (ie, 30-day rehospitalizations, emergency department visits), and (4) HHA financial outcomes (ie, revenue, expenses, and profits).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 165 PE-acquired HHAs, serving 71 610 beneficiaries, and 422 matched for-profit non-PE HHAs, serving 170 066 beneficiaries, were identified. PE acquisition was associated with an absolute decrease of 1.11 HHA visits per episode (95% CI, -1.68 to -0.54 ; relative decrease, 8.3%) and an 11.3% decrease in total net expenses (log coefficient, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.22 to -0.01), while operating margins were 7.9 percentage points higher (95% CI, 5.1-10.7 percentage points). There were no statistically significant changes in net patient revenue, 30-day rehospitalizations, or emergency department visits. Heterogeneity analyses indicated that results were primarily driven by a single, large PE acquisition.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cohort study with a difference-in-differences design, PE ownership of HHAs appeared to reduce service use and was associated with higher operating margins, with no statistically significant changes in patient quality outcomes, suggesting PE's use of cost-containment strategies rather than revenue generation to increase profits. The effects appear to be driven by 1 large acquisition, highlighting the heterogeneity of the impact of PE across HHA deals.

articles.title: Prescription drugs and the risk of road traffic crashes in Bordeaux, France: a study matching emergency department health reports and a pharmaceutical reimbursement registry.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Prescription medications may impair driving ability and increase the risk of road traffic crashes (RTC). This study aimed to estimate the association between prescription medication use and RTC risk among patients attending the adult emergency department of Bordeaux University Hospital, France, assess trends in psychotropic medication use, and estimate the proportion of RTCs attributable to medication exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency department records were linked with the French National Health Data System from 2013 to 2021. The study included 17 296 individuals aged 15 years or older presenting within 24 hours of an RTC. Drivers of motorised vehicles and vulnerable road users were included, whereas passengers were excluded. Acute and chronic effects were assessed using case-crossover and matched case-control designs, respectively. Medication exposure was classified according to the French pictogram-based driving risk classification (levels 0-3). ORs were estimated using conditional and multivariable logistic regression, and population attributable fractions were calculated using national prescription data.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: On the day of the RTC, 32.9% of individuals were exposed to at least one prescription medication. In the case-crossover analysis, level 3 medications were associated with increased RTC risk, particularly anxiolytics, opioids and antidepressants. In the case-control analysis, level 2 medications were associated with increased RTC risk (adjusted OR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17 to 1.38), as were level 3 medications (1.43, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.57). The highest risk was observed for centrally acting muscle relaxants (2.26, 95% CI 1.46 to 3.51). The population attributable fraction for level 2 and 3 medications decreased from 4.5% in 2013 to 3.8% in 2021.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prescription medications with a high driving-risk classification, particularly those acting on the nervous system, significantly increase RTC risk. Despite a slight decline in psychotropic use, a substantial burden of RTCs remains attributable to high-risk medication exposure, highlighting the need for continued public health interventions.

articles.title: Changes in earnings and employment after isolated traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injury.
articles.journal_full: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSES
abstract.text: Following traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries, the functional limitations and prolonged recovery can lead to time away from work, reduced productivity, and long-term economic consequences. This study aimed to assess the impact of isolated, traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries on changes in income and employment among working Canadians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, matched cohort study using linked Canadian health and tax administrative data (2007-2017). We included adults aged 18 to 64 years presenting to emergency departments (excluding Quebec) with isolated upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries. We estimated injury-attributable changes in income and employment using a difference-in-differences approach with linear and probit mixed-effects models, respectively.

abstract.label: MAIN FINDINGS
abstract.text: A total of 3300 cases (mean [SD] age, 37 [11] years; 2200 male [66.7%]) were matched to 2100 controls. Injured individuals experienced an average decline in income of Canadian dollars (CAD) $1718.96 (95% CI, -$2624.80 to -$813.12; p=0.0002) in the first year postinjury and CAD $1830.83 (95% CI, -$2627.61 to -$1034.03; p<0.0001) in the fifth year. Employment status also declined, with a difference of -2.71% points (95% CI, -3.26 to -2.16; p<0.0001) in the first year postinjury and -2.03 points (95% CI, -2.66 to -1.40; p<0.0001) in the fifth year.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries are associated with significant and sustained income loss, as well as modest but persistent declines in employment. These findings highlight the long-term economic burden of nerve injuries and underscore the importance of timely intervention and supportive return-to-work strategies.

articles.title: Combining a Modified Emergency Severity Index Score with Chief Complaints - Validation of a New Allocation Algorithm for Integrated Emergency Centers.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Current health policy reforms in Europe aim to synchronize emergency departments and acute outpatient clinics (AOC)/primary care services through the establishment of Integrated Emergency Centers (IECs). A central challenge of this model is the upstream triage at a central point of assessment (CPA). To date, there is a lack of standardized concepts for a single-stage assessment conducted by emergency-qualified staff that also facilitates cross-sectoral allocation. To address this gap, this study introduces the optimized leading-symptom-weighted modified Emergency Severity Index (L-mESI opt.) triage instrument. This tool aims to safely distribute the clinical workload between emergency departments (EDs) and AOCs by linking a modified emergency severity index (mESI)-omitting vital signs-with the patient's chief complaint (CEDIS).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis of walk-in emergency patients was conducted at two university hospitals in 2024 (training dataset: n = 26,845). Outpatient treatment rates were determined for combinations of chief complaints and mESI categories. These probabilities informed an optimized allocation algorithm (L-mESI opt.) via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and the maximum Youden Index. The model was verified using a separate validation dataset (n = 11,512).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The pretest probability for AOC allocation was identified at 74%. The optimized L-mESI-opt. algorithm correctly allocated 54.2% of patients to the AOC, the ED workload was reduced by 46.9%. Compared with standard ESI-based steering, the L-mESI-opt. significantly improved sensitivity for inpatient care from 54.5% to 69.5% and achieved a negative predictive value of 85.4%. Although 14.6% of AOC-allocated patients required subsequent ED admission ("Upstream") in the validation set, critical outcomes remained minimal (observation unit transfer: 0.3%; mortality: 0.1%). Validation confirmed consistent quality and safety.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: L-mESI opt. model demonstrates the potential to effectively reduce ED workload while maintaining high patient safety in a simulated environment. These results show that its adaptability could allow for broad application in IECs. However, the successful implementation of such an algorithm will likely depend on close spatial and organizational links between EDs and AOCs to manage bilateral patient flow efficiently. Prospective clinical trials are warranted to confirm these findings in real-world settings.

articles.title: Complete Symptom Resolution After Rest in Acute Dizziness: Implications for Selective Magnetic Resonance Imaging Use and Patient Out-of-Pocket Costs in Japan.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: We examined the association between symptom resolution after rest and causative central lesions on initial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and the patient-perspective economic implications of hypothetical MRI omission. Methods: This exploratory, single-center, retrospective observational study included 170 patients with dizziness who underwent MRI between April 2022 and March 2024. Symptoms were reassessed after 10 min of supine rest. Among patients discharged home, MRI-related charges were hypothetically omitted for those with complete resolution, with other care unchanged. Sensitivity analyses examined the impact of hypothetical additional outpatient revisit costs. Results: Causative central lesions were detected in 0 of 90 patients with complete resolution (0.0%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.0-4.0%) and 12 of 80 with residual symptoms (15.0%; 95% CI, 8.0-24.7%; p < 0.001). Among 89 discharged patients, hypothetical MRI omission in 54 (60.7%) reduced estimated initial medical expenditures by JPY 909,300 (22.6%); the median estimated patient-payment reduction was JPY 3552. In sensitivity analyses limited to additional outpatient revisits, estimated reductions remained positive across the principal scenarios but diminished as assumed revisit use increased. Conclusions: Complete symptom resolution was associated with a lower observed proportion of causative central lesions and warrants evaluation as information complementary to established assessment. Hypothetical selective MRI use reduced estimated initial expenditures and patient payments. These exploratory findings do not establish the safety of MRI omission; prospective validation incorporating clinical outcomes and downstream healthcare use is required.

articles.title: Whole blood transfusion in adult patients with traumatic brain injury: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Whole blood (WB) transfusion may improve outcomes in trauma patients compared with component therapy, but evidence in traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains limited. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of WB transfusion in adults with TBI requiring transfusion.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ICTRP for studies published from January 2006 through August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized trials and observational studies using propensity score matching or inverse probability of treatment weighting. Random-effects meta-analysis with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was performed for mortality. Component-specific transfusion requirements were summarized qualitatively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five studies were included in the systematic review, and four studies were included in the mortality meta-analysis. WB transfusion was not clearly associated with lower mortality (RR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.62-1.16; P = 0.19; I2 = 48.3%), with a 95% prediction interval of 0.48-1.49. Sensitivity analyses using alternative effect-size conversion methods, baseline risks, effect measures, and mortality definitions yielded consistent results. In exploratory leave-one-out analyses, pooled RRs ranged from 0.74 to 0.91, with all 95% CIs including 1. Three studies contributed component-specific transfusion data; red blood cells and plasma requirements were generally lower with WB, although this may partly reflect substitution by WB itself. The certainty of evidence was very low.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Current evidence is insufficient to determine whether WB transfusion reduces mortality after TBI because of the limited number of studies, clinical and methodological heterogeneity, risk of bias, and imprecision. Further randomized trials in clearly defined TBI populations are needed.

articles.title: The Expanding Role of Autoinjector Technologies: Redefining Drug Delivery for the 21st Century.

abstract.text: Autoinjectors (AuI) have changed considerably over the past few decades. This review describes their development, from the early spring-loaded antidote injectors built for military use to the connected, software-enabled platforms now entering clinical practice. It compares AuI with conventional syringes, with attention to dose consistency, needle concealment, and the ability of untrained users to inject correctly outside clinical settings. Devices are classified along three dimensions: actuation mechanism (springloaded versus electronic), reusability (single-use versus cartridge-based), and connectivity (mechanical versus smart). The drug classes that shape device design are reviewed, including monoclonal antibodies, GLP-1 receptor agonists, insulin analogues, and emergency antidotes, together with the formulation problems each of them creates. Emergency medicine receives equal weight throughout. Atropine and pralidoxime for nerve agent poisoning, naloxone for opioid overdose and epinephrine for anaphylaxis impose engineering requirements that differ from those of chronic therapy devices. Regulatory frameworks in the European Union (MDR 2017/745; EMA) and the United States (FDA combination product pathway; human factors guidance) are summarised, as is the global market, estimated at USD 10.2 billion in 2025. The review closes with emerging directions: high-volume subcutaneous delivery, reusable and sustainable formats, personalised dosing, 3D-printed designs and automatic multi-injector systems for mass casualty events. Unlike existing reviews, which cover either chronic biologic delivery or single- device subtypes, this article treats chronic self-administration and emergency or CBRN use within one framework. It also introduces the automatic multi-injector concept as an unresolved engineering problem.

articles.title: Pneumocephalus and pneumorrhachis after combined spinal-epidural anesthesia for labor analgesia: a case report.

abstract.text: Pneumocephalus is an extremely rare but potentially life-threatening complication of epidural anesthesia. We report the case of a 31-year-old woman who received combined spinal-epidural anesthesia for labor analgesia at 39 weeks of gestation. During the procedure, in which the loss-of-resistance-to-air (LOR-A) technique was used, approximately 2-3 mL of air was injected into the epidural space. The patient subsequently developed acute neurological deterioration, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5 and flaccid quadriplegia. Emergency head computed tomography showed gas accumulation in the suprasellar and ambient cisterns, and spinal imaging revealed concurrent pneumorrhachis (intraspinal air) at the L2-L3 level. Due to incomplete recovery of consciousness and persistent quadriplegia, the patient underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) once daily for a total of seven sessions. Notably, transient psychotic symptoms developed during the fifth HBOT session. This case highlights that clinicians should consider intracranial pneumocephalus and intraspinal complications whenever a patient shows acute neurological deterioration after an intraspinal procedure. Although HBOT is a feasible option for pneumocephalus, clinicians should recognize that imaging improvement may lag behind or even diverge from clinical recovery, and decisions should therefore be made against the backdrop of repeated clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Baseline cognition accounts for most predictive information on cognitive recovery during rehabilitation after carbon monoxide poisoning.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cognitive change during rehabilitation after carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning may differ from prognosis at acute presentation. We examined whether information recorded in a rehabilitation pathway added predictive information beyond baseline cognition.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort included 200 patients who completed 30 repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) sessions and serial cognitive assessments between January 1, 2018, and January 31, 2026. Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores were assessed before rTMS and after 20 and 30 sessions. A MoCA increase of at least 5 points was the study-defined classification outcome; this threshold has not been validated for CO poisoning. Four exploratory algorithms were evaluated against a baseline-cognition benchmark. Performance was estimated from stratified five-fold out-of-fold predictions, with paired bootstrap comparisons of area under the curve (AUC) and Brier score.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: MMSE increased from 23.73 ± 2.85 to 27.83 ± 2.15 and MoCA from 21.58 ± 3.57 to 27.02 ± 2.78 after 30 sessions (both p < 0.001); 137 patients (68.5%) met the classification criterion. The baseline-cognition-only random forest had an AUC of 0.836 (95% CI 0.758-0.905) and a Brier score of 0.122, compared with 0.860 (95% CI 0.798-0.908) and 0.119 for the expanded model. Neither the paired AUC difference (0.024, 95% CI - 0.013 to 0.064; p = 0.219) nor Brier-score improvement (0.003, 95% CI - 0.008 to 0.014; p = 0.581) was statistically detectable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Baseline cognition dominated prediction of a score-change outcome that is mathematically linked to baseline and constrained by ceiling effects. The additional routine measures and coarse imaging categories available here showed no detectable incremental value. These preliminary findings describe selected rehabilitation completers and require external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Enhancing prognostic evaluation in cardiac amyloidosis: PALS, GLS and functional tests beyond KCCQ.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) often leads to reduced functional abilities, quality of life, and potential psychological repercussions. Several tests assess functional capacity, with the KCCQ score being the most widely used for heart failure symptoms, but it may overly rely on psychological factors. Left atrial (LA) strain indicates left ventricular (LV) diastolic function and filling pressure but doesn't correlate with KCCQ scores. The relationship between other tests and functional capacity or HRQoL (health-related quality of life) in CA remains unexplored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This observational study aimed to assess the correlation between LA strain and LV global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) with functional tests. Furthermore, we aimed to examine their association with NT-proBNP levels and 6MWT in patients affected by CA, encompassing both AL and ATTR subtypes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We enrolled patients with CA during their follow-up visits. They underwent clinical, echocardiographic, functional capacity and quality-of-life assessments, including the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at baseline and after 3-6 months during follow-up visits, while subsequent clinical follow-up was used to ascertain the composite endpoint. The composite endpoint included all-cause mortality, hospitalization or emergency department visit for heart failure, and urgent cardiovascular visits for worsening heart failure symptoms. Deaths were further classified as cardiovascular or non-cardiovascular according to the predefined cause-of-death classification.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 67 patients diagnosed with CA (48 ATTRwt and 19 AL, average age 78 years, 21% female) were included. At baseline, patients had an LVEF of 53 ± 7%, a LVGLS of -13 ± 6% and mean PALS of 13 ± 7%. Global PALS demonstrated a positive correlation with DASI score (p = 0.06) and 6MWT (p = 0.004), and showed an inverse correlation with MLHFQ score (p = 0.005) and NT-proBNP (p = 0.003) while it was not correlated with KCCQ (p = 0.21). GLS demonstrated a positive correlation with NT-proBNP (p = 0.001), Minnesota score (p = 0.01), DASI score (p = 0.017). In contrast, the KCCQ did not correlate with NT-proBNP, PALS, 6MWT, or GLS. 42 patients (62.7%) experienced the composite endpoint. GLS was lower in the event group, PALS was lower, interventricular septal thickness (IVS) was larger, NT-proBNP was greater, and LAVi was higher. Our study showed that LVGLS, PALS, and apical sparing (RELAPS) were associated with the composite clinical endpoint, with LVGLS showing the numerically highest AUC among the evaluated parameters (AUC 0.704 (95% CI: 0.595-0.813) for LVGLS, 0.663 (95% CI: 0.549-0.777) for PALS, and 0.660 (95% CI: 0.545-0.775) for RELAPS).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: LVGLS showed significant associations with functional status and quality-of-life measures and had the numerically highest AUC for the composite clinical endpoint among the evaluated parameters.

articles.title: Bridging pathways after venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in infarct-related cardiogenic shock: a single-center real-world cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock remains highly lethal. We evaluated venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as a time-limited bridging platform rather than as stand-alone rescue support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single center retrospective observational cohort study, we retrospectively screened adults who received venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for infarct-related cardiogenic shock at Linyi People's Hospital from January 2021 to December 2025.
