Standardized anteroposterior and lateral wrist radiographs were reviewed for 6 parameters: radial height, inclination, radiocarpal angle, volar angulation, volar tilt, and ulnar variance, measured twice by a blinded observer (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.92-0.98). Stratification by age and gender used 50 years as a menopause proxy. Statistical analysis included t tests (Bonferroni correction, α = 0.010) and effect sizes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 585 patients, 466 met criteria (mean age, 45 years; 40.6% female). Mean values were 13.4 mm for radial height, 25.4° for inclination, 11.6° for radiocarpal angle, 145.1° for volar angulation, and 17.1° for volar tilt. Radial height was significantly greater in males than in females (P < .001). Ulnar variance was neutral in 69.5%, negative in 17.8%, and positive in 12.7%. Volar angulation declined significantly with age in women, especially post-menopause (P < .01), but not in men.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Distal radius morphology in Israelis aligns with international norms. Age-stratified differences in volar angulation among women over 50, which may reflect menopausal bone remodeling, indicate that both age and sex should be incorporated into individualized assessments. In the management of distal radius fractures in postmenopausal women, baseline volar angulation is approximately 3° lower than in younger women, a factor that may influence reduction targets.

articles.title: Pediatric Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor With Extensive Necrosis: A Case Report.

abstract.text: We describe an unusual presentation of a pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). A 17-year-old previously healthy male presented to the emergency department with altered mental status, lethargy, nausea, vomiting, fever, and tachycardia. Head imaging incidentally demonstrated a large expansile sellar/suprasellar cystic and solid mass displacing the optic chiasm, invading bilaterally into the cavernous sinuses, and encasing the internal carotid arteries. He developed decreased vision of the left eye on hospital day two and underwent urgent endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal resection of the mass. Pathology demonstrated a PitNET with extensive necrosis, lactotroph differentiation, and changes suggestive of superimposed tumoral infection. His postoperative course was complicated by panhypopituitarism, chronic diabetes insipidus, and a cerebrospinal fluid leak managed with lumbar drainage. His presenting symptoms resolved completely, with no tumor recurrence at two-month follow-up. The initial clinical manifestation in this case was suggestive of adrenal crisis secondary to pituitary hypofunction and secondary adrenal insufficiency, attributed to significant tumor compression and pituitary necrosis, and surgical decompression was performed for new visual loss.

articles.title: Spontaneous Heterotopic Pregnancy in a Primigravida: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Heterotopic pregnancy is the coexistence of an intrauterine pregnancy and an ectopic pregnancy. It is uncommon after spontaneous conception and may be overlooked once a normal intrauterine pregnancy has been identified. We report the case of a 33-year-old primigravida at approximately seven weeks of gestation who presented to the emergency department with sudden severe lower abdominal pain radiating to the back. Conception had occurred spontaneously, without assisted reproductive technology. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a viable intrauterine pregnancy together with a separate viable left tubal pregnancy and free intraperitoneal fluid. Initial investigations showed microcytic anemia, with a hemoglobin concentration of 7.6 g/dL and a mean corpuscular volume of 66.6 fL. Laparoscopy demonstrated approximately 150 mL of hemoperitoneum and a macroscopically unruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy with a fimbrial hematoma. A left salpingectomy was performed while preserving the intrauterine pregnancy. Histopathologic examination of the excised tube confirmed chorionic villi. Recovery was uncomplicated, and ultrasonography the following day confirmed continued viability of the intrauterine pregnancy. Subsequent first-trimester follow-up showed appropriate progression. The intrauterine pregnancy continued to term, with cesarean delivery of a live male infant at 39 weeks and four days for breech presentation in labor. This case emphasizes that identification of an intrauterine pregnancy should not end the evaluation of a pregnant patient with significant abdominal pain. Careful assessment of the adnexa remains important even after spontaneous conception.

articles.title: Readying Asia-Pacific health systems for integration of blood-based biomarkers in mild traumatic brain injury assessment: An expert opinion review.

abstract.text: Rapid screening tests incorporating brain biomarkers offer a practical solution to some persistent challenges in acute mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) assessment by functioning as high-negative predictive value rule-out tools for unnecessary computed tomography (CT) scans; however, their implementation is not uniform globally. Emergency physicians and pathologists from across the Asia-Pacific region convened to examine current evidence on diagnostic tests utilizing the biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for acute mTBI. This narrative expert review reflects the discussions and conclusions of the advisory board meeting and is intended to serve as an educational resource for decision makers in the region. As region-specific data are scarce, most data derive from non-Asian and non-Pacific Islander populations. Pivotal mTBI studies conducted in the United States and Europe have demonstrated that the GFAP/UCH-L1 biomarker panel achieves high diagnostic sensitivity (ranging from 95% to 100%) for detecting CT-positive intracranial lesions, and high negative predictive value for ruling out traumatic intracranial injury on head CT, exceeding 99.6% in combined panel testing. A point-of-care GFAP/UCH-L1 whole blood test provides results within 15 minutes, supporting rapid decision-making, and is cleared for use up to 24 hours after injury in adults with suspected mTBI (Glasgow Coma Scale 13-15), extending its utility to assessment settings beyond the emergency department. Although barriers to widespread implementation of biomarker testing persist across the Asia-Pacific region, we are taking steps to close the gap by outlining expert recommendations for incorporating GFAP/UCH-L1 biomarkers into acute care pathways.

articles.title: Dual-Energy Computed Tomography in the Emergency Department for Body Imaging Applications: An Update.

abstract.text: Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) has moved from a niche technique to a routine problem-solving tool in the emergency department. By using the energy-dependent attenuation of different materials, DECT provides material-specific characterization not available in conventional single-energy CT. Low-keV reconstructions, virtual noncontrast, and iodine maps improve the detection of subtle bowel ischemia, occult gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and active vascular extravasation. This article outlines the fundamentals of DECT and highlights its clinical utility in addressing acute abdominopelvic and thoracic emergencies as well as new emerging technologies.

articles.title: Renal Failure Following Traumatic Bladder Rupture: A Case Report.

abstract.text: When the bladder ruptures into the peritoneal cavity, urine rich in creatinine and urea can accumulate freely within the abdomen. The resulting rise in serum creatinine and urea therefore stems from passive reabsorption of these solutes across the peritoneal membrane rather than from an actual decline in kidney function, and the calculated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) returns to normal shortly after the bladder is repaired and the peritoneal cavity washed out. We describe a previously healthy six-year-old girl who developed pseudo-renal failure from an intraperitoneal bladder rupture sustained one day earlier during a fall from standing height. She presented to the emergency department with severe generalized abdominal pain and macroscopic hematuria with preserved diuresis. The examination revealed a patient stable hemodynamically and respiratorily, with ascites and general tenderness without abdominal guarding, the pain being most pronounced in the suprapubic area. Blood tests showed elevated creatinine levels at 61.64 mg/L and a urea level at 2.66 g/L. The abdominal and pelvic CT scan revealed a large amount of ascites, with identification of the distal end of the urinary catheter in the intra-abdominal cavity through a defect in the upper wall of the bladder measuring 9 mm in diameter, and extravasation of contrast medium during the urinary phase. However, the liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys, and ureters appeared normal. Through this observation, we raise awareness of the possibility of bladder rupture in the presence of acute renal failure even without a history of severe trauma.

articles.title: Reassurance or Redundancy: A Retrospective Observational Study of the Clinical Utility of Abdominal Radiographs in an Australian Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Introduction Acute abdominal pain accounts for a significant proportion of emergency department (ED) presentations, and abdominal radiographs or X-rays (AXR) remain among the most frequently performed investigations for this presentation. Although radiographs carry a lower radiation dose than computed tomography (CT), this is offset by comparatively poor diagnostic yield, and CT has been shown to improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical outcomes in acute abdominal pain. The Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) iRefer guidelines define appropriate indications for abdominal radiographs to maximise its clinical utility and are endorsed for use in Australia by the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Radiologists. This study aimed to assess whether abdominal radiograph requests at an Australian tertiary ED met RCR iRefer indications and whether radiograph findings informed management or led to further imaging within the same presentation. Methods This retrospective study reviewed all abdominal radiographs performed at the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital ED between 1 January and 30 June 2025, identified via the Radiology Information System. Adult patients (≥18 years) imaged for acute abdominal pain were included; those imaged to monitor known pathology were excluded. Request-form indications were compared against RCR iRefer guidelines. Clinical notes were reviewed to determine whether radiograph findings directly informed management or whether further imaging was required. Results Of 191 radiographs identified, 162 met inclusion criteria. The mean age was 48.3 years (range 18-99), with an approximately equal sex distribution. Overall, 85.18% (n=138) of requests were iRefer-compliant, with non-compliance (14.82%, n=24) largely attributable to inpatient-initiated and device-position check requests. The leading indications were exclusion of constipation (37.03%) and suspected bowel obstruction or volvulus (29.6%). No acute pathology was identified in 45.06% (n=73) of studies. Constipation and faecal loading were seen in 36.41% (n=59) of studies and bowel obstruction in 7.4% (n=12). Radiograph findings directly informed management in 75.9% (n=123) of cases (79 discharged, 44 admitted). Further imaging was required in 24.10% (n=39): 34 underwent CT, four underwent ultrasound, and one obtained both modalities. This further imaging identified a positive finding in 26 patients (66.6%), while 13 (33.3%) had no defined aetiology. Notably, clinically significant pathologies, including bowel obstruction, new inflammatory bowel disease, and previously undetected foreign bodies, were identified on further imaging in a subset of patients despite an initially negative or non-specific radiograph. Conclusion Abdominal radiography in this centre was largely compliant with the iRefer guidelines, but diagnostic yield was limited, and a meaningful proportion of patients required subsequent cross-sectional imaging, some of which revealed pathology not apparent on the initial radiographs. These findings support closer adherence to core iRefer indications and consideration of more selective first-line abdominal radiograph use, with earlier consideration of CT in patients with a high pre-test probability of significant pathology.

articles.title: Military-Civilian Partnerships in Disaster Management.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) are a strategic necessity for modern medicine. By bridging the gap between military medical providers and local civilian hospitals, these alliances ensure both sectors are prepared for the changing environment of large-scale disasters. MCPs enable a two way transfer of knowledge between military and civilian medical providers and institutions. For civilian providers, MCPs offer access to effective triage and complex casualty management. For military providers, providing clinical repetitions helps maintain skills. The future of MCPs and evolving disaster management is critical for the readiness of medical centers.

articles.title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, or Nuclear-related Injuries in Disaster.
articles.journal_full: The Surgical clinics of North America

abstract.text: In a disaster involving chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) agents, the surgeon must lead the medical response by merging standard trauma protocols with response to specific CBRN agents. This article outlines the management of CBRN-related injuries, integration of Advanced Trauma Life Support and CBRN, and decontamination. The article details the physiologic impact of specific agents, the necessity of rigorous decontamination, and the specialized surgical timelines needed for casualties suffering from combined injuries of CBRN and trauma.

articles.title: Progressive Plantar Foot Pain as a Presentation of Arteriovenous Malformation: A Case Report of Diagnostic Delay.

abstract.text: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) of the foot are rare vascular anomalies that may present with nonspecific symptoms and mimic common emergency department conditions. We report a 26-year-old man with progressive plantar foot pain and swelling who had multiple healthcare encounters before an AVM was diagnosed. Initial evaluation included unremarkable radiographs, treatment for presumed cellulitis, and negative venous duplex ultrasonography for deep venous thrombosis. Persistent and worsening symptoms ultimately prompted targeted ultrasonography, which identified a plantar AVM. On subsequent emergency department presentation for severe pain and inability to bear weight, examination demonstrated a warm, exquisitely tender plantar lesion with pulsatile Doppler flow, and computed tomography angiography confirmed the diagnosis. The patient underwent transarterial embolization with subsequent improvement in pain, swelling, and ambulation. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis in patients with persistent or recurrent symptoms, particularly when clinical features are atypical for common conditions such as cellulitis or when abnormal vascular findings are present.

articles.title: Effect of an Educational Intervention on Lower Limb Pain During the Hajj Mass Gathering: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Lower limb pain is common and disabling from age 50 onwards, yet prevention before predictable episodes of intense ambulatory load has never been tested. We evaluated a pre-departure therapeutic patient education program in pilgrims attending a mass gathering.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A parallel-group randomized controlled trial (1:1) was conducted in two Moroccan vaccination centers: 218 pilgrims aged 50-75 years were enrolled in April 2025 and followed until late June 2025. The intervention group received a therapeutic patient education program, comprising a one-hour group education session plus an unsupervised home-based adapted physical activity program and WhatsApp reminders; controls received none. The primary outcome was lower limb pain on a visual analog scale (0-10) 48 hours after the end of the peak activity period. Analysis was by intention to treat, using linear mixed models, with blinded assessors and analyst.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The primary outcome was available for 216 of 218 participants (mean age: 62.6 years; 147 (67.4%) women). At T2 (48 hours after the end of the peak activity period), lower limb pain was lower in the education group (-1.75 points; 95% CI: -2.40 to -1.09; p<0.001); a smaller difference was already present seven days before departure, and the difference persisted seven days after return. The education group also had less limping (24 (22%) versus 42 (39.3%); p=0.01), less increased analgesic use (33 (30.3%) versus 48 (44.9%); p=0.027), less foot pain (11 (10.1%) versus 24 (22.4%); p=0.01), and better quality of life (+0.059; p=0.021). Low back pain, healthcare use, and falls did not differ.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A pre-departure therapeutic patient education program, evaluated as a whole, produced a statistically significant reduction in lower limb pain in adults aged 50-75 years exposed to several days of intense walking. The point estimate did not reach the 2-point threshold set a priori, so a clinically important benefit can be neither confirmed nor excluded. Predictable episodes of high ambulatory load may offer a practical window for resource-light prevention, which requires confirmation against an active comparator.

articles.title: Post-spinal Aseptic Meningitis Following Cesarean Delivery Presenting as an Acute Febrile Meningeal Syndrome: A Diagnostic Challenge.

abstract.text: Post-spinal aseptic meningitis is a rare complication of neuraxial anesthesia that may be clinically indistinguishable from bacterial meningitis at presentation. We report the case of an 18-year-old primigravida at approximately 38-39 weeks of gestation who underwent emergency cesarean delivery for acute fetal distress under spinal anesthesia with preservative-free hyperbaric bupivacaine and fentanyl. Within hours of the procedure, she developed somnolence followed by fever, confusion, neck stiffness, and photophobia. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed marked neutrophilic pleocytosis and substantial protein elevation with preserved glucose, while Gram staining and cultures remained negative. Empirical antimicrobial therapy was initiated because bacterial meningitis could not initially be excluded. During the subsequent course, the patient developed transient binocular diplopia with limitation of upward gaze. Brain and orbital magnetic resonance imaging showed no explanatory abnormalities. An extensive microbiological investigation, including bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, and viral testing, remained negative. Although herpes simplex virus type 1 was detected from a subsequently appearing perioral lesion, CSF herpes simplex virus polymerase chain reaction was negative. Repeat lumbar puncture on day 10 demonstrated near-complete normalization of CSF findings, and the patient achieved complete neurological recovery, including resolution of diplopia. The close temporal relationship with spinal anesthesia, repeatedly negative microbiological investigations, normal neuroimaging, rapid CSF normalization, and favorable neurological outcome supported the diagnosis of post-spinal aseptic meningitis. This case emphasizes the importance of initially treating suspected post-neuraxial meningitis as a bacterial infection while considering aseptic meningitis when microbiological studies remain negative and the subsequent clinical and biological course supports a noninfectious inflammatory process.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Suspected Radiographically Occult Proximal Femoral Fracture in Adults With Acute Hip Pain: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies.

abstract.text: Radiographically occult proximal femoral fracture is a recognised diagnostic hazard in acute care. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the reference standard but is rarely available at the bedside, and point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has been proposed as an adjunct that may modify clinical suspicion while advanced imaging is arranged. This systematic review aimed to identify and appraise primary studies of clinician-performed hip ultrasound in adults presenting acutely with hip pain and suspected proximal femoral fracture with non-diagnostic or pending radiographs. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and trial registers were searched from inception to 1 September 2026, with citation searching. The review was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 and PRISMA-diagnostic test accuracy (PRISMA-DTA) and was not prospectively registered. Eligible studies were original peer-reviewed diagnostic accuracy studies using B-mode hip ultrasound against MRI, computed tomography (CT) or a composite reference standard; radiography was accepted only to confirm a visible fracture, never to classify a participant as fracture-negative. Two-by-two tables were reconstructed, exact binomial confidence intervals (CIs) were derived, and risk of bias was appraised with the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies, Version 2 (QUADAS-2). Pooling was not performed because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Four prospective studies (389 participants; 186 with proximal femoral fracture) were included. Only two restricted enrolment to radiograph-negative patients and verified all participants with MRI. Observed sensitivity ranged from 0.96 to 1.00, with lower CI bounds of 0.69-0.92. Specificity ranged from 0.65 to 0.99; the lowest values occurred with qualitative capsular signs and the highest with cortical discontinuity or a measured capsular threshold, but these were indirect comparisons confounded by setting, operator, population and reference standard. A hypothetical scenario analysis suggested that the largest study's sensitivity would fall to 0.89 if only 10 fractures had been missed among unverified excluded patients. Every study was at high or unclear risk of bias in at least one QUADAS-2 domain, and fracture-subtype-specific accuracy could not be reconstructed. Hip POCUS showed high observed sensitivity and variable specificity in small, heterogeneous and biased studies; these estimates should not be taken as its true performance in routine emergency practice. The evidence supports POCUS only as an adjunct that may modify suspicion and help prioritise CT or MRI, not as a rule-out test. Adequately powered emergency department studies with blinded emergency-clinician sonographers, prespecified criteria, subtype-specific reporting and universal MRI verification are needed.

articles.title: Rapid Symptom Resolution After Adjunctive Oral Colloidal Silicon Dioxide in a Non-anaphylactic Hazelnut Allergy Reaction: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Acute food allergy reactions that do not fulfil the criteria for anaphylaxis are common in the emergency department and are managed symptomatically, principally with H1 antihistamines. No current recommendation addresses the allergen that remains unabsorbed in the gastrointestinal lumen at the time of presentation. We report a case of a 44-year-old man with childhood-onset hazelnut allergy who presented 30 minutes after inadvertently eating a packaged dessert containing hazelnut, with generalised urticaria, intense pruritus, nausea, vomiting and crampy abdominal pain. He was haemodynamically stable with no respiratory or laryngeal involvement and did not meet diagnostic criteria for anaphylaxis, so adrenaline was not given. Alongside standard care with an intravenous H1 antihistamine and intravenous fluids, a single 3 g oral dose of colloidal silicon dioxide (SiO2), a non-absorbed silica-based enterosorbent, was administered. Fifty minutes later, his gastrointestinal symptoms had resolved and the urticaria was found fading. He was observed for eight hours, developed no biphasic reaction, and was discharged uneventfully. Adjunctive enterosorbent therapy was well tolerated and was followed by rapid improvement. Because an intravenous antihistamine was given concurrently and spontaneous resolution cannot be excluded, no causal role can be attributed to the enterosorbent. The case is reported to draw attention to a mechanistically plausible but untested adjunct, not to advocate its use.

articles.title: Cannabis use Disclosure and Opioid Prescribing at Emergency Department Discharge.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: It is unclear whether documented cannabis use disclosure is independently associated with opioid prescribing practices when patients discharge from the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine associations between cannabis use disclosure and opioid prescribing as well as dose among adults with selected acute painful conditions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational study of adult patients seen in the ED between 2021 and 2023 in a Southern California healthcare system. For patients with multiple ED visits, only the earliest encounter was included in the study. Eligible conditions included major/long-bone fractures, acute low-back/lumbar/sciatic conditions, and selected minor acute musculoskeletal injuries. The primary outcome was an opioid prescription at discharge. Among who were prescribed an opioid, secondary outcomes were total and daily prescribed morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Multivariable models adjusted for demographic, clinical, substance-use, utilization, year, and diagnosis variables.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3159 patients, 507 (16.0%) disclosed cannabis use. Opioids were prescribed to 27.6% of cannabis-disclosing and 31.3% of documented noncannabis patients (absolute difference, -3.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.9 to 0.6). Cannabis disclosure was not associated with discharge opioid prescribing after adjusting for covariates (adjusted odds ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.67-1.11). Among opioid recipients, cannabis disclosure was not associated with total MME (adjusted mean ratio, 1.11; 95% CI, 0.92-1.34) or daily MME (1.07; 95% CI, 0.95-1.21).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Documented cannabis disclosure was not independently associated with opioid prescribing at ED discharge or prescribed opioid dose.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Time to Triage in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Efficient triage in emergency departments (ED) is crucial for timely patient care, as evidence indicates that time to triage could affect treatment outcomes. Sex differences have been observed in different healthcare areas. The objective of this study was to determine whether sex differences exist in a patient's time to triage and the magnitude of any observed differences at presentation to the ED of a Jerusalem hospital.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study used anonymized data from adult ED visits between January 1 to September 30, 2024, at an ED in Jerusalem. Our primary outcome measure was the mean time to triage, defined as the interval between documented patient arrival and the first encounter with a triage nurse. Our secondary outcome measures included the proportion of patients triaged within 15 minutes, stratified by sex, ED division, and Emergency Severity Index (ESI) level.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study analyzed 30,447 adult ED visits over nine months. Mean time to triage was 10.9 minutes for women versus 10.3 minutes for men (absolute difference, 0.6 minutes; P < .001). Women were less likely to be triaged within 15 minutes (75.2% versus 76.9%; absolute difference, 1.7%; P < .001). Median time to triage was 6.0 minutes (interquartile range [IQR]) for men, 1.0-15.0 vs 7.0 minutes (IQR, 1.0-15.0) for women. Among patients with ESI levels 3-5, women had lower odds of triage within 15 minutes (odds ratio [OR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.73-0.84; P < .001), while no significant sex differences were observed for ESI levels 1-2 (OR 1.30; 0.90-1.88; P = .17). Differences were most pronounced in ED triage to the ambulatory care area (absolute difference, 1.8%; OR, 0.95) and minimal in acute care (absolute difference, 0.5%; OR, 0.84), with no significant difference in the shock-trauma unit. Both sexes had similar triage rates within 60 minutes (99.2%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although we found statistically significant sex differences in time to triage, the absolute difference of 0.6 minutes is not clinically meaningful. The near-universal triage within 60 minutes suggests that early triage prioritization differences do not translate into clinically significant delays. Within this ED, triage processes function similarly for men and women. Future research should evaluate downstream processes (eg, time to physician evaluation) to determine aspects of ED care that may demonstrate clinically important sex-based disparities.

articles.title: Machine Learning Versus Traditional Statistical Models for Emergency Department Volume Forecasting.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) crowding harms patient care and strains hospital operations. Forecasting daily patient arrivals can help ED medical directors, department chairs, and hospital administrators plan staffing and bed capacity in advance, rather than reacting after a surge has already occurred. This study compared five computer-based forecasting methods, including three machine learning models (eXtreme gradient boosting [XGBoost], light gradient boosting machine [LGBM], and long short-term memory [LSTM]) and two traditional statistical models (autoregressive integrated moving average [ARIMA] and seasonal ARIMA [SARIMA]), to determine which most accurately predicts ED patient volume seven days in advance, using eight years of daily visit data from an academic freestanding ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study analyzed 3,202 consecutive days of daily patient volume (March 27, 2017, to December 31, 2025) from an academic freestanding ED with approximately 31,102 annual visits. Each model used the preceding 365 days of data to forecast the subsequent 7 days, repeated across the study period to reflect the weekly cycle by which most EDs plan staffing. Our primary measure of accuracy was mean absolute error (MAE), defined as the average number of patients per day by which a forecast missed the actual volume. Secondary measures included root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), the coefficient of determination (R2, a score from 0 to 1 reflecting how well predictions tracked actual day-to-day volume), and the percentage of forecasts accurate within 5, 10, 15, and 20 patients, thresholds selected for their relevance to staffing decisions. The best-performing model on initial metrics, XGBoost, served as the reference model for statistical comparison using the Diebold-Mariano (DM) test, which determines whether an observed difference in accuracy between two models is statistically meaningful or attributable to chance.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 453 rolling weekly forecast windows, SARIMA, XGBoost, and LGBM demonstrated the lowest absolute errors and best forecasting of patient volume, with MAE values of 9.60 (95% CI, 9.29-9.91), 9.61 (95% CI, 9.31-9.91), and 9.64 (95% CI, 9.33-9.94) patients/day, respectively; these three models therefore missed the actual daily patient count by approximately 9 to 10 patients, on average. Models ARIMA and LSTM were less accurate, with mean MAE values of 10.54 (95% CI, 10.21-10.87) and 12.01 (95% CI, 11.63-12.39) patients per day. Relative to the XGBoost reference (MAPE 13.82%), ARIMA (MAPE 14.93%) and LSTM (MAPE 17.27%) showed a marked decrease in predictive accuracy. For operational planning, the top-performing models (SARIMA, XGBoost, and LGBM) correctly predicted daily volume within a margin of 20 patients in 90.3% to 90.6% of instances, while LSTM performed less well and reached this threshold in only 83.3% of forecasts. Statistical testing confirmed these differences were unlikely due to chance, with XGBoost significantly outperforming ARIMA (DM = -6.09, P < .001) and LSTM (DM = -6.96, P < .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Models SARIMA, XGBoost, and LGBM performed comparably well, and all three would provide reliable, operationally useful forecasts for ED staffing and resource allocation decisions. A traditional statistical method, SARIMA, which is simpler and less resource-intensive to implement, performed as well as the newer machine learning methods evaluated in this study. This finding suggests that hospitals do not necessarily need to invest in more complex artificial intelligence tools to obtain accurate ED volume forecasts.

articles.title: Emergency Medicine Reimagined: Development of the Patient Rights Index for Emergency Medicine.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency medicine has evolved beyond episodic acute care to encompass a growing range of clinical, social, and system-level responsibilities. This scholarly perspective proposes the Patient Rights Index in Emergency Medicine (PRI-ED), a conceptual framework designed to organize recurring domains through which emergency departments promote access to care, patient safety, relief of suffering, autonomy, and dignity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The PRI-ED was developed through iterative domain generation informed by clinical observation, professional experience, and targeted review of peer-reviewed literature, policy analyses, and professional organizational reports. No primary data collection, systematic review, formal consensus process, or empirical validation was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 12 domains that represent recurring clinical, operational, and system-level challenges encountered in emergency medicine. These domains were organized within a standardized framework linking domain-specific objectives, intervention strategies, measurable indicators, and relevant policy or funding mechanisms.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The PRI-ED is a proposed conceptual framework for organizing and evaluating domains in which emergency medicine intersects with access, safety, autonomy, relief of suffering, and dignity. The framework is intended to inform future implementation, evaluation, and policy discussion and requires feasibility testing and outcome validation before effectiveness can be determined.

articles.title: Cannabis Use versus Cigarette Smoking in Emergency Department Patients: Comparative Outcomes.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Cannabis is one of the most commonly used psychoactive substances worldwide, with 20% of adults in the U.S. reporting using cannabis at least once in the past year. Nicotine dependence is reported in 9% to 10% of adults in the U.S. This study aims to investigate the relationship between cannabis use and cigarette smoking on mortality, cardiovascular outcomes, suicide, cancer of the lung and bronchus, and reactive airway disease in emergency department (ED) patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, propensity score-matched study used the TriNetX database to analyze records of 120,689,106 patients from 69 healthcare organizations in the U.S. between 2005 and 2022. The first cohort consisted of adult patients and was grouped based on diagnosis of cannabis-related disorders (CRD) within five years before or one month after an ED visit. The second cohort consisted of adult patients with a diagnosis of "nicotine dependence, cigarettes" within five years before to one month after an ED visit. The outcomes evaluated were all-cause mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, suicide, cancer of the lung and bronchus, and reactive airway disease (asthma/chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [COPD]) within three years after the ED visit. Patients who previously experienced these outcomes or belonged to both cohorts were excluded from the study. We performed 1:1 greedy nearest-neighbor propensity score matching for demographics and seven preexisting conditions associated with mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 1,682,117 patients identified with ED visits and CRD or cigarette smoking. After propensity score matching, there were a total of 651,232 adult patients with CRD (n = 325,616) or cigarette smoking (n = 325,616) within five years prior or one month after an ED visit. Patients with CRD were associated with a significantly higher mortality rate (2.35% vs 2.16%; relative risk [RR] 1.09; 95% CI, 1.05-1.12; P < .001), stroke (0.45% vs 0.28%; RR 1.59; 95% CI, 1.47-1.73; P < .001), myocardial infarction (0.53% vs 0.35%; RR 1.51; 95% CI, 1.40-1.63; P < .001) and suicide (0.62% vs 0.35%; RR 1.77; 95% CI, 1.65-1.90; P < .001) within 3-years of the ED visit compared to patients smoking cigarettes. Individuals with CRD were associated with a significantly lower rate of lung and bronchus cancer (0.16% vs 0.31%; RR 0.53; 95% CI, 0.48-0.59; P < .001) and reactive airway disease; asthma (6.30% vs 7.37%; RR 0.86; 95% CI, 0.84-0.87; P < .001) and COPD (1.65% vs 3.05%; RR 0.54; 95% CI, 0.52-0.56; P < .001) than those with cigarette smoking.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: We found that cannabis use was associated with higher risks of mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, and suicide for ED patients when compared to cigarette smoking. Cannabis-related disorder was associated with lower rates of reactive airway disease and lung and bronchus cancer when compared to those with cigarette smoking.

articles.title: Emergency Department Operational Measures Associated with EMS Redirection Activation and Duration.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency medical services (EMS) redirection is used to manage emergency department (ED) strain, but whether it reflects operational conditions is unclear. We compared associations of prespecified ED operational measures, including visit volume, patient flow times, admissions, boarding, and left-early measures, with redirection activation and total daily redirection minutes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective study at a single urban tertiary care center over 392 consecutive days from April 7, 2021 through May 3, 2022. Redirection temporarily routed ambulances away from the study hospital and was activated centrally by EMS. New York City's 9-1-1 system included about 500 ambulance units and over 60 hospitals. The primary outcome was activation, defined as any redirection during a calendar day. The secondary outcome was total redirection minutes among days with redirection. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated activation, and negative binomial regression evaluated duration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Redirection occurred on 250 of 392 days (63.8%). Median daily duration was 47 minutes (interquartile range 23-78). Higher ED visit volume was associated with activation (odds ratio [OR] 1.14 per 10 patients; 95% CI, 1.02-1.27). Longer door-to-room time was associated with activation (OR 1.42 per 5 min; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and duration (incidence rate ratio 1.022 per min; 95% CI, 1.002-1.042). Boarding time and admission count were not associated with either outcome.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Emergency department visit volume was associated with activation but not duration, while door-to-room time was associated with both. Evaluating redirection as a single outcome may obscure differences between activation and cumulative duration.

articles.title: Trends in Mushroom Exposures Reported to the Florida Poison Information Center Network, 2014-2024.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Toxic mushroom exposures can occur through multiple mechanisms, including consumption as a delicacy, foraging, and use for psychoactive properties. Recent evidence suggests that psylocibin mushroom use is increasing in the United States. However, information on trends in mushroom poisonings in Florida is limited. This study aims to characterize trends in psychoactive and nonpsychoactive mushroom exposures reported to the Florida Poison Information Center Network (FPICN) over an 11-year period.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a retrospective review of all mushroom exposures reported to the FPICN between 2014 to 2024. Our primary outcome was to evaluate the annual trend of psychoactive and nonpsychoactive exposures. Secondary outcomes included identifying patient demographics, exposure intent, clinical effects, and medical outcomes associated with each exposure type. Psychoactive mushrooms were defined as belonging to groups 2 (muscimol), 4 (muscarine and histamine), and 6 (psilocybin and psilocin) in the National Poison Data System coding manual. We performed statistical analyses using chi-square and Mann-Whitney tests, and joinpoint regression models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 2,995 mushroom exposures were reported. Psychoactive mushrooms comprised 15.6% (n = 467) of exposures and were more likely to involve males (72.5%, P < .001) and intentional ingestions (80.9%, P < .001). Joinpoint regression analysis showed that from 2014 to 2018, the rate of psychoactive mushroom exposures did not change significantly (annual percentage change [APC] = -1.5%; 95% CI, -35.9% to 19.3%; P = .88). In contrast, from 2018 through 2024, exposure rates increased significantly by an average of 34.4% per year (APC = 34.4%; 95% CI, 27.0%-60.4%, P < .001). These trends were standardized to overall poison center call volume. There were three deaths: a 67-year-old male (intentional-suspected suicide); an 81-year-old male (unintentional); and a 44-year-old female (unintentional), all involving mushrooms of unknown category.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Psychoactive mushroom exposures in Florida have increased substantially since 2018, particularly among adolescents and adults, and were more commonly associated with intentional use. These findings may reflect changing cultural attitudes and increased accessibility. Further research is needed to better understand the evolving landscape associated with psychoactive mushroom use.

articles.title: Impact of an Overnight Stay in the Emergency Department Hallway on Admitted Geriatric Patients.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Patients frequently board overnight in the emergency department (ED) while awaiting medical admission, sometimes in hallway care spaces. Prior literature suggests that timing of boarding may matter; a single overnight stay in the ED may be associated with increased mortality and adverse events, especially for older adults. Given the deliriogenic ED environment, these effects may be magnified in the hallway. However, little is known about the effects of prolonged hallway stays. We evaluated whether an overnight stay in the ED hallway, compared to an ED room, was associated with increased delirium and adverse outcomes for geriatric patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective multisite cohort database study of patients aged 65 years and older admitted to a general medicine service January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2023, who spent an entire night (midnight to 8 am) in the ED prior to admission. We compared those who spent the entire night in the ED hallway with those who were in ED rooms. Our primary outcome was a composite outcome for incident delirium and severe agitation (defined by the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Rev, code for delirium, positive nursing screen, use of parenteral antipsychotics, and/or physical restraints, since delirium was not routinely screened for at these sites). Secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay (LOS), inpatient and 30-day mortality, and 30-day ED revisit and readmission. We implemented mixed-effect regression models and adjusted for confounders.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 8,576 patients met inclusion criteria, including 1,231 patients (14%) in the hallway group. Overall, 847 patients (9.9%) developed incident delirium and severe agitation: 160 (13%) of the hallway group and 687 (9%) of the non-hallway group. An overnight stay in the ED hallway was not associated with delirium and severe agitation (OR, 1.06, 95% CI, 0.58-1.94; P = .84), but increased ED LOS was independently associated with delirium and severe agitation (OR, 1.01; 95% CI, 1.0-1.01 per hour; P = .01). There was no association between an overnight stay in the hallway and secondary outcomes except increased hospital LOS (OR 1.01, 95% CI, 1.00-1.01 per hour; P = .01).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: An overnight in the ED hallway care space was not associated with increased delirium and severe agitation for geriatric patients, but prolonged ED LOS was associated with this outcome. Hospital systems should consider prioritizing geriatric patients for expedited transfer from the ED to inpatient units, and prospective research with consistent delirium screening is needed to rigorously evaluate the safety of hallway care for older adults.

articles.title: Cardioversion of Stable Atrial Fibrillation in the Emergency Department: Electrical Versus Pharmacological in the Era of Overcrowding.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading cause of emergency department (ED) visits. Optimizing the management of recent-onset AF is crucial to reduce length of stay (LOS) and improve ED resource utilization.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate differences in ED LOS between pharmacological (PC) and electrical cardioversion (ECV) in patients with recent-onset AF. Secondarily, to compare adverse event profiles of propofol versus midazolam.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, single-center observational study analyzed ED patients with stable recent-onset AF who underwent PC or ECV. Patients with hemodynamic instability, combined sedatives, or concurrent clinical issues prolonging ED LOS were excluded from the primary analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 575 patients were analyzed: ECV-propofol (n = 201), ECV-midazolam (n = 27), flecainide (n = 312), propafenone (n = 15), and amiodarone (n = 20). The overall ECV approach demonstrated a significantly shorter median LOS (114 min) compared with overall PC (130 min) (p = 0.006). In a propensity score matched analysis (excluding crossover pathways), ECV-propofol showed a numerically shorter LOS (106 min) versus flecainide (118 min), though not statistically significant (p = 0.086). However, a secondary analysis of 121 crossover patients revealed that pharmacological failures drove massive ED delays (median LOS 317 min). Adverse events in the ECV-propofol cohort (5%) were strictly minor and self-limited.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: While uncomplicated PC with flecainide approaches the temporal efficiency of propofol sedation, the overall ECV strategy is associated with a significantly shorter ED LOS. By adopting structured propofol-based ECV protocols, emergency physicians can effectively avoid the enormous time delays that occur when initial pharmacological interventions fail.

articles.title: Assessment of Combined Food and Nutrition Insecurity Screening in the Emergency Department: A Brief Report.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) food insecurity (FI) screening traditionally identifies insufficient access to food but does not account for diet quality. We evaluated the incremental yield of adding a nutrition insecurity (NI) screener to routine FI screening.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center observational study enrolled adult ED patients from April-September 2025. Participants completed the 2-item Hunger Vital Sign and a 1-item NI screener. Our primary measure was incremental yield of NI screening beyond FI screening, defined by the number of NI-positive/FI-negative patients identified. Secondary outcome measures included FI and NI prevalence, screening concordance, and number needed to screen. Screening fidelity was supported through structured training of research associates and standardized phrasing.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,120 patients, 13.6% (95% CI, 11.6-15.7%) screened positive for FI and 11.4% (95% CI, 9.7-13.5%) for NI. While the measures showed substantial agreement (κ = 0.67), they identified significantly different populations (McNemar P = .01). Specifically, 28 patients (2.5%) screened NI-positive but FI-negative, yielding an 18.4% relative increase in identified at-risk patients compared to only screening for FI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Dual screening identified a clinically relevant NI-only subgroup whose diet-quality barriers were not captured by FI screening alone. Incorporating NI into ED social needs assessments may improve identification of diet-related risk and guide medically tailored interventions.

articles.title: Cumulative Weighted-Average Acuity Level: A Novel Clinician-Level Metric to Detect Emergency Department Surge Conditions in Real Time.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) surge events, defined as the episodic clustering of high-acuity patients that transiently overwhelms available clinician capacity, are associated with delays in care and potential patient harm. Existing crowding metrics do not quantify real-time clinician-level workload. This paper describes the development and preliminary feasibility evaluation of a novel acuity-weighted metric-the cumulative weighted-average acuity level (CWAAL)-to detect physician-level surge conditions in real time.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multiphase observational feasibility study was conducted at two rural community EDs. The CWAAL is defined as the sum of weighted acuity scores for all active patients under a single clinician's management: it incorporates a feasibility threshold derived by combinatorial enumeration. The primary outcome was door-to-doctor time (DDT); secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and CWAAL distribution. The DDT comparisons at Hospital B (n = 4 surge events per condition) used the Mann-Whitney U test. All data were obtained from the practice of a single physician.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We evaluated a single emergency physician across 354 patients on 10 study dates at two rural community EDs, tracking 11 surge events and one proof of concept. A CWAAL feasibility threshold of ≤ 12 (±1)-equivalent to four simultaneous Level 3 patients (~120 minute demand within a 60-minute window)-emerged consistently across both sites. At Hospital B, surge-period DDTs were substantially lower with advanced practice clinician (APC) coverage than without (median, 31.5 minutes [interquartile range {IQR}, 24.7-38.0] vs 107.7 minutes [IQR, 85.7-133.5]); Mann-Whitney U = 0, P = .03, 2-tailed exact; rank-biserial r = 1.0), with complete distributional separation across eight surge events. All APC-supported events occurred at CWAAL ≤ 12; all unsupported events at CWAAL > 12. A proof-of-concept application on May 28, 2024, demonstrated operational feasibility; supplemental staffing reduced the physician's weighted acuity burden by 31 points and normalized DDT and LOS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this development cohort, the physician reached functional care capacity at cumulative weighted average acuity level = 12 (four simultaneous Level 3 patients; ~120 minutes demand within a 60-minute physician-hour). Complete separation of APC-supported and unsupported outcomes across eight events supports this novel acuity-weighted metric as a meaningful operational signal. Formal prospective validation across independent datasets is required before generalizing.

articles.title: Prehospital Videolaryngoscope Availability and Use in Belgium: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey.

abstract.text: Background Emergency endotracheal intubation (ETI) outside the operating room is challenging because of patient-, operator-, situational-, and logistical factors. Videolaryngoscopy is an alternative to direct laryngoscopy and can reduce ETI failure and complications. In Belgium, no published data are available regarding the availability of videolaryngoscopes (VL) for prehospital ETI by mobile intensive care unit (MICU) crews. The main objective of this survey was to estimate VL availability among responding Belgian MICUs. The secondary objective was to identify physicians' prehospital VL use patterns as well as to explore factors potentially associated with VL use. Methods This cross-sectional survey used two online questionnaires distributed to all Belgian MICUs. Questionnaire A was intended for the heads of department and collected information about VL availability and local protocols. Questionnaire B was intended for all MICU physicians and assessed their frequency of VL use and their reasons for using it or not using it. Results Of the 96 eligible Belgian MICUs, 35 heads of department responded to Questionnaire A (36.5%) and 32/35 (91.4%; 95% confidence interval, CI, 77.6-97.0%) reported VL availability. Out of the 115 MICU physicians who responded to Questionnaire B, 81 reported using a VL (70.4%; 95% CI, 61.5-78.0%). Among respondents with access to a VL, reported use differed by region of practice (p = 0.012); odds of VL use were lower in the Brussels-Capital Region (odds ratio 0.123; 95% CI, 0.028-0.546). More than half of the VL users reported using it for less than 10% of their ETIs, and only 6.2% used it as a first-choice device. The most frequently reported indication for VL use was failed ETI with a direct laryngoscope (81.5%). Conclusion VL availability was high among responding Belgian MICUs. However, the reported prehospital VL use was infrequent.

articles.title: Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension and Diagnostic Pitfalls in Severe Polycystic Liver Disease: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Polycystic liver disease (PLD) is a rare inherited disorder characterized by progressive hepatic cyst formation and, in severe cases, noncirrhotic portal hypertension. Although ascites is a recognized complication of advanced PLD, diagnostic frameworks for ascites and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) were developed primarily in patients with cirrhosis and may not be directly applicable to noncirrhotic disease. We present the case of a 60-year-old male with severe PLD who developed recurrent massive ascites following hepatic cyst surgery. Imaging demonstrated extensive hepatic cystic disease with portal vein compression and hepatic venous outflow obstruction. Ascitic fluid demonstrated a high serum-ascites albumin gradient and elevated protein, consistent with noncirrhotic portal hypertension. Despite a polymorphonuclear leukocyte (PMN) count of only 16 cells/mm³, broth-only growth of three oropharyngeal commensal organisms prompted treatment for presumed SBP; subsequent negative cultures and the absence of neutrocytic ascites favored contamination or transient bacterascites. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) facilitated rapid identification of free fluid despite extensive cystic hepatic anatomy and enabled safe paracentesis by identifying appropriate fluid pockets. This case highlights the importance of contextualizing cirrhosis-derived diagnostic frameworks when evaluating noncirrhotic ascites and demonstrates the value of POCUS as a practical diagnostic and procedural tool in patients with severe PLD.

articles.title: Perforated Viscus as a Rare Complication of Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) is a potentially serious complication of in vitro fertilization (IVF). While abdominal pain and intra-abdominal free fluid are common manifestations of OHSS, intestinal perforation occurring in patients with OHSS is extremely uncommon. We report a case of small bowel perforation following IVF in a patient with features of OHSS, presenting a diagnostic challenge due to overlapping clinical features. A 39-year-old female patient presented with severe lower abdominal pain 5 days after undergoing ovum retrieval for IVF. The patient's past surgical history included sleeve gastrectomy nine years prior and gastric bypass surgery two years earlier, without postoperative complications during the preceding two years. On presentation, she was tachycardic with lower abdominal tenderness and guarding. Laboratory investigations showed leukocytosis and a rising CRP. Bedside ultrasound showed intra-abdominal free fluid. IV contrast-enhanced CT raised concerns for gastrointestinal perforation and demonstrated features suggestive of OHSS. The patient rapidly deteriorated. Given the concern for gastrointestinal perforation and evolving septic shock, the patient underwent diagnostic laparoscopy, which was converted to a midline laparotomy. A 1.5-cm perforation at the jejunal omega loop near the gastrojejunal anastomosis was identified and primarily repaired with abdominal washout. During the laparotomy, a bulky uterus and enlarged ovaries with large ovarian cysts were also noted. The postoperative course was complicated by pulmonary embolism and septic shock; however, she improved with appropriate management and was discharged home in good condition. This case emphasizes that although OHSS commonly presents with abdominal pain and ascites following IVF, physicians should consider bowel perforation as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with severe abdominal pain, particularly in patients with previous bariatric surgery.

articles.title: Fatal Edwardsiella tarda Sepsis With Acute Enlargement of Multiple Abdominal Organs on Noncontrast Computed Tomography.

abstract.text: Edwardsiella tarda (E. tarda) is a Gram-negative bacillus found in freshwater and brackish environments. Human infection is relatively uncommon and most frequently presents as gastroenteritis, although invasive infections may occur. We report a fatal case of E. tarda sepsis with the acute enlargement of multiple abdominal organs on computed tomography (CT). A 63-year-old woman with pancreatogenic diabetes mellitus and a history of surgery for malignancies presented with abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, and headache. She developed severe lactic acidosis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and multiorgan dysfunction. Noncontrast CT demonstrated the enlargement of both kidneys and adrenal glands, as well as the liver, compared with CT images obtained approximately six months earlier; given normal renal function eight days before admission and the fulminant course, these changes were highly likely to have developed acutely. The kidneys were diffusely enlarged, with increased attenuation of the perirenal and renal sinus fat. No definite abscess, gas within the organs, or focal fluid collection was identified. Despite intensive care, multiorgan failure progressed rapidly. Blood cultures yielded E. tarda, and subsequent history-taking revealed that the patient had consumed eel on the day of symptom onset. She died of multiorgan failure on day 9 after symptom onset. This case suggests that severe E. tarda sepsis may be associated with the diffuse enlargement of multiple abdominal organs even in the absence of a localized abscess or gas-forming lesion. When no apparent focal source of infection is identified despite a clinical presentation suggestive of severe infection, prompt blood culture testing and comparison with previous imaging studies are important, and a history of seafood or freshwater fish consumption, including eel, may provide a supportive clue.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Early ED Return Among Patients Discharged After Treatment for Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS) is a frequent cause of emergency department (ED) visits, and some patients return soon after discharge. Identifying factors associated with short-term ED return may inform targeted interventions. Our primary objective was to identify factors associated with 72-hour ED return and 30-day hospital admission among patients discharged after treatment for AWS.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective review of 318 ED encounters for AWS at a single academic medical center from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2023. Demographic, psychiatric, housing, insurance, and discharge pharmacology variables were collected. We evaluated ED pharmacologic treatment strategy and discharge taper prescriptions. The primary outcome measure was 72-hour ED return, and the secondary outcome measure was hospital admission within 30 days. We compared groups using chi-square, Shapiro-Wilk, Fisher exact, and Mann-Whitney U tests. Variables with significant univariate associations were included in multivariable logistic regression, and results were reported as odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fourteen patients (4.4%) returned within 72 hours, and 32 patients (10.1%) were admitted within 30 days. On multivariable logistic regression, schizophrenia (OR, 8.59; 95% CI, 2.07-35.61), Medicaid insurance (OR, 4.43; 95% CI, 1.39-14.14), and anxiety (OR, 3.53; 95% CI, 1.10-11.39) were independently associated with increased 72-hour ED return. Homelessness was independently associated with higher 30-day admission (OR, 3.19; 95% CI, 1.26-8.07). Discharge tapers were not associated with either outcome.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among patients discharged after ED treatment for alcohol withdrawal syndrome, Medicaid insurance, anxiety, schizophrenia, and homelessness were associated with short-term return or admission. These findings suggest that social and psychiatric vulnerability may contribute to short-term ED reuse following discharge after AWS treatment. These results highlight opportunities to strengthen follow-up pathways and to address social determinants of health. Larger, multicenter studies are needed to clarify whether these associations are specific to AWS or reflect broader patterns of ED utilization.

articles.title: Prehospital Buprenorphine: A National Cross-Sectional Analysis.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Initiation of buprenorphine reduces mortality in people with opioid use disorder. However, patients who decline hospital transport after overdose may not be connected to treatment. To augment treatment engagement, prehospital buprenorphine pilot programs began in 2019. To date, few studies have looked at these programs nationally. Our objective was to evaluate national prehospital buprenorphine usage.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional evaluation of emergency medical service (EMS) encounters involving prehospital buprenorphine administration using the 2020-2023 National EMS Information System Public Release Research datasets. Our primary outcome was trends in prehospital buprenorphine usage. Quarterly rates of prehospital buprenorphine were evaluated using joinpoint regression to identify inflection points. The secondary outcome was patient demographics and encounter characteristics, which were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of all EMS encounters with patient contact in the dataset (N = 167,221,959), there were 2,180 encounters where buprenorphine was administered (62% male [n = 1,349], mean age 37 years, standard deviation [SD] 10), with a significant increase per year (2020: n = 33; 2023: n = 1,574). Approximately half (52%; n = 1,125) of prehospital buprenorphine administrations occurred during 9-1-1 responses. Most encounters occurred in the South Atlantic region (4 administrations/100,000 encounters) and urban areas (72%; n = 1,572). Nearly all EMS crews were advanced life support (ALS) level of care (paramedic: 53% [n = 1,155]; ALS-community paramedic: 46% [n = 1,008]). Initial dosages of administered buprenorphine were 8 milligrams (mg) (45%; n = 973), 16 mg (36%; n = 786), or 24 mg (7%; n = 160). Most patients (80%; n = 1,746) had documented improvement with only four (0.2%) worse after administration. Few 9-1-1 encounters (16%; n = 180) resulted in hospital transport by EMS. Only 7% (n = 82) of 9-1-1 prehospital buprenorphine encounters had documented naloxone administration prior to buprenorphine dosing. There was a significant increase in number of buprenorphine administrations in quarter 2 of 2022 (slope increase of 54 administrations [95% CI, 20-89] per quarter versus 1 administration [95% CI, -1 to +3] per quarter from 2020-2022 quarter 1).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Rates of prehospital buprenorphine have increased significantly between 2020 and 2023. Buprenorphine administration largely resulted in documentation of improvement in patient condition. With continued high rates of opioid-related deaths, prehospital buprenorphine may be considered by EMS agencies to prevent deaths from subsequent opioid use and connect patients to treatment.

articles.title: Pediatric Thoracic Imaging Emergency: Practical Approach for Daily Practice.

abstract.text: Imaging of thoracic emergencies in children is crucial for early diagnosis, guiding treatment, and avoiding severe complications. Radiography, ultrasound, and computed tomography are the most common modalities in emergency imaging. Radiologists should be familiar with the appropriate choice of imaging modality and the radiologic characteristics of serious conditions that can present acutely in the pediatric emergency room. This article discusses a practical overview of the major pediatric thoracic emergencies, including pulmonary infections, airway abnormalities, neoplasms, air leaks, traumatic injuries, and foreign bodies. An up-to-date review of key imaging findings is provided, with emphasis on features that are unique to children.

articles.title: Increasing Emergency Department Burden of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Injuries: A National 10-Year Analysis of Mechanisms and Severity Predictors, 2015-2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) is a rapidly growing grappling-based combat sport, but emergency department (ED) surveillance and sport-specific mechanism classification are limited.

abstract.label: HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: We hypothesized that BJJ-related ED visits have grown disproportionately compared with overall martial arts ED presentations and that sport-specific mechanisms predict nonroutine disposition.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Descriptive epidemiology study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS), 2015-2024. BJJ cases were identified from product code 3257, which corresponds to martial arts equipment and activity-related injuries, followed by a 2-reviewer narrative review. Trends were analyzed using survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression. An 11-category force vector mechanism taxonomy was developed from narratives. Pre- versus post-COVID eras were compared with false discovery rate correction. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of nonroutine disposition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 7618 martial arts ED visits, 1448 (19.0%) were BJJ related (58,170 weighted national cases). Annual BJJ volume rose nearly 5-fold (incidence rate ratio, 1.148/year; 95% CI, 1.090-1.209; P < .001) while total martial arts volume remained stable; BJJ's share climbed from 7.3% to 27.7%. The cohort was 78.0% male (mean age 25.7 ± 12.3 years); pediatric patients (≤17 years) comprised 29.5%. Strain/sprain (23.2%), fracture (15.5%), and contusion/abrasion (9.3%) predominated. The taxonomy classified 69.8% of cases into 8 defined categories, led by direct impact (21.8%), joint torque (16.4%), and fall (11.2%), with the remaining 30.2% indeterminate; the era profile was stable after multiplicity correction. Four independent predictors of nonroutine disposition emerged: internal injury (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 20.62; 95% CI, 7.55-56.26), neck compression (aOR, 5.26; 95% CI, 1.84-14.98), fracture (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 1.30-10.90), and age (aOR, 1.50 per decade; 95% CI, 1.18-1.90); optimism-corrected C-statistic = 0.748.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our study showed that BJJ-related ED presentations are rising rapidly while the injury profile remains stable; because denominators are unavailable, these are presentation counts rather than a measured change in per-capita injury risk. The injury taxonomy and disposition model further identified predictors of injury patterns and ED disposition. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective, exposure-denominated validation.

articles.title: Impact of portable point-of-care ultrasound on clinical decision-making and referrals in general practice: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in general practice, but evidence on its impact on clinical decision-making when performed with portable devices remains limited. Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Cross-sectional observational study conducted over 12 months in a primary care centre in Barcelona, Spain. Three general practitioners with accredited training performed POCUS examinations using portable devices in 108 patients. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥15 years requiring clinical ultrasound. Clinical management plans were documented before and after POCUS using same questionnaire. Changes in decision-making and referral patterns were analysed using McNemar's test. Reporting followed the STROBE statement for cross-sectional studies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: POCUS changed clinical decision-making in 66.7% of cases. Intended referrals to secondary care decreased from 44.4% to 25.0% (absolute risk reduction 19.4%, 95% CI 8.4-30.5%, relative risk reduction 44%). Musculoskeletal examinations represented 73.1% of cases, with management modified in 63.3%. All seven patients with suspected deep vein thrombosis were managed without hospital referral. Referrals for conventional radiology ultrasound decreased from 32.4% to 12.0%, while GP-performed invasive procedures (infiltrations) increased from 0.9% to 18.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Portable POCUS substantially influences clinical decision-making and reduces secondary care referrals in general practice. Further research is needed, especially longitudinal studies, to evaluate whether these changes translate into improved health outcomes for patients.

articles.title: The use of real-time CPR quality feedback prompts during in-hospital cardiac arrest in medical intensive care: uptake and barriers, a single-center cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: High-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) improves survival after in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA). Real-time audio and visual CPR quality feedback may improve CPR quality, but real-world use and uptake are incompletely understood. We evaluated awareness, use, and barriers to defibrillator-integrated CPR feedback among Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) clinicians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used a cross-sectional study design. An anonymous REDCap survey was distributed to nurses, advanced practice providers (APPs), and physicians across three adult MICUs at a single urban academic medical center in February 2024. Respondents reported usual IHCA roles (chest compressor, code leader, CPR coach), familiarity with the Zoll R Series defibrillator's visual and audio feedback functions, use of feedback during real IHCA events, and role-specific perceived barriers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-nine clinicians responded of the 413 invited, 54% by nurses and 43% by physicians. 94% reported involvement in an IHCA during the past year and 92% had received defibrillator training. Awareness of visual and audio feedback functions was 57% and 72%, respectively. Among those aware, 10% often or always looked at the screen for visual feedback while performing chest compressions, 37% while leading a code, and 57% as CPR coach. Audio feedback use was higher 46%, 58%, 50%. Reported barriers during IHCA events included screen placement, reliance on others to monitor visual feedback, and difficulty hearing auditory feedback.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this single-center survey, uptake of integrated CPR feedback during IHCA was incomplete despite near-universal training, and barriers varied by role during IHCA.

articles.title: Anatomic Ulnar Collateral Ligament Repair With Internal Brace and Palmaris Longus Graft Using a Suture Bridge Construct.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) and lateral collateral ligament (LCL) injuries of the elbow are common in athletes, particularly those involved in overhead sports. Traditional repair techniques may not always provide optimal long-term outcomes, necessitating the development of advanced reconstruction methods. Over the years, techniques such as the Modified Jobe and Docking Methods have been refined to improve graft fixation and reduce complications. Emerging strategies, such as suture augmentation and internal bracing, have demonstrated potential to enhance biomechanical stability and facilitate early rehabilitation.

abstract.label: INDICATIONS
abstract.text: UCL/LCL reconstruction techniques, including those that utilize joint-spanning and/or internal brace augmentation, are indicated in cases where joint instability and dysfunction cannot be adequately addressed via traditional reconstruction or primary ligament repair alone.

abstract.label: TECHNIQUE DESCRIPTION
abstract.text: In the first step, the native UCL is repaired with a running, locking 2-0 FiberWire suture and reinforced with a spanning-suture bridge using linked, knotless suture anchors integrated into a spanning-suture construct. Next, the UCL reconstruction is performed using palmaris longus autograft passed through ulnar tunnels and docked into a humeral socket, with final graft tensioning to complete the reconstruction.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In our experience, UCL reconstruction with an internal brace yields superior functional outcomes, including improved time-zero biomechanics and overall reconstruction outcomes, particularly in younger, high-demand athletes.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Evolution of UCL reconstruction techniques has led to improved surgical outcomes and patient recovery. While traditional methods, such as the Jobe and docking techniques, remain widely used, advancements such as suture augmentation and internal bracing offer promising enhancements in biomechanical stability and clinical efficacy. As research continues to validate these approaches, their integration into clinical practice may further optimize ligament reconstruction strategies, particularly in high-performance athletes requiring rapid return to play.

abstract.label: PATIENT CONSENT DISCLOSURE STATEMENT
abstract.text: The author(s) attests that consent has been obtained from any patient(s) appearing in this publication. If the individual may be identifiable, the author(s) has included a statement of release or other written form of approval from the patient(s) with this submission for publication.

articles.title: Bathrooms as a Patient Safety Blind Spot in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review and Nursing Practice Framework.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) bathrooms preserve privacy and dignity but interrupt direct observation. Risks described across clinical publications and professional guidance include falls, unrecognized deterioration, overdose, hazardous ingestion, infection, inaccessible environments, and unmet elimination needs. This review integrated those risks and translated them into a nursing practice framework.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: For the structured narrative review, PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL Plus, and Scopus were searched on July 30, 2026, without date, language, age, or publication-type filters. Backward and forward citation chasing and a targeted search for professional documents supplemented database searching. Publications were categorized by ED relevance and synthesized thematically. Professional guidance was analyzed separately.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 659 records, 248 duplicates were removed and 311 records were screened. Of the 53 reports sought, 12 were not retrieved, 41 were assessed in full text, and 40 were included; citation chasing evaluated 15 candidates and added 3, yielding 43 publications/reports. Direct or contextual ED evidence was provided by 32 publications, and 11 were transferable. The synthesis identified 6 domains: falls and deterioration; fundamental care, continence, and dignity; overdose, self-injection, hazardous ingestion, and surveillance; infection and equipment; accessibility and design; and privacy and clinical use. Evidence was heterogeneous and largely descriptive, qualitative, quality-improvement, or case-based.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The ED bathroom should be managed as a clinical space rather than an environmental afterthought. This review proposes the original Assess-Assist-Observe-Respond-Document framework, which connects individualized risk assessment, proactive assistance, proportionate surveillance, rapid response, and reassessment. Local validation is required before implementation.

articles.title: Critical Care Catalyst: The Impact of Trauma Nurse Leads on Mortality, Patient Outcomes, and Throughput.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Trauma is the leading cause of years of life lost in the United States.
