Dedicated trauma nurse leaders (TNLs) coordinate resuscitation and streamline care, but data evaluating their clinical impact at level I trauma centers are limited. We evaluated the association between a newly implemented dedicated TNL program and patient outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, preimplementation and postimplementation observational study at an urban level I trauma center compared adult tier 1 and tier 2 trauma activations from the pre-TNL period (January 1, 2017, through April 30, 2020) with the post-TNL period (May 1, 2020, through December 31, 2023; 8 dedicated TNLs). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality (including hospice discharges). Secondary outcomes included time to initial computed tomography (CT), time to operating room, emergency department length of stay (LOS), hospital LOS, and ventilator days. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for Injury Severity Score (ISS), demographics, payor status, frailty, and activation acuity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 9112 activations included (pre-TNL, n = 2943; post-TNL, n = 6169), crude in-hospital mortality was unchanged overall (3.53% vs 3.55%; P = .97), but crude mortality decreased significantly among high-severity cohorts: ISS greater than 15 (20.1% vs 12.6%; P < .001), ISS greater than 24 (25.8% to 15.7%; P < .001), and emergent laparotomy (22.2% to 18.5%; P < .001). Median time to CT decreased from 34.48 to 29.64 minutes (P < .001), and mean hospital LOS decreased from 5.57 to 4.93 days (P = .018). After multivariable adjustment, TNL implementation was independently associated with a 36% reduction in odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio = 0.64; 95% CI, 0.48-0.84; P = .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Implementation of a dedicated TNL program was independently associated with significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality, driven primarily by survival gains in severely injured patients, faster time to initial diagnostic CT, and reduced hospital length of stay.

articles.title: Time to Antibiotic Administration in the Treatment of Sepsis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines recommend antimicrobial therapy within 1 hour for probable septic shock, while the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) mandates a 3-hour window. Current literature presents conflicting evidence on whether these universal time thresholds yield a definitive survival benefit. This study aims to evaluate the real-world impact of delayed antibiotic administration on patient mortality and length of stay (LOS).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted analyzing 62 153 adult encounters with severe sepsis or septic shock at emergency departments (EDs) between December 31, 2023, and December 31, 2025. Time to first antibiotic was categorized into 5 intervals (<1, 1-3, 4-12, 13-24, >24 hours). The primary outcome, in-hospital mortality, was analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. The secondary outcome, LOS, was analyzed among survivors using a gamma generalized linear model to calculate adjusted mean ratios (aMR).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort was clinically complex, with 63.5% of patients demonstrating a high Elixhauser comorbidity score (≥ 4). Only 2.8% of patients received antibiotics within the first hour. Mortality odds were significantly higher for patients receiving antibiotics after 24 hours compared to the less than 1 hour baseline (odds ratio = 1.52, 95% confidence interval: 1.18-1.95, P = .001). No statistically significant mortality difference was observed for the 1-3, 4-12, and 13-24 hour intervals relative to baseline. However, delayed administration increased LOS incrementally, with a 9% longer stay for the 13-24 hour group (adjusted means ratio [aMR] = 1.09, P = .003) and a 56% longer stay for the >24 hour group (aMR = 1.56, P < .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Achieving a less than 1-hour door-to-antibiotic time is operationally challenging. Delays up to 24 hours did not significantly increase mortality risk compared to immediate administration, though administering antibiotics before 13 hours offered modest improvements in hospital LOS.

articles.title: A Nurse-Driven Escalation in Trauma Team Activation Reduces Mortality of Injured Patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: There is a dearth of literature examining the clinical outcomes of injured patients who experience physiological deterioration in the emergency department (ED). At our trauma center, injured patients who develop hemodynamic, respiratory, or mental status instability after arrival are retriaged and upgraded to a full trauma team activation (fTA). The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical outcomes of patients with fTA based on prehospital signs and symptoms (initial) versus upgraded fTA patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study of injured patients presenting to a tertiary trauma center between June 1, 2022, and June 30, 2024. The study facility is a state-designated level I trauma center, an American College of Surgeons (ACS)-verified level II trauma center with a catchment area of 17 800 square miles, serving a population of 3.1 million in the central, southeastern region of the United States. The primary exposure was retriage with an upgrade in patient status to fTA. Bivariate analyses with Wilcoxon rank sum, Chi-square, and Fischer's exact tests were used, where appropriate. Binary logistic regression analyses were applied, adjusting for fTA status, Elixhauser comorbidity index (ECI), payer type, race, and sex, to determine if upgraded fTA status was independently associated with injured patient mortality, high-intensity time-sensitive (HITS) interventions, and discharge disposition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1538 fTA occurred during the study period with 66 patients (4.3%) upgraded to fTA after hospital arrival. In-hospital mortality or hospice discharge was less common among upgraded fTA patients compared to initial fTA patients (9.1% vs 19.7%; P = .032). After adjusting for ECI, payer type, race, sex, and trauma activation group, patients initially activated as fTA had 2.64 times higher odds of mortality or hospice discharge compared with patients upgraded to fTA (OR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.10-6.30; P=.029). Within the HITS subcategories, upgraded fTA patients were more likely to receive blood transfusion (63.6% vs 40.8%; P <.001) and less likely to receive mechanical ventilation (24.2%; vs 38.5% P = .020). Upgraded fTA status was not associated with patient discharge disposition.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Injured patients in the ED who develop signs and symptoms consistent with severe injury benefit from retriage and nurse-driven upgrades to fTA status. A hospital safety culture empowers bedside nurses to act on patients' physiologic changes, resulting in the rapid marshalling of health care resources for life-saving interventions.

articles.title: Emergency Room Nurses' Perceptions of Transformational Leadership and Its Role in Their Well-Being: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency room (ER) nurses work under conditions frequently associated with burnout, emotional exhaustion, and turnover intention. Leadership behavior is one of the few workplace conditions that can be modified without additional capital investment, and transformational leadership (TL) has been examined predominantly through cross-sectional survey designs. How ER nurses themselves describe these leadership behaviors and what they attribute to them remains poorly documented in Saudi public hospitals.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To describe ER nurses' perceptions of their nurse managers' TL behaviors and how these behaviors were perceived by the participants to shape their emotional and psychological well-being.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This qualitative descriptive study used non-probability convenience sampling to recruit eight frontline registered nurses from an ER in Saudi Arabia, each with at least six months of ER experience. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews of 45-60 minutes were audio recorded and transcribed verbatim. The analysis followed Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis using a deductive coding strategy; NVivo 14 supported the data management. Two researchers independently coded the data and resolved discrepancies by consensus.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three main themes emerged from the data analysis: (1) clinical credibility and professional security, (2) individualized consideration and personal advocacy, and (3) empowerment and intellectual stimulation. The participants described managers' visible clinical presence during crises, bedside teaching, personal advocacy during family emergencies, recognition, and invitations to contribute to workflow decisions as conditions they connected to feeling calmer, safer, and more willing to remain in their ER.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The participants perceived clinically credible, personally attentive, and intellectually engaging leadership as supporting their well-being while also describing clear limits to what leadership behavior alone could offset. The findings are descriptive and self-reported at one point in time; no causal or mediating relationship is claimed.

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on the emergency diagnosis and treatment of acute exacerbation of asthma (2026)].
articles.journal: Zhonghua Wei Zhong Bing Ji Jiu Yi Xue
articles.journal_full: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
authors: Emergency Physicians Branch Of The Chinese Medical Doctor A
Working Group Of The Chinese Expert Consensus On The Emergency Diagnosis And Treatment Of Acute Exacerbation Of Asthma

abstract.text: Asthma is a heterogeneous disease with complex etiologies and predisposing factors. Its pathogenesis involves the interaction between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors. Chronic airway inflammation, including type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation, is a central feature and contributes to reversible airflow limitation and airway remodeling. Acute asthma exacerbations involve the sudden onset or worsening of wheezing, dyspnea, cough, or chest tightness, accompanied by reduced expiratory airflow and often by expiratory wheezes on auscultation. Exacerbations are commonly triggered by allergens, irritants, or infections and require urgent treatment. The Emergency Physicians Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association convened a panel of experts in emergency medicine, respiratory medicine, critical care medicine, and general practice. The panel developed the Chinese expert consensus on the emergency diagnosis and treatment of acute exacerbation of asthma (2026) using a modified Delphi method, based on current evidence and emergency care practices in China. The consensus addresses 13 clinical issues related to emergency diagnosis and treatment of acute asthma exacerbations, and recommendations are proposed accordingly. Topics include identification and management of triggers; urgent assessment and initial treatment following first medical contact; ancillary investigations; recognition of life-threatening features, severity assessment, and management according to severity; assessment of inflammatory phenotypes; identification of risk factors for asthma-related death; respiratory support; nebulized drug administration; commonly used emergency medications; the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation; and pre-discharge management. The consensus strives to make the diagnosis and treatment process simple and clear, providing practical guidance for emergency and primary care, aiming to standardize the diagnosis and treatment of acute asthma exacerbations and achieve a seamless connection with specialist diagnosis, treatment, and management.

articles.title: The effects of common emergency call system applications in pre-hospital emergency medical services from a lean management perspective: The case of Ordu province, Turkiye.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of a centralized Common Emergency Call Center (CECC) system on prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) efficiency through the lens of Lean Management principles.

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: This retrospective, longitudinal study analyzed secondary data from Ordu province, Turkey, comparing a 36 months pre-CECC period (2018-2020) with a 48 months post-CECC period (2021-2024). The dataset comprised 2,346,774 calls and 721,897 cases. Key performance indicators, selected as proxies for lean waste (communication, time, transport), were compared using independent samples t-tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Following CECC implementation, significant improvements were observed (p<0.001). The call-per-incident ratio, a proxy for communication waste, decreased by 49.0% (from 4.63 to 2.36). Time-based waste was reduced, with respond time of ambulance teams falling by 36.9% and ambulance mobilization time by 23.7%. Transportation waste, measured by distance per incident, decreased by 15.1%. On-time arrival rates improved significantly in both urban (93.9% to 98.4%) and rural (82.2% to 89.2%) areas. These gains were achieved without a statistically significant increase in the patient load coefficient.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The centralized CECC system, acting as a structural lean intervention, significantly reduced operational waste and improved efficiency in prehospital EMS. This centralized CECC model offers a scalable blueprint for health systems seeking to enhance emergency care delivery.

articles.title: Return to Play and Performance After Operative Repair of Scapholunate Interosseous Ligament Tears in National Basketball Association Athletes.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The rate of scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) injuries in National Basketball Association (NBA) players continues to increase. There is a paucity of data regarding return-to-play (RTP) rates and performance metrics after sustaining SLIL injuries in these athletes.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To determine the rate of RTP and performance outcomes in NBA players following a SLIL tear.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Case series; Level of evidence, 4.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review was conducted in January 2024 using the Pro Sports Transactions database of NBA injury notifications to identify isolated SLIL ligament injuries in NBA athletes between the 1956-1957 and 2022-2023 seasons. Confirmed injuries were matched with healthy controls based on similar career trajectories, and demographic, injury-related, and performance data were collected. Statistical analyses compared performance up to 2 seasons pre- and postinjury and assessed differences between the injury and control cohorts. Paired t tests were used to compare parametric performance data, and Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank tests were used for nonparametric data. Unpaired t tests were used to evaluate differences in means between injury and control cohorts, while Mann-Whitney U tests were used to compare medians for nonparametric data. Shapiro-Wilk testing was used to determine normality for all continuous variables before analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 863 wrist injury reports identified, 18 NBA athletes with confirmed SLIL tears met the inclusion criteria, alongside 18 matched healthy controls. The injury cohort had a significantly higher body mass index than controls. After surgical repair, 94.4% of injured athletes returned to play within an average of 6.2 months, with a significant reduction in points per game during their first season back (14.99 to 13.29 after; P = .0433) and a decrease in games played in their second season postinjury.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our study showed that NBA athletes have a high rate of return after sustaining and undergoing surgery for repair of a torn SLIL. Players may experience an initial decrease in playing time and performance; however, these variables returned to baseline by season 2 postsurgery. NBA players who tear their SLIL and undergo surgical fixation are expected to make a full recovery and return to play at their previous level of performance.

articles.title: Outcomes of Primary and Revision UCLR: Return to Play, Performance, and Role Adaptation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction (UCLR) is a common procedure among Major League Baseball (MLB) pitchers, but the effects of revision UCLR on performance and career longevity remain unclear.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To compare return-to-play (RTP) and return-to-level (RTL) rates, performance metrics, and role transitions between pitchers undergoing primary and revision UCLR.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Cohort study; Level of evidence, 3.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 177 MLB pitchers who underwent primary or revision UCLR between 2015 and 2021 were included. Performance metrics, including fastball velocity, spin rate, fastball usage, fielding independent pitching, and pitch movement, were analyzed up to 3 years postreconstruction (PRY1-PRY3). Role transitions between starter and reliever positions were also evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: RTP (P = .046) and RTL (P = .039) rates were significantly lower after revision UCLR. After stratification by pitcher role, revision starters demonstrated greater increases in fastball usage (P = .014) and horizontal break (P = .031) at PRY3, whereas no significant differences were observed among relievers. Revision UCLR remained independently associated with lower RTL, but not with RTP, after multivariable analyses. Starter-to-reliever transitions were common after surgery, with no significant between-group difference.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study underscores the importance of recognizing role changes and reduced recovery success in revision cases, as well as the need for tailored strategies to support long-term performance and durability.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-driven advancements in radiation biodosimetry.
articles.journal: Mutat Res Genet Toxicol Environ Mutagen
articles.journal_full: Mutation research. Genetic toxicology and environmental mutagenesis

abstract.text: Radiation dose estimation is fundamental to the effective management of radiological emergencies, where prompt and accurate assessment is critical for medical intervention. Conventional biodosimetry methods, including the dicentric chromosome assay (DCA), premature chromosome condensation (PCC), γ-H2AX foci detection, cytokinesis-block micronucleus (CBMN) assay, and fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH) translocation analysis, remain important approaches for biological dose estimation. However, their conventional implementation can involve labour-intensive sample preparation and manual or semi-automated analysis, require specialised expertise, and have limited scalability for mass-casualty events. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), offer considerable potential to enhance biodosimetry through automated image analysis, multimodal data integration, and accelerated dose assessment. DL approaches, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), enable high-throughput image analysis and automated identification of radiation-induced cytogenetic damage. Furthermore, integrating explainable AI (XAI) approaches may improve model transparency, interpretability, and confidence in clinical applications. This review examines current advances, challenges, and prospects of AI in radiation biodosimetry, highlighting its potential to support rapid, accurate, reproducible, and scalable dose assessment in radiological emergencies.

articles.title: Emergency Department Management of Traumatic Pneumothorax and Hemothorax.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Thoracic trauma is commonly encountered in the emergency department, often with severe injuries including pneumothorax and hemothorax. This article reviews the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and emergency management of pleural injuries, emphasizing rapid recognition and intervention of tension physiology and massive hemothorax in unstable patients. It reviews and compares imaging modalities for diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making. Management has shifted from routine large-bore chest tubes toward selective observation and smaller drainage devices in carefully chosen patients. The article also addresses ventilated patients, procedural complications, tube malfunction, retained hemothorax, persistent air leak, antibiotic prophylaxis, secure tube placement, and disposition planning.

articles.title: Pharmacology in Emergency Trauma Management.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Pharmacotherapy is an important aspect of management of the acutely injured trauma patient to address symptoms, to facilitate evaluation and emergent interventions, as well as to manage the physiology present in trauma patients. Important pharmacologic categories include analgesia, sedation, rapid sequence intubation, antibiotics, management of hemorrhage, addressing intracranial pressure and vasopressors. Consideration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes in the critical trauma patient as well as knowledge of benefits and risks across this range of pharmacotherapies can optimize patient management.

articles.title: Emergency Department Management of Geriatric Trauma and Falls.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma in older adults is a growing public health challenge due to age-related physiologic changes, frailty, comorbidities, and reduced reserve, which increase morbidity and mortality after injury. Falls are the leading cause of trauma, while motor vehicle crashes are the second most cause of injury-related death. Frailty is a stronger predictor of outcomes than age alone and guides evaluation and disposition. Older adults are at increased risk of traumatic brain injury, hip fractures, rib fractures, spinal injuries, and elder abuse. Liberal use of computed tomography imaging, comprehensive geriatric assessment, multidisciplinary care, and geriatric-specific trauma pathways improve outcomes and care quality.

articles.title: Nerve Blocks for Traumatic Injuries.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks are important for modern, opioid-sparing trauma care. Proficiency in select, high-yield blocks can provide rapid targeted analgesia and improve clinical outcomes. For example, in a patient with multiple rib fractures, performing an erector spinae or serratus anterior block can alleviate chest wall pain and improve respiratory function. Similarly, a fascia iliaca block in an elderly patient with a hip fracture minimizes pain while also reducing the risk of delirium. Safety requires precise needle visualization and proper anesthetic dosing. Standardizing workflows with dedicated carts and documentation templates promotes efficiency. This approach delivers effective pain managment while maintaining the speed and safety necessary in emergency settings.

articles.title: Spinal Cord Injury.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: The emergency physician plays a key role in detecting initial and evolving injury by correctly restricting spinal motion and using imaging criteria to diagnose unstable fractures and compressive bleeding within the spinal canal. The ED physician must also focus on stabilizing the polytrauma patient and begin blood pressure treatment after ruling out other traumatic causes of hypotension. Most importantly, the emergency physician must lead a team approach, communicating early with consultant trauma surgeons, spine surgeons, and intensive care unit providers to prevent delays in critical early decompression and stabilization surgery or transfers to appropriate trauma centers.

articles.title: Resuscitation of the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: This article provides a practical overview of modern trauma resuscitation for emergency clinicians. It emphasizes early recognition of shock, timely hemorrhage control, and activation of massive transfusion protocols. Guidance is provided on fluid resuscitation, permissive hypotension, airway management, and treatment of agitation in critically ill trauma patients. Personalized management of trauma-induced coagulopathy using viscoelastic testing, along with monitoring biomarkers such as lactate and base deficit, is highlighted. The importance of effective team coordination, leadership, and rapid decision-making to improve outcomes in high-acuity trauma care is emphasized.

articles.title: From backbone to bedside: Nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding spinal cord injury care.
articles.journal_full: The Southern African journal of critical care : the official journal of the Critical Care Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Spinal cord injury (SCI) represents one of the most severe forms of central nervous system damage and has profound effects on the physical, psychological and social wellbeing of affected individuals. Patients with SCI are particularly vulnerable to secondary complications such as pressure ulcers, deep vein thrombosis and urinary tract infections. Nurses play a pivotal role in the prevention and management of these complications.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate nurses' knowledge and attitudes before and after implementation of a digital educational application focused on the care of patients with SCI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, two-phase study was conducted between January 2023 and July 2024. During the first phase (January - May 2023), 86 nurses employed in the intensive care unit (ICU), emergency department and rehabilitation centre completed a structured 21-item questionnaire assessing baseline knowledge and attitudes. During the second phase (May - July 2024), the same nurses were reassessed using the same questionnaire following a digital educational intervention. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The findings demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in nurses' knowledge and attitudes following the intervention. Notable improvements were observed in areas related to complication prevention, the use of assistive devices, caregiver education, nutrition, bowel management and remaining informed about updates in patient care. Statistically significant correlations were identified between improvement and both department of employment and level of education. Nurses working in the ICU showed the greatest improvement (phase 1 v. phase 2: 3.1 v. 4.1), while nurses with postgraduate education also demonstrated statistically significant improvement (p=0.007).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The digital educational application was effective in enhancing nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding the care of patients with SCI. Continuous education, particularly within specialised clinical settings, is essential for optimising patient outcomes and maintaining high standards of care.

abstract.label: CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY
abstract.text: This study evaluated nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding spinal cord injury (SCI) care across intensive care, emergency and rehabilitation settings, and tested whether a low-cost, custom-built digital educational application could improve these outcomes. The intervention was associated with significant improvements in knowledge and attitudes, particularly around complication prevention, caregiver education and psychosocial support, with the largest gains seen among ICU nurses and those with postgraduate qualifications. These findings support digital training tools as an accessible way to strengthen nursing capacity for SCI care, especially where structured in-person continuing education is difficult to sustain.

articles.title: Auricular Battlefield Acupressure: A Promising Non-Pharmacologic Therapy for Pain in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Assess the utility of Battlefield Acupuncture (BFA) protocol with beads (BFA-B) to treat pain in the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective chart review was performed for patients who received BFA-B in an inner city ED from 2019-2020.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-one charts were reviewed.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Eleven Pediatrics: The median age 13 years (range 8-19), 55% female, 91% of Hispanic.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Twenty Adults: The median age 39 years (range 21-73); 70% female, 40% Hispanic, 15% Not Hispanic or Latino, 45% unknown race/ethnicity.Pain locations as follows.For pediatric patients: Headache (7), abdomen (2), musculoskeletal (2).For adult patients: headache (8), abdomen (3), musculoskeletal (7), chest (3), flank (1), facial or eye (1), and not specified (1) Some patients had multiple pain locations.The Verbal Pain Scores 0-10 Scale was used. Combined pediatric and adult groups -Mean pre-acupressure pain score: 7.55 ± 2.01 SD.Mean post-acupressure pain score: 3.37 ± 2.53 SD.Mean change of pain score: 4.18 ± 2.38 SD (p < 0.001). Median time to lowest pain score: 32 min (range 3-146 min). No adverse events were noted.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Battlefield acupressure with beads may provide pain relief for adult and pediatric patients who present to the ED with various pain syndromes. Further investigation is warranted.

articles.title: Abdominopelvic Imaging Emergency in Children: A Comprehensive Update and Review.

abstract.text: Abdominopelvic emergencies are one of the most common causes of pediatric emergency department visits, frequently resulting in urgent surgical management. Because conditions such as midgut, volvulus and torsion are time-sensitive, accurate and timely diagnosis is essential and imaging evaluation plays a crucial role. Following abdominal radiograph, ultrasound remains the preferred next imaging modality in most conditions to avoid radiation, even more so with the introduction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound. Advancements in computed tomography and MRI continue to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient safety. This article provides an up-to-date review of current imaging protocols and imaging characteristics of pediatric abdominopelvic emergency conditions.

articles.title: A narrative review of airway changes after prolonged use of supraglottic airway devices: Molecular mechanisms, pathophysiology, and preventive strategies.

abstract.text: There has been an exponential increase in the use of supraglottic airway devices (SGAs) to provide a secure airway without tracheal intubation. They are widely used for many elective surgeries, rescue ventilation after failed intubation, and have been widely recommended for prehospital care. However, its use for extended periods when endotracheal intubation is not feasible may lead to tongue engorgement, mucosal injury, nerve palsy, and subsequent difficult intubation. This narrative review aims to synthesize current evidence on difficult airways and airway-related complications following prolonged use of SGA placement. Here we describe plausible mechanisms, including inflammatory and ischemic pathways, and discuss the severity patterns, risk factors, and preventive/management strategies of a possible difficult airway after prolonged use of SGA in perioperative and intensive care unit settings. Preventive strategies across concentric petals, highlighting correct SGA device and its size selection, minimal cuff inflation in devices that have a cuff, continuous monitoring of cuff pressure, early replacement with an endotracheal tube, appropriate head positioning, device replacement, humidification, and sedation. Implementing these measures can minimize the complications as well as the risk of a difficult airway after prolonged SGA use. Literature on this topic is difficult to find, and definitive recommendations need research, which should prioritize standardization and robust study designs, which may help guide practice. Mechanistic and translational research work should explore pressure-ischemia and inflammatory pathways to facilitate device design improvements and evidence-based protocols for monitoring, timing of exchange to a definitive airway, and safe removal strategies.

articles.title: Mass Religious Gathering-Associated Nationwide Salmonella Outbreak in South Korea, 2025.

abstract.text: A foodborne outbreak associated with a mass religious gathering occurred in South Korea on August 30, 2025. A retrospective cohort investigation was conducted among 1,677 participants. The attack rate of clinical cases was 48.7% (816/1,677), and 36 laboratory-confirmed Salmonella Typhimurium infections with an identical PFGE pattern were identified. Consumption of a pre-packaged meal was strongly associated with illness (relative risk, 17.69; 95% confidence interval, 7.53-41.57). Epidemiologic findings supported a common-source outbreak. Prolonged storage at ambient temperature was a likely contributing factor. These findings emphasize the importance of food safety management and coordinated response systems in mass gathering settings.

articles.title: Opening the Door to Sunrise: A Pediatric Integrative Chinese Medicine Approach to War-Related Trauma and Resilience.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Armed conflict exposes children to trauma and continuous threat, leading to high rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression, and somatic complaints. Following the October 7, 2023, attacks and subsequent multi-front conflict in Israel, demand for mental health services increased substantially, highlighting the need for scalable supportive interventions. Pediatric complementary and integrative medicine (CIM), including Chinese medicine (CM) and mind-body approaches, may provide adjunctive tools for addressing trauma-related symptoms and promoting resilience in war-exposed children.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To respond to the rising need for CIM treatment for pediatric emotional distress, addressing both emotional and somatic manifestations of trauma and supporting resilience and post-traumatic recovery.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A protocol, integrating principles of CM Five-Element theory with various pediatric CIM modalities, was developed during the acute phase of the conflict.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The protocol was initially implemented in the emergency department of Barzilai Medical Center, a hospital located near the Israeli-Gaza border, for children presenting with acute stress reactions and later disseminated to practitioners across Israel.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The Five-Element theory-based framework enables practitioners to address trauma-related emotional and somatic manifestations through targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring regulation, stability, and adaptive functioning.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Five-Element model may provide a structured approach for addressing trauma-related symptoms in war-exposed children and may support resilience and recovery when conventional mental health services are limited. Additional studies are required to explore the generalizability of this model in varied international settings where children are challenged by war-related concerns.

articles.title: Barriers and Enablers of Trauma Triage Tool Implementation in Ireland: A Qualitative Study of First Responders.

abstract.text: The trauma triage tools play an important role in assisting first responders in deciding who needs to be taken to specialist trauma services urgently. However, time pressure, limited training, resource problems, and clinical judgment are factors that hinder the use of these tools in prehospital care. This qualitative study considers the factors that can hinder and facilitate the use of the Health Service Executive Trauma Triage Tool amid the evolving trauma system in Ireland. The study examines a range of individual, organizational, and system-level factors that influence the adoption of the tool among first responders and senior managers using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). In order to capture the participants' lived experiences and professional perspectives, a descriptive phenomenological design is used. Semi-structured interviews and, more so focus groups with a maximum of 30 Dublin Fire Brigade paramedics, advanced paramedics, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and managers who participate in trauma response or management are being conducted. Interviews are conducted online or in person and are 45-60 minutes in duration. All audio recordings will be verbatim transcribed, verified, and analyzed using framework analysis with NVivo. Inductive and deductive coding will be employed, and themes will be related to CFIR domains. The study should aim to identify practical barriers to implementing the trauma triage tool, including training needs, resource limitations, communication difficulties, and reluctance to change, as well as enablers such as leadership, interagency collaboration, and clear implementation processes. Findings will contribute to future trauma triage implementation strategies in Ireland.

articles.title: Management of the Anticoagulated Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: The management of anticoagulated trauma patients is an increasingly common, high-risk challenge driven by an aging population and expanding use of oral anticoagulants, particularly direct oral anticoagulants. Up to 4% to 7% of trauma patients are present on preinjury anticoagulation, facing higher rates of hemorrhagic complications, morbidity, and mortality. This article reviews a systematic approach spanning epidemiology, emergency department (ED) evaluation, and the primary and secondary surveys, emphasizing rapid identification of anticoagulant use and liberal computed tomography (CT) imaging. It details agent-specific laboratory assessment, transfusion principles, and tailored reversal strategies.

articles.title: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Emergency Chest Imaging.

abstract.text: The high-volume, fast-paced, and high-stakes nature of emergency department (ED) imaging poses substantial challenges to the interpreting radiologist. This article lays an inside-to-outside framework for approaching cardiothoracic findings in ED patients from the heart and vasculature (often the most urgent findings and diagnoses) through the bones with an overview of acute cardiothoracic imaging findings and their potential pitfalls.

articles.title: Trends and demographic predictors of cefdinir use for common bacterial infections in children enrolled in Medicaid, 2016-2023.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To determine trends and predictors of cefdinir use for common pediatric infections in the United States.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study, 2016-2023.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: U.S. outpatient encounters (ambulatory, emergency department, urgent care) included in the Medicaid MarketScan database.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Children aged 0-18 years diagnosed with bacterial rhinosinusitis, pharyngitis, urinary tract infection (UTI), acute otitis media (AOM), or community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We assessed cefdinir prescription rates by diagnosis and year, comparing to other commonly administered antibiotics. We used logistic regression to identify demographic predictors of cefdinir use.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 7,346,547 encounters, most common diagnoses were AOM (36.9%) and bacterial pharyngitis (36.2%). Patients were predominantly non-Hispanic White (53.0%), 1-5 years-old (41.1%), and seen in ambulatory settings (75.3%). Cefdinir was prescribed in 10.4% of encounters, ranking among the top prescribed antibiotics. After an initial increase, use declined post-2020 to 7.6%. In children 1-18 years-old, younger age was uniformly associated with higher odds of cefdinir prescription across all diagnoses. This pattern was inconsistent among infants <1 years-old across diagnoses but persisted for UTI, with ORs of 9.38 (95% CI, 8.91-9.88) for <1 years-old and 5.91 (95% CI, 5.76-6.06) for 1-5 years-old versus 15-18 years-old patients. NH Black patients and those seen in urgent care or the emergency department were less likely to receive cefdinir.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite a small decline in use since 2020, cefdinir use remains substantial, especially among young children with UTI. Continued efforts to reduce inappropriate use and promote antibiotic stewardship are warranted.

articles.title: Trauma in Pregnancy.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma is the leading cause of death in reproductive-aged individuals, complicating 6% to 8% of pregnancies and accounting for approximately 20% of maternal deaths. This article reviews a maternal-first resuscitation approach, emphasizing that fetal survival hinges on maternal stabilization. It details pregnancy-specific alterations affecting the primary survey including difficult airway, respiratory compensation, aortocaval compression, and delayed recognition of hemorrhagic shock. It also provides guidance on blood product resuscitation, RhD considerations, TXA, and resuscitative hysterotomy. Diagnostic evaluation covers imaging recommendations and laboratory nuances. Finally, it addresses mechanism-specific injuries, intimate partner violence, fetal monitoring, patient counseling, and criteria for discharge.

articles.title: Metabolic risk factors on pediatric hidradenitis suppurativa: A retrospective multicenter cohort analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder that affects a clinically significant proportion of pediatric patients. Metabolic syndrome has been associated with HS in adults; however, its influence on disease characteristics and healthcare utilization in pediatric populations remains poorly understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the relationship between metabolic comorbidities and pediatric HS outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX collaborative network. Patients aged 0-18 years with an HS diagnosis were categorized into HS with metabolic components (HS+MetC) and HS alone (HS only). Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, and age at diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, treatment patterns, and healthcare utilization outcomes were compared.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 4,392 HS+MetC and 3,783 HS only patients were identified prior to matching. HS+MetC patients were diagnosed at a younger age and were more likely to be Black/African American or Hispanic/Latino. After matching, HS+MetC patients demonstrated significantly higher rates of emergency department visits, ambulatory visits, hospitalizations, surgical interventions, and most therapeutic treatments.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pediatric HS patients with metabolic comorbidities experience higher healthcare utilization and more intensive treatment needs. Early identification of metabolic risk factors may support earlier diagnosis, improved disease management, and reduce morbidity.

articles.title: Concussion in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Traumatic brain injuries (TBIs) account for a significant number of emergency department (ED) visits each year. Concussions, a type of mild TBI, represent the majority of these cases; however, there is no clear consensus on ED-based management. Concussion is a clinical diagnosis made through careful history and focused physical examination as there are no definitive pathognomonic signs. Management in the ED is primarily supportive, but patients require education and counseling to better understand their diagnosis, expected trajectory, follow-up plans, and need for aftercare. Improving ED-based concussion diagnosis and follow-up has strong potential to positively influence patient recovery and outcomes.

articles.title: Oral health behaviours and shift work barriers among Hungarian EMS personnel: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shift-working emergency medical services (EMS) personnel face structural barriers to preventive oral care, yet national workforce data remain scarce.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To estimate prevalence of oral symptoms, behaviours, dental attendance, and psychosocial OHRQoL impacts among Hungarian National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) staff; assess associations with occupational enablers/barriers; and evaluate acceptability of employer-supported screening.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Nationwide cross-sectional anonymous online survey (13 Sep 2024-17 Apr 2025; n = 1,061; 73% men, 74% 24-hour shifts). Logistic regression examined a priori outcomes (ORs, 95% CI), adjusted for age/sex/attendance; STROBE-compliant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,061 respondents, 74% reported 24-hour shifts as their primary duty pattern. Over half reported current or recent dental/oral problems (54.9%), and 20% had not attended a dental check-up within the previous two years. Off duty, 33% brushed twice daily, whereas during duty about two-thirds reported regular brushing. Workplace hygiene kits were reported by 40% of respondents and were more common among 24-hour shift workers. In regression analyses, kit availability was strongly associated with daily or more frequent on-duty brushing among 24-hour staff (85% vs. 21%). Daily brushing was associated with lower odds of toothache, non-use of interdental cleaning with higher odds of hiding teeth, and rare on-duty brushing with higher odds of halitosis. Psychosocial impacts were similar across roles, and 88-90% were willing to undergo workplace screening.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Shift-constrained EMS staff face substantial, preventable oral health burdens amenable to occupational solutions. Enabling on-duty hygiene and supporting routine care are key priorities. High screening readiness supports integrating teledentistry. Consistent gaps across roles underscore the need for further longitudinal and interventional studies.

articles.title: Bone Marrow Biopsies.
articles.journal_full: The Medical clinics of North America

abstract.text: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy are foundational diagnostic procedures in hematology, supporting evaluation of peripheral blood abnormalities, malignancy, infection, infiltrative disease, and rare systemic disorders. This article reviews contemporary indications and contraindications, with emphasis on safe patient selection and individualized management of bleeding risk. Key anatomic landmarks are summarized, highlighting the posterior superior iliac spine as the preferred adult site and describing point-of-care ultrasound to improve localization. Step-by-step techniques for powered and manual approaches are outlined, along with best practices for specimen handling, post-procedure monitoring, billing considerations, and common technical pitfalls, affecting diagnostic yield.

articles.title: Pain Management in the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Effective pain management in adult trauma patients is essential to improve recovery, reduce complications, and prevent long-term consequences such as chronic pain, depression, and PTSD. Multimodal analgesia combines medications and nonpharmacologic strategies to achieve better pain control while minimizing opioid use and associated risks. Key agents include acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents, ketamine, topical and systemic lidocaine, gabapentinoids, muscle relaxants, and carefully selected opioids when necessary. Pain management should be individualized based on patient factors, including age, comorbidities, traumatic brain injury, and substance use disorders. Early assessment, regular reassessment, and coordinated multidisciplinary care optimize outcomes across trauma settings.

articles.title: High-Value Emergency Department Interventions for the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal_full: Emergency medicine clinics of North America

abstract.text: Trauma remains a major cause of death and disability, making early emergency department interventions crucial. This review highlights evidence supporting high-value trauma interventions, particularly in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and damage control resuscitation (DCR). For TBI, preventing secondary brain injury through avoidance of hypoxia, hypotension, and abnormal carbon dioxide levels is essential, although evidence is largely observational. Recommended targets include SpO2 greater than 92%, Pao2 80 to 100 mm Hg, normocapnia, and age-appropriate blood pressure goals. In hemorrhagic trauma, DCR strategies such as tranexamic acid administration, tourniquet use, balanced transfusion, permissive hypotension, temperature control, calcium replacement, and anticoagulation reversal improve outcomes.

articles.title: Nutrition assistance program participation, healthcare access, and perinatal health among U.S. Latinos in the context of the "public charge" rule: a systematic review.
articles.journal_full: International journal for equity in health

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The "public charge" rule assesses whether an immigrant to the U.S. is likely to become dependent on government assistance, particularly for potential use of cash-benefit programs or long-term institutionalization at government expense. Being deemed a public charge can make an applicant for legal status inadmissible. Although the rule applies to specific immigration determinations, its effects may impact health outcomes. This systematic review synthesized evidence on public charge policy and health-related outcomes among U.S. Latino populations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following PRISMA guidelines and a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD42024507861), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published in English or Spanish from January 1996 through February 20, 2026. Eligible studies included U.S.-based Latino populations, examined the public charge rule as exposure, and reported health-related outcomes, health behaviors, healthcare access, or use of health or social programs. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, with disagreements resolved by consensus and, when needed, a third reviewer. Data were extracted using a standardized PECO-based form and narratively synthesized.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 157 citations identified, 19 studies met inclusion criteria. Studies examined program utilization and access (n = 13, 68%), maternal health (n = 4, 21%), or both domains (n = 2, 10%). Nearly all used cross-sectional designs (n = 18, 95%); 9 used qualitative and 10 quantitative data. Across studies, fear, misinformation, and concerns about immigration and legal consequences were the most consistent barriers to nutrition assistance programs, healthcare, Medicaid, and government-funded perinatal services. During the policy changes briefly implemented in 2018, Latino children with medical needs had the highest estimated risk of losing Medicaid, CHIP, or nutrition assistance benefits (79.8%; 95% CI, 74.4%-85.1%). Among likely undocumented Latino patients, self-pay emergency department visits increased after the 2018 proposed rule expansion. Maternal health studies documented delayed perinatal care, reduced Medicaid-funded prenatal care initiation, higher odds of preterm birth, and lower birth weights.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The public charge policy may function as a structural determinant of health for Latino families by discouraging the use of safety-net programs, including among eligible individuals. Additional research is needed to assess downstream health consequences, reduce misinformation, strengthen trusted communication, and protect access to healthcare and social welfare programs.

articles.title: Predicting operational risks in an O2O home nursing platform in China: machine learning models with SHAP-based explanations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The rapid expansion of Online-to-Offline (O2O) home nursing services addresses the growing continuity of care demands of aging populations but introduces complex operational risks due to spatial dispersion and dynamic community environments. Traditional retrospective management approaches are inadequate for addressing these highly non-linear spatiotemporal uncertainties, highlighting an urgent need for proactive risk stratification.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To develop, compare, and interpret predictive models utilizing traditional machine learning and Tabular Transformer architectures for stratifying two core operational risks (service overtime and long service duration) and one fee-structure classification task (high-cost orders) in digital nursing delivery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study analyzed 89,623 continuous operational records from the "Yujian Nursing at Home" platform in 2025. The dataset was strictly partitioned into training, validation, and independent test sets. We compared the predictive performance of six traditional baseline classifiers against deep learning architectures, specifically comparing a simplified Minimal Transformer and a standard TabTransformer. Model efficacy was evaluated using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), Sensitivity, F1-score, and Precision-Recall curves. TreeSHAP for the Random Forest models and KernelSHAP for the TabTransformer were applied to extract global feature importance and interpret the decision-making mechanisms.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the full operational monitoring scenario, the Tabular Transformer achieved an AUC of 0.934 for high-cost order risks, while Random Forest achieved AUCs of 0.789 and 0.794 for long service duration and overtime risks, respectively. However, under the strict pre-dispatch setting (using only features available at order submission), predictive performance experienced an expected decrease: AUCs were 0.856 for high-cost risks (TabTransformer), 0.726 for long duration, and 0.744 for overtime (Random Forest). Identifying minority class cases in the highly imbalanced overtime task (9.78% positive rate) remained challenging under fixed thresholds, resulting in a low positive predictive value (PPV). SHAP analysis revealed that geospatial impedance and specialized service items were the features with the largest model-attributed contributions across all tasks.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Advanced machine learning algorithms can stratify multidimensional operational risks in O2O home nursing platforms. By quantifying the impact of geospatial impedance and clinical complexity, these interpretable models facilitate a critical paradigm shift from retrospective quality control to proactive, algorithm-driven nursing governance, potentially generating hypotheses for optimizing human resource allocation, exploring interventions to mitigate occupational burnout, and informing equitable digital health policies.

articles.title: Joint modeling of hypertension and cardiovascular disease among Iranian Hajj pilgrims using Bayesian multivariate generalized linear mixed model.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hypertension (HTN) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) are major contributors to global morbidity and mortality and represent important health concerns during the Hajj pilgrimage, where large numbers of pilgrims are exposed to substantial environmental and physical stress. Despite their close biological relationship and frequent co-occurrence, HTN and CVD have largely been investigated as independent outcomes, potentially overlooking their shared determinants and underlying correlation. Therefore, we jointly modeled these conditions to provide a more comprehensive assessment of cardiovascular risk among Iranian Hajj pilgrims.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, medical records of 478,360 Iranian Hajj pilgrims participating in seven pilgrimage seasons (2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2022) were analyzed. A Bayesian multivariate generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was employed to jointly analyze HTN and CVD, allowing the correlation between these outcomes to be modeled while accounting for geographic clustering among individuals through province-level random intercepts. Associations with demographic and clinical risk factors were estimated using adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% credible intervals (CrIs), and model performance was evaluated using the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC). Spatial analyses were performed to characterize regional variation in disease burden.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The prevalence of HTN and CVD was 20.90% and 3.93%, respectively. Among all included pilgrims, the mean age was 54.87 ± 10.92 years, and 49.96% were women. Compared with separate univariate models, the joint Bayesian GLMM demonstrated substantially better model fit (ΔDIC = 51,720.5) and identified a strong residual correlation between HTN and CVD (ρ = 0.75). Age, sex, chronic renal failure, thyroid dysfunction, and diabetes (DM) were significantly associated with both outcomes. Representative estimates from the joint model showed that each additional year of age increased the odds of HTN (OR = 1.14, 95% CrI: 1.13-1.15) and CVD (OR = 1.11, 95% CrI: 1.10-1.11). Women had higher odds of HTN (OR = 2.15, 95% CrI: 1.99-2.32) but lower odds of CVD (OR = 0.80, 95% CrI: 0.76-0.84) compared with men, whereas DM was associated with substantially increased odds of HTN (OR = 9.15, 95% CrI: 7.57-10.95) and CVD (OR = 3.07, 95% CrI: 2.90-3.27). Temporal variation was observed across pilgrimage years, with HTN risk highest in 2018 and lower in 2022 relative to 2013, while CVD risk was also reduced in 2022. Geographic heterogeneity was evident, with HTN prevalence ranging from 13.52% in Qom to 32.39% in East Azerbaijan and CVD prevalence ranging from 1.87% in Esfahan to 8.93% in Ilam.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The Bayesian multivariate GLMM provided an informative framework for jointly evaluating correlated HTN and CVD outcomes in a large clustered population. By accounting for the correlation between outcomes and identifying shared determinants, this approach can inform integrated cardiovascular risk assessment, targeted pre-Hajj screening, and region-specific preventive strategies for high-risk pilgrims.

articles.title: A scoping review on the economic burden of falls among older adults.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Falls are the second leading cause of unintentional injury death globally, and the World Health Organization estimates that approximately 82% of fall-related mortality occurs in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite this disproportionate burden, the economic impact of falls among older adults in resource-limited settings remains poorly documented. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on the economic burden of falls among older adults, describe the extent and nature of available cost data, and identify evidence gaps, with particular attention to LMICs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The protocol was registered with the Open Science Framework ( https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/N23H5 ). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Semantic Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2010 and January 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data, and findings were summarised using narrative synthesis. Eligible studies reported quantitative monetary cost data associated with falls or fall-related injuries in populations aged 60 years and older.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 198 records identified (183 after de-duplication), 33 studies met the inclusion criteria, originating from 12 countries and one multi-country European study. Most studies (n = 30, 90.9%) were conducted in high-income countries (HICs); two (6.1%) were from upper-middle-income countries (Iran and Mexico) and one (3.0%) from a lower-middle-income country (India). No studies were identified from low-income countries, Sub-Saharan Africa, or most of Southeast Asia. In the United States, reported total medical costs of falls rose from US$50.0 billion (2015) to US$80.0 billion (2020). Reported per-episode costs ranged from US$5,974 (emergency department) to US$48,679 (inpatient admission). Hip fractures were consistently reported as the most costly injury type. Seven studies (21.2%) reported indirect costs, and a single study quantified informal caregiving costs (US$4,274 per faller per year). Fifteen studies (45.5%) included cost-effectiveness components, all conducted in HIC settings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This review maps a marked geographic mismatch: although LMICs are estimated to bear the majority of global fall-related mortality, only 9.1% of the economic evidence identified originated from these settings. The limited cost data from LMICs constrains evidence-based fall-prevention policy in the regions where the demographic transition is most rapid. Further investment in LMIC-specific economic research on falls among older adults would help inform resource allocation and policy in ageing low-resource settings.

articles.title: Endotracheal intubation practices, success rates and adverse events in four Dutch emergency departments: a multicentre retrospective study.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Endotracheal intubation in the emergency department (ED) is a high-risk intervention associated with significant complications. Contemporary European data on emergency airway management remain limited, and no published data are available from the Netherlands. This study aimed to describe endotracheal intubation practices, success rates, and adverse events in four Dutch EDs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing endotracheal intubation in four teaching hospital EDs in the Netherlands between January 2019 and December 2023. Patients were identified using procedure registrations, diagnostic codes, billing information and disposition records. Trained abstractors collected standardized data on patient characteristics, indications, provider characteristics, intubation techniques, medications, first-pass success and adverse events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1250 intubations were included. The most common indication was post-return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after cardiac arrest (47%), followed by neurologic pathology (14%), cardiac arrest (12%), respiratory insufficiency (8%), intoxication (8%), and trauma (5%). Emergency medicine and intensive care physicians performed most intubations. Videolaryngoscopy was the primary technique in 89.5% of cases, and etomidate was the most frequently used induction agent (73.5%). The overall first-pass success rate was 93.8% and did not differ by provider specialty or level of training. Adverse events occurred in 181 patients (14.5%), with hypotension (6.5%) and desaturation (4.7%) being most common. Increasing age (OR 1.07 per year, 95% CI 1.04-1.10) and cardiac pathology as indication for intubation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 1.03-11.88) were associated with hypotension. A higher body mass index (OR 1.08 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.13), younger age (OR 0.98 per year, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p = 0.022) and multiple intubations attempts (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.12-7.33) were associated with desaturation. Lower pre-intubation oxygen saturation was associated with peri-intubation cardiac arrest (OR 0.96 per point, 95% CI 0.92-0.99).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study provides the first multicentre description of emergency airway management in Dutch EDs and demonstrates a distinctive emergency intubation population, characterised by a high proportion of post-ROSC intubations. Contemporary practice was characterised by widespread adoption of videolaryngoscopy, frequent use of etomidate, and high first-pass success rates. Peri-intubation hypotension and desaturation remained common and represent important targets for quality improvement.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: clinicaltrials.gov NCT06374030.

articles.title: Associations of ambient temperature and PM2.5 concentration with temporal variability in emergency department visits for acute gastrointestinal illnesses in central Bangkok, Thailand: a 5-year retrospective analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The combined effects of temperature and air pollution on acute gastrointestinal (GI) illnesses remain underexplored in tropical settings. This study examined the association between ambient temperature, fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and emergency department (ED) visits for gastritis and gastroenteritis in Bangkok, Thailand.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of ED visits from 2018 to 2023 at a large urban hospital in Bangkok, Thailand. The effects of heat index (HI) levels and daily PM2.5 were assessed using generalized additive and distributed lag non-linear models, with stratified analyses to explore interaction effects.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher HI and PM2.5 levels were associated with increased acute GI-related ED visits. PM2.5 concentrations exceeding 139.8 µg/m³ were associated with elevated risk compared with the mean daily level. Conversely, HI below 30 °C was linked with a lower cumulative risk. Stratified models suggested that extreme heat may exacerbate the adverse impact of elevated PM2.5.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In the urban setting of Thailand, very high PM2.5 (> 139.8 µg/m³) may be associated with increased patients presenting to the ED with acute GI illnesses. The risk of increased patient counts appeared to be higher with greater PM exposure, particularly when elevated PM levels coincided with a high heat index, whereas cooler conditions appeared protective. These findings highlight the need for further investigation of interactive environmental exposures to inform public health and adapt the ED management strategies.

articles.title: Discrimination of the National Early Warning Score versus the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard for in-hospital mortality in emergency department patients with confirmed high-risk cardiovascular and aortic emergencies: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is a physiological severity score, whereas the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard is a categorical triage system used to assign treatment priority. Both use information available at first emergency department (ED) assessment, but their relative ability to discriminate mortality risk in high-risk cardiovascular and aortic emergencies has not been directly compared. We compared their discrimination for all-cause in-hospital mortality and explored a possible adjunctive role for NEWS in routine triage.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults presenting to the ED of a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2023 with a confirmed high-risk acute cardiovascular or aortic emergency, including acute myocardial infarction, acute pulmonary embolism, acute aortic syndrome, or aortic aneurysm. A retrospectively reconstructed NEWS (supplemental-oxygen status was unavailable and scored 0 for all patients) was calculated from data recorded at first ED triage. Triage grade, assigned by the triage nurse according to the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard, was extracted as a recorded variable. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC) and compared using DeLong's test. Internal validation was performed by bootstrap resampling, and associations between vital signs and mortality were explored using restricted cubic splines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,168 included patients, in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (129/3,168). NEWS showed higher discrimination for in-hospital mortality than the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage grade (AUROC 0.750 [95% CI 0.706-0.794] vs. 0.584 [95% CI 0.538-0.629]; DeLong's test P < 0.001). At the Youden-optimal threshold of NEWS ≥ 3, sensitivity was 68.2% and specificity was 71.6%. Discrimination was similar when NEWS was recalculated without the respiratory-rate component (AUROC 0.758 [95% CI 0.715-0.800]), and bootstrap internal validation showed negligible optimism. Higher NEWS was associated with increased mortality, and several vital signs showed non-linear associations with mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this retrospective single-centre cohort of patients with confirmed high-risk acute cardiovascular and aortic emergencies, a retrospectively reconstructed, incomplete NEWS discriminated all-cause in-hospital mortality better than the 2018 Chinese Emergency Triage Standard. Whether NEWS adds prognostic value beyond triage grade requires prospective evaluation. Improved physiological data recording, prospective multicentre validation, and development and external validation of an appropriate NEWS-to-risk mapping are needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: The diagnostic value of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for sepsis: to provide early warning before clinical deterioration.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's abnormal immune response to infection.Current diagnostic criteria is affected by multiple clinical factors, resulting in a diagnostic delay.Objective To investigate the diagnostic value of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with sepsis, to provide a simple and practical laboratory index reference for the early diagnosis of sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 18,570 patients from the MIMIC database (2015-2020). After screening, 11 858 patients were included and classified into sepsis (n = 10 145) and control (n = 1713) groups based on Sepsi3.0. Biomarkers measured within 24 h when admitted in Intensive Care Unit(ICU) before diagnosed with sepsis which were analyzed using logistic regression. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.Restricted cubic spline (RCS) logistic regression model to explore the nonlinear association between MLR and the odds ratio (OR) of sepsis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: MLR and NLR in the sepsis group were significantly higher than those in the non-sepsis group (all P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified that MLR (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.40-1.74, p < 0.001) and NLR(OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, p < 0.001) was strongly and independently associated with sepsis. The ROC curves showed that the areas under the curve of PLR, NLR and MLR levels alone and in combination for predicting sepsis were 0.496, 0.545and 0.571, respectively. The RCS identified OR for sepsis remained consistently below 1.00 when MLR was less than 0.69. Beyond this threshold, the OR increased sharply above 1.00.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified MLR and NLR were strongly and independently associated with sepsis after confounders are adjusted( P < 0.001).the markedly imbalanced study population substantially may influence ROC performance, MLR and NLR have a weak diagnostic value for sepsis as independent laboratory markers.The Restricted cubic spline logistic regression model (RCS) showed MLR > 0.69 could serve as a potential warning threshold for identifying patients at elevated sepsis risk, as simple and easy-to-obtain inflammatory ratios reducing misdiagnosis and missed diagnoses.

articles.title: Factors influencing willingness to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation and use an automated external defibrillator: a convergent parallel mixed-methods study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study applied the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Intention-Focused Model for Bystander Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) Performance to examine the associations between attitude, perceived norms, self-efficacy and intention to perform CPR and use an automated external defibrillator (AED); the mediating role of intention and the moderating roles of knowledge, training, and barriers concerning behavioral willingness; and stakeholder perspectives regarding factors influencing willingness to perform CPR and use an AED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The present convergent parallel mixed-methods study collected quantitative and qualitative data concurrently, analyzed them independently, and integrated the data during interpretation to compare, contrast, and synthesize the findings. The quantitative strand was prioritized and involved 449 participants from a CPR program (2018-2020) who met the inclusion criteria. The quantitative data were collected using the Factors Influencing Community Willingness to Perform CPR and Use an AED (FIXED) questionnaire and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The qualitative strand involved 10 stakeholders (basic life support [BLS] instructors, healthcare staff, village community members, community leaders, nongovernmental organization [NGO] representatives) to explain and contextualize the quantitative results. The qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews and underwent deductive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Partial least squares-SEM demonstrated that self-efficacy was the strongest predictor of intention (effect size: large, β = 0.515, p < .001, f² = 0.353). Attitude was positively associated with intention despite its small effect (β = 0.206, p < .001, f² = 0.053). Perceived norms had a statistically significant but practically negligible association with intention (β = 0.094, p = .014, f² = 0.010). Intention significantly mediated the relationships between self-efficacy, attitude, perceived norms, and behavioral willingness, with self-efficacy having the strongest indirect effect. Knowledge, training, and barriers did not significantly moderate the intention and behavioral willingness relationship. Qualitative findings identified psychological factors, skill-related factors, and contextual constraints influenced behavioral willingness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Self-efficacy was the strongest factor associated with intention to perform CPR and use an AED, whereas attitude and perceived norms contributed to a lesser extent. The findings highlighted the importance of confidence-building strategies in CPR and AED education programs and supported theory-informed interventions to strengthen intention and behavioral willingness to respond to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Epidemiology, outcomes, and associated factors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Zhejiang, China: a province-wide registry study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge with poor survival worldwide. Although previous studies have described OHCA epidemiology and outcomes in China, province-wide data comprehensively characterizing patient and arrest characteristics, clinical outcomes, and factors associated with survival and neurological recovery remain limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize the epidemiology and outcomes of OHCA and identify factors associated with 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome in Zhejiang, China.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the Zhejiang Emergency Registry (ZER), a mandatory province-wide emergency medical services (EMS) registry based on Utstein-style standardized reporting in Zhejiang, China. Adult EMS-treated OHCA cases of medical etiology between January 2024 and December 2025 were included. Patient characteristics, arrest circumstances, community response, dispatcher-related factors, EMS characteristics, prehospital interventions, and clinical outcomes were described. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 17,646 EMS-treated OHCA patients, 531 (3.0%) survived to 30 days and 345 (2.0%) achieved favorable neurological outcome. Bystander CPR was performed in 47.7% of cases, while dispatcher recognition of OHCA, dispatcher-assisted CPR, and bystander automated external defibrillator (AED) use occurred in 25.1%, 20.0%, and 1.8% of cases, respectively. Home arrests accounted for 64.3% of cases and had a 30-day survival rate of 2.2%. Both 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome progressively declined with increasing EMS response time. In multivariable analysis, shockable rhythm showed the strongest association with both 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcome. Younger age, witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, bystander AED use, dispatcher recognition, dispatcher-assisted CPR, and shorter EMS response time were independently associated with improved 30-day survival.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this province-wide registry study, 30-day survival and favorable neurological outcomes after OHCA remained low in Zhejiang, China. Low rates of dispatcher recognition, dispatcher-assisted CPR, and bystander AED use were observed, and outcomes declined progressively with increasing EMS response time.
